docs.title: DomiNet
docs.text: Self-hosted home automation and video surveillance, rewritten in Rust: Zigbee2MQTT devices, IP cameras (ONVIF, WebRTC, recordings, motion and object detection), energy, automations, scenes, alerts, messaging, Android, observability (Prometheus, Grafana) and backups.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
I want to… Page Install in production (3 commands) Deployment Understand every environment variable Configuration Set up a development machine Development machine Monitor and alert Observability, Rules Back up and restore Backups Know why it is built this way Architecture decisions

This documentation is served by the application itself (/docs/), behind the login.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
Rules, evaluation, alerts page and sidebar badge (R4 lot 6). Decisions: ADR 0035, R4 plan (D8, D10, D12).

A rule watches a key of a device's state (temperature, state, power…); when its condition is true, an alert is created. It stays "firing" until the condition ends ("resolved") or an account acknowledges it.

docs.title: For every account
docs.text:
• /alerts (the "Alerts" link of the sidebar, with a badge of the number of firing alerts, updated live): the most recent alerts (200) filtered by status — firing (default), resolved, acknowledged, all. Each row gives the severity, the rule, the device, the triggering value, the date and the status (and who acknowledged, when). Acknowledge (one firing alert) and Acknowledge all buttons.
  • Every fired alert shows a banner in the interface of all signed-in accounts: [DomiNet] Heatwave — meteo_locale : 36.2 (level according to severity).

docs.title: Platform alerts (Prometheus and Grafana)
docs.text: The sidebar badge also counts the alerts currently firing in Prometheus and Grafana (application offline, 5xx errors, MQTT disconnected, heat wave…), read every minute and read-only: they have no "Acknowledge" button and disappear when their cause does. No new setting (PROMETHEUS_URL, GRAFANA_URL, GRAFANA_USER, GRAFANA_PASSWORD). ADR 0061. The /alerts page lists them in a Platform section (severity, source, name, summary, since when) above the device alerts, for the "Firing" and "All" filters. If Prometheus or Grafana does not answer, the page says so ("Prometheus cannot be reached") instead of showing "no alerts". With no address configured for either, the section does not appear.

docs.title: For administrators
docs.text: • /admin/alert-rules: device, state key, operator (>, ≥, <, ≤, =, ≠, contains), numeric (decimal comma accepted) or text threshold, severity (info, warning, critical), delay between two alerts (0 to 1,440 min), three channels (e-mail, SMS, Android), enabled. A change applies immediately. Deleting a rule keeps its alerts.

docs.title: How a rule is evaluated
docs.text:
• On every state of the device (Zigbee2MQTT or automatic device). Missing or null key: skipped, nothing fired or resolved.
  • Condition: numbers (numeric text and booleans included: "40" or true are read as numbers); if the value or the threshold is not a number, = and ≠ compare texts ignoring case and spaces and other operators are false; "contains" searches the text threshold in the value's text, ignoring case.
  • True: an alert is created, unless a firing alert of the rule is younger than the delay. False: the rule's firing alerts are resolved.
  • Quirks kept on purpose: an acknowledged alert no longer counts in the delay (the next hot state creates one right away); a condition that stays true recreates an alert each time the delay expires; a delay of 0 creates an alert on every true state.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
Each fired alert first shows a banner in the interface, then a background task serves the rule's channels (R5 lot 6, ADR 0042):

Channel What goes out Email to the alert recipient (EMAIL_RECIPIENT, else the sender), subject [DomiNet Alerte <severity>] <rule>, long text (rule, device, value, date) SMS Free Mobile SMS, short text (160 characters at most); skipped without SMS_FREE_USER / SMS_FREE_KEY Android alert_notification pushed to all online Android devices. The current app ignores this message ("Message ignored"): it is sent for a future version

Each channel is tried even if another fails (failures go to the server log, never the secret); an unconfigured channel is simply skipped. The alert becomes notified after the attempt, failures or not and is not sent again: the rule's repeat delay decides the next attempt. Channels and their settings: notifications. Tests and the demonstration never send anything "for real".

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• dominet_automation::alerts: AlertEngine, AlertHandle, Notifier, AlertNotice; wired in dominet_server::mqtt::spawn (AlertNotifier in dominet_server::alerts). Domain: AlertRuleDraft::evaluate, alert_messages.
  • Real-time topic alerts (WsServerMsg::AlertCount): last state retained; published at startup and on every change.
  • Server functions: alerts/{page,acknowledge,acknowledge-all} (any signed-in account), alert-rules/{list,save,delete} (administrators).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: cargo test -p dominet-domain --test alerts_oracle (2,030 evaluations compared with frozen reference values), -p dominet-automation --test alerts (8 scenarios of the alerting.py cycle compared with frozen reference values after every step, texts, restart, disabled rules), -p dominet --test ui alert (permissions, field-by-field validation, page, badge), -p dominet-server --test alerts (the production heatwave rule end to end on the dev broker); E2E alerts.

docs.title: Android relay (server side)
docs.text: R5 lot 3, ADR 0039 (model: ADR 0037). The Android app is not modified: the Rust server speaks exactly its protocol.

docs.title: What the app does
docs.text:
It connects to wss://<server>/ws/android/device/<token>/ (the device token, shown only once when created or regenerated) and reconnects by itself after 5 s.

Direction Frame Effect app → server sms_received {from, body, contact_name, timestamp} SMS stored (unread), shown live app → server call_event {state, number, contact_name, timestamp, duration} call log (ringing / outgoing create, ended / missed close, answered changes nothing) app → server sms_sent_ack {message_id, success, error} the requested SMS is "sent" or "failed" server → app auth_ok {device_name} connection accepted; the device is "online" server → app send_sms {to, body, message_id} sends an SMS; the app answers with sms_sent_ack carrying the same message_id server → app pong, alert_notification {…} (the current app ignores the latter)

Unknown token: close with code 4001.

docs.title: Presence and heartbeat
docs.text: The server sends a control frame every 30 s; with nothing received for 90 s it closes (code 4408). A new connection from the same device replaces the old one (4009). At startup every device goes "offline".

docs.title: SMS to send
docs.text: AndroidRelay::send_sms queues the SMS (sms_outbox) and sends it to the device; the ack settles it. Without an ack after 60 s the SMS fails ("no ack from the device"). An ack from another device, for an unknown id, or late, has no effect.

docs.title: For browsers
docs.text: Topic android:<id> of the notifications WebSocket (owner or administrator): device_status, sms_received, call_event, sms_sent_ack. The current presence arrives on subscription.

docs.title: The pages (lot 4, ADR 0040)
docs.text:
Page Content /android devices (live presence), last 10 SMS and calls, unread SMS count /android/devices add a device (name, number), new token, delete (with confirmation); the token is only shown at creation or regeneration /android/sms?device=N the last 100 SMS (received ones are marked read when displayed), send an SMS; each outgoing SMS shows its state: waiting, sent, failed and why /android/calls?device=N the last 100 calls (incoming, outgoing, missed, duration mm:ss, "ongoing")

Each account sees its devices, an administrator sees all devices. Everything updates live (received SMS, calls, acks, presence). Address to enter in the app: ws://server-address/ws/android/device/TOKEN/ (wss:// behind HTTPS).

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The token is only stored hashed (SHA-256) and appears in no log (the path is masked).
  • Frames limited to 64 KiB; fields clipped to the database bounds; invalid JSON ignored without closing the line.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: cargo test -p dominet --test android_ws (15: token, presence, replacement, heartbeat, SMS, calls, acks, messaging, timeout, alerts, subscription rights), --test android_oracle (21 sessions replayed against frozen reference exchanges), -p dominet-domain --test android_fixtures (frames from the Kotlin code), --test ui android (rights, token, sending), E2E android (simulated phone tools/sim_android.py).

docs.title: Appearance: customise colours, font and widths
docs.text: What can be set without touching the code (menu, dashboards, widgets) is done in the administration: see Devices and the interface. This page describes the style: colours, font, rounded corners and menu width.

docs.title: The custom.css file
docs.text:
After its main style sheet, DomiNet loads deploy/custom/custom.css if it exists (CUSTOM_CSS variable, ./custom:/custom:ro mount of the production compose). It is read again on every page load: a change shows when you reload the browser, with no restart and no image rebuild. It is ignored by git: it is a machine setting.

cd ~/opt/dominet/deploy/custom
cp custom.css.example custom.css
$EDITOR custom.css            # uncomment and edit the variables you want

Reload the page (Ctrl+Shift+R if the browser keeps the old version). Back to the original look: delete custom.css. A missing, unreadable or over-256 KiB file gives an empty sheet: never an error.

docs.title: The variables
docs.text:
They go in a :root { … } block.

Variable Role Default --bg-base page background #0d1117 --bg-surface menu and card background #1c2128 --bg-elevated, --bg-hover raised elements, hover #2d333b, #373e47 --accent, --accent-dim, --accent-glow main colour, its dark variant, its glow #00d4aa, #00a884, translucent green --danger, --warning, --info, --success state colours (error, warning, information, success) #f85149, #e3b341, #58a6ff, #56d364 --text-primary, --text-secondary, --text-muted text levels #f0f6fc, #b1bac4, #768390 --border lines and borders #30363d --radius-sm, --radius-md, --radius-lg rounded corners 6px, 10px, 16px --sidebar-w left menu width 220px --font font 'Segoe UI', system-ui, …

Example (orange theme, wider menu):

:root {
    --accent: #ff9f1a;
    --accent-dim: #d98200;
    --sidebar-w: 260px;
}

Beyond the variables you can write any CSS rule (for example .vc-table td { font-size: .85rem; }); the classes are those of crates/dominet-web/style/main.css.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The theme stays dark: there is no light variant. A light background also means changing the text and line colours.
  • The sheet is served by DomiNet at /custom.css, public (the login page is styled too). It must contain no secret.
  • The file must be in deploy/custom/ (mounted read-only). A change made elsewhere is not seen.
  • Development: without the CUSTOM_CSS variable, /custom.css answers an empty sheet.

docs.title: Local assistant (R12)
docs.text:
The assistant answers in French, inside the interface, to requests such as "Which shutters are still open?" or "Close them". It runs at your place: the model is a self-hosted llama-server, no remote API, no data leaves your network. Roadmap: ROADMAP-agent.md; decision and measurements: ADR 0060; evaluation: 50 requests.

Administrators only, off by default

The Administration › Assistant page (/admin/assistant) is reserved for the administrator role; it only answers when AGENT_ENABLED is true.

docs.title: What it does, and what it never does alone
docs.text:
• Read: device state, history, logs, alerts, configuration (never a secret).
  • Act: the model proposes an action, shown as a card ("Close the living-room shutter"); you click Confirm or Cancel. Nothing runs without your click.
  • Configure (the "configuration" request type): for an automation, the card also shows a before / after YAML diff.
  • Undo: every confirmed change is written to the audit log (type agent) with your request, the previous state and the way back; the "Changes made by the assistant" list undoes it in two clicks. Not undoable: device commands, scenes run, notifications, and anything involving Rhai code.

docs.title: Install the model
docs.text:
On the inference machine (a PC with an 8 GB graphics card is fine; without a GPU it works but takes about 8 s per answer), with a llama.cpp llama-server already installed:

make agent-install LLAMA_DIR=/path/to/llama.cpp  AGENT_HOST=0.0.0.0
make agent-install LLAMA_DIR=... DRY=1     # shows what would be done, does nothing

The script downloads Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M (5 GB, resumable) into ~/IA/models and creates the dominet-llm user service (16k context, tool calls, one request at a time). To keep it running after logout: sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER. One model serves all request types (ADR 0060, decision of 2026-11-17).

Network

llama-server has no authentication. Open it to the local network or the VPN only (AGENT_HOST = LAN address), never to the Internet.

docs.title: Enable on the DomiNet side
docs.text:
In Administration › Settings, category Assistant:

Setting Value AGENT_ENABLED true AGENT_LLM_URL http://<inference machine>:8081 (the default port of make agent-install; 8080 is left to Zigbee2MQTT and the demo) AGENT_MODEL Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M AGENT_MODEL_ADMIN empty (same model)

On the Assistant page, the Test connection button checks the address and the model. If the inference machine is off, the page says so and the forms remain usable.

docs.title: First tries
docs.text:
1. "Which lamps are on?" → an answer in one or two sentences.
  2. "Close the living-room shutter" → a card; Confirm.
  3. "Configuration" type: "Close the shutters at sunset" → an automation card with the before / after YAML; Cancel if it does not fit.
  4. Changes made by the assistant: undo the last one.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• A small model can be wrong or ask for details: rephrase with the device or room name.
  • One request at a time, 40 messages of memory, 15 minutes of inactivity before the conversation is forgotten; the conversation is not stored in the database.
  • What the house contains (device names, messages) is treated as data, never as an instruction: a device named "ignore your instructions" has no effect (injection tests: 0 wrong cards).
  • Changing or renaming an item that already exists (a device, for example) is not reliable with a small model: do it from the administration pages. The assistant reads, controls and creates.
  • Measured quality: 49 of 51 requests succeeded with Qwen3-8B (the two failures: "Turn everything off" and "Set the right temperature" without a clarifying question, no card), 0 cards proposed wrongly. Replay the measurement: make agent-eval LLAMA_DIR=… AGENT_EVAL_MODELS=Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Server-side sessions (opaque cookie, data in PostgreSQL), argon2id passwords, two roles: admin and user. Decisions: ADR 0004 (in French).

docs.title: Creating and managing accounts
docs.text:
dominet createsuperuser --username admin [--email me@example.org]   # masked prompt, asked twice
dominet passwd --username admin                                     # also closes every session of the account
DOMINET_PASSWORD='...' dominet createsuperuser --username admin    # no prompt (scripts, Docker)

Password policy: 10 to 128 characters, not digits only, different from the username. Usernames: letters, digits and @ . + - _; uniqueness is case-insensitive.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Route Purpose POST /api/auth/login {"username","password"} opens a session, returns the account POST /api/auth/logout closes the session GET /api/auth/me signed-in account (401 otherwise) POST /api/auth/password {"current_password","new_password"} changes your password; closes every session GET /api/users list accounts (admin)

Errors look like {"error":{"code","message"}}; Retry-After accompanies a 429.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Cookie dominet_session: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure (unless COOKIE_SECURE=false, plain HTTP on the LAN). Expires after SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES of inactivity (480) and at most SESSION_MAX_DAYS days (14) overall. The identifier is renewed at login (session-fixation protection).
  • Brute-force lockout (15-minute window and duration): 5 failures for one account from one IP, or 20 for an account from anywhere, or 30 from one IP. While locked, the password is not even checked (even if correct). A successful login resets the account counters. Attempts are kept for 7 days.
  • No account enumeration: unknown name, wrong password, disabled account and lockout look alike; a dummy computation of the same cost evens out response times.
  • CSRF: any POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE must come from the site's origin (Origin or Referer compared to Host) or from an origin listed in CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS; Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site is refused. Non-browser clients (curl, the Android app) are not affected.
  • Client IP behind nginx: X-Forwarded-For is only trusted when the peer is in TRUSTED_PROXIES.
  • Headers: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS over TLS, Cache-Control: no-store on /api. The Content-Security-Policy arrives with the Leptos front end (lots 7-8).
  • Passwords are never logged nor printed (Debug of requests and configuration is masked).

docs.title: Automations
docs.text:
Engine and administration of automations (R4 lot 3). Decisions: ADR 0031 (schema, domain), ADR 0032 (engine), R4 plan (D1 to D3).

An automation has a trigger, an optional condition and an action. Administrators create, edit, enable / disable and delete them in /admin/automations.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
Type Fires when Status device_state a state message of the device contains the key with the given value (28 = "28") active mqtt_message a message arrives on a topic matching the filter (+, #) and its content contains the message filter (JSON object, value equality) active schedule the five-field cron expression (local time, TZ setting) active (scheduler) solar one of the nine solar events at the given place (latitude, longitude; decimal comma accepted) active (scheduler)
  • Condition (optional): if the message contains the key it must equal the value; otherwise the condition is true. Values are typed as JSON (100, true, "ON") or plain text (ON).
  • A device_state fires on every matching state message: a repeating "ON" state fires again. Remote-control keys (action: 1_single) are events.
  • An mqtt_message waits for neither bridge/… messages nor …/set / …/get commands. The MQTT client subscribes by itself to the topic of every active mqtt_message automation: no source to create.
  • A state coalesced by ingestion (two states of the same device within the same second) stays visible to automations: a remote sending action: 1_single then action: "" does not lose its key press.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Type Effect mqtt_publish publishes the JSON object on the topic (QoS 1, not retained) scene activates the scene (commands go out in order, see scenes.md); the scene must exist when saving notification log + banner in the interface of all signed-in accounts + email to the alert recipient, and Free Mobile SMS if the "SMS" box is ticked (default message "Automation triggered"; R5 lot 6, ADR 0042) script Rhai script run in a sandbox, see scripts.md; its effects (publish, scene, history) are applied afterwards, only if it finishes without error

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text: schedule and solar automations are run by the scheduler role (ADR 0033), present by default in dominet serve. Each has a job in schedule_job; the Next run column of /admin/automations shows it, in the server's local time (TZ, Europe/Paris by default), like every date in the interface; the REST API stays in UTC. Editing, disabling or deleting the automation updates the job immediately. - No catch-up: a missed run (server stopped) is not replayed, unless it is discovered less than 60 s after its time. - Cron: five fields, Sunday = 0, day of month and day of week; local time with daylight-saving changes (nonexistent hour: shifted by one hour; repeated hour: once). - Sun: sunrise, sunset, solar noon, civil / nautical / astronomical dawns and dusks, computed without a library (within 13 s of ephem on our 1,036 cases). Beyond the polar circles, with no rise or set, the automation waits for the day they return. - The system job compute_daily_energy (00:05 local) already exists; its calculation comes with lot 7.

docs.title: Guard and log
docs.text:
• At most 30 firings per automation per minute (anti-loop); beyond that they are ignored and the overrun is logged once per minute (limited).
  • The log (below the table of /admin/automations, last 50 rows) gives the cause, the result (ok, failed, no effect, limited) and detail; the table shows the number of firings and the last one. A false filter or condition writes nothing. Retention: 30 days.
  • A change is applied immediately (engine and subscriptions are reloaded), no restart.

docs.title: Notable behaviors
docs.text:
• device_state works; mqtt_publish really publishes; mqtt_message sees all useful messages. schedule and solar need neither Redis nor an external scheduler.
  • Anti-loop protection and an execution log.
  • At cut-over, the five "inert" production automations will become active: three for the remote control (Tele-commande will really command Volet-salon) and two Volet-SB-est plugins (rewritten in Rhai, see scripts.md).

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• dominet_automation::engine: Engine, EngineHandle, Executor, fires_on (pure), topic_matches_py. The server wires the engine in dominet_server::mqtt::spawn (ServerExecutor in dominet_server::automation).
  • Domain: loose_equal, payload_filter_holds, device_state_holds, value_from_text (dominet_domain::automation).
  • Server functions: automations/{list,save,delete,runs} (administrators).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: cargo test -p dominet-domain --lib automation (equalities, filters, meaning of device_state), -p dominet-automation --test matching (396 cases compared with frozen reference values), --test engine (triggers, condition, actions, log, guard, queue, production automations), --test hooks (announced messages, coalesced states), -p dominet-automation --test schedule and -p dominet-domain --test schedule_oracle (cron and sun compared with frozen reference values), --test scheduler (synchronisation, on-time runs, no catch-up, failures, the two production solar automations), -p dominet-server --test automations (end to end on the dev broker: the production remote control moves the shutter, the production sunset / sunrise activates its scenes, topic without source, scene, hot disable), -p dominet --test ui automation (permissions, field-by-field validation); E2E automations.

docs.title: What is backed up
docs.text:
Source File Content PostgreSQL <BACKUP_DIR>/postgres/dominet_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.sql.gz everything: accounts, settings, devices and their history, scenes, automations, cameras, indexed recordings, alert rules… ReductStore <BACKUP_DIR>/reductstore/reductstore_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.tar.gz data volume: archived video segments, snapshots and detections if any, raw IoT

Each file has its SHA-256 checksum (….sha256, checkable with sha256sum -c). Keep the DOMINET_MASTER_KEY separately — without it, camera passwords and SMS keys of a restored database are unreadable. Not backed up: segments still on disk before archiving, local snapshots, annotated images, generated Grafana dashboards, Prometheus and Grafana volumes (recomputable or short-lived data).

docs.title: Automatic backup
docs.text: Every day at BACKUP_HOUR (3 am, local time), if BACKUP_DIR is set (scheduler role). Backups older than BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS days (7) are deleted afterwards; the newest of each kind always stays. A failure is logged ("sauvegarde echouee"), counted (dominet_backup_runs_total{result="error"}) and triggers the BackupFailing alert; BackupTooOld warns when no backup has succeeded for 36 h.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
dominet backup      # immediate backup (database + ReductStore), prune expired ones
dominet backups     # list

In the deployment: make prod-backup (lot 6).

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
1. The database (it replaces the current data; a single transaction: all or nothing):

dominet restore --latest postgres --yes             # the newest
dominet restore /backups/postgres/dominet_20261109_030000.sql.gz --yes

The checksum is verified first. Without the tool: gunzip -c dominet_….sql.gz | psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction (if the server is PostgreSQL 16 and the dump was made by a 17 client, remove the SET transaction_timeout line: | grep -v '^SET transaction_timeout').

2. ReductStore (ReductStore stopped, its data folder empty):

dominet restore --latest reductstore --to /path/to/reductstore/volume
# then start ReductStore on that folder

A non-empty folder is refused (--force to override).

3. Restart DomiNet with the original DOMINET_MASTER_KEY.

docs.title: Checking the procedure
docs.text: tools/check-backup.sh (after make dev-up and make image) replays everything with the Docker image: a throwaway database backed up then restored into another one and compared table by table; real ReductStore records backed up, restored into another folder and read back byte for byte by a second ReductStore; a damaged file refused. ADR 0054.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
dominet is configured through environment variables only (names reused from DomiNet's .env.example.prod where they make sense). All errors are reported together at startup (exit code 2). Secrets are never printed or logged.

Variable Default Purpose DATABASE_URL — (required) postgres://user:password@host:5432/db HTTP_ADDR 0.0.0.0:8000 HTTP listen address BACKUP_DIR — backup folder (postgres/, reductstore/); absent: scheduled backup disabled BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS, BACKUP_HOUR 7, 3 maximum age of backups (the newest always stays); local hour of the daily backup REDUCTSTORE_BACKUP_SRC — ReductStore data folder, mounted read-only, to archive; absent: only the database is backed up PG_DUMP_BIN, PSQL_BIN pg_dump, psql PostgreSQL clients PROMETHEUS_RULES_PATH — rules.yml file that Prometheus reads (rules edited in /admin/prometheus-rules); absent: not written PROMETHEUS_ALERTS_POLL_SECS, PROMETHEUS_ALERT_COOLDOWN 60, 3600 polling of /api/v1/alerts (scheduler role, active when PROMETHEUS_URL is set) and the silence of an alert already notified (seconds) PROMETHEUS_URL — e.g. http://prometheus:9090: POST /-/reload after each write (Prometheus started with --web.enable-lifecycle) GRAFANA_ALERTING_PATH — rules.yaml file of Grafana's alerting provisioning (/admin/grafana-rules) GRAFANA_URL, GRAFANA_USER, GRAFANA_PASSWORD —, admin, — reload of Grafana's alerting provisioning (administrator account) METRICS_ADDR 0.0.0.0:9100 /metrics listener for Prometheus (never published on the host); off turns it off; a busy port does not stop the server SECRET_KEY — reserved, unused in R1 (CSRF protection relies on the Origin header, sessions are in the database); accepted so an existing .env keeps working, 32 characters minimum when provided DOMINET_MASTER_KEY — AES-256 key (32 bytes, base64) for encrypting secrets at rest (dominet gen-master-key); validated at startup; see Settings SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES 480 sign-out after this long without activity SESSION_MAX_DAYS 14 maximum lifetime of a session MCP_ENABLED false enables the MCP server on /mcp (R11); tokens are created in Administration › Assistants (MCP) MCP_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN 120 calls per minute and per token; beyond it, 429 MCP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS 365 how long the MCP audit trail is kept WS_HEARTBEAT_SECS 25 WebSocket heartbeat interval (1 to 300); the session is re-validated at every beat SYSTEM_STATS_SECS 5 machine resources measurement interval (1 to 3600 s): sidebar gauges, /api/system-stats/ TRUSTED_PROXIES — IPs or CIDR networks of the proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted (e.g. 172.18.0.1,10.0.0.0/8) ALLOWED_HOSTS — accepted hosts, comma separated CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS — trusted origins, comma separated COOKIE_SECURE true false for plain HTTP without TLS on the LAN SITE_ROOT target/site (/app/site in the image) folder of the interface files (WASM, JS, CSS) produced by cargo leptos build DOCS_ROOT target/docs-site (/app/docs in the image) documentation site (MkDocs), served on /docs/ behind the login CUSTOM_CSS — appearance customisation file, served at /custom.css and read again on every load (in production: /custom/custom.css, mounted from deploy/custom/): see appearance TZ Europe/Paris display time zone LOG_FORMAT pretty pretty or json; the filter is set with RUST_LOG (default info) MQTT_HOST, MQTT_PORT, MQTT_USER, MQTT_PASSWORD port 1883 MQTT broker (used from R3); without MQTT_HOST the mqtt role is inactive MQTT_CLIENT_ID dominet MQTT client identifier, stable (persistent session) REDUCTSTORE_URL, REDUCTSTORE_TOKEN — ReductStore: raw history archive (iot bucket, from R3), video (R6) IOT_QUOTA_GB, REDUCTSTORE_IOT_BUCKET 5, iot FIFO quota of the iot bucket (applied when it is created) and its name HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS 400 maximum age of the PostgreSQL device history (daily purge) GRAFANA_DASHBOARDS_DIR — folder watched by Grafana where device dashboards are written (device page); without it, generation is refused with a message OPEN_METEO_URL, SOLARMAX_HOST, SOLARMAX_PORT, SOLARMAX_INVERTER_ID, SOLARMAX_TOPIC, SOLARMAX_INTERVAL_SECS public API, —, 12345, 1, default topic, 10 weather and SolarMax publishers: see publishers; SOLARMAX_HOST has no default MEDIAMTX_API_URL — MediaMTX REST API (e.g. http://mediamtx:9997): one path per active camera is created, replaced or removed on the fly, and everything is resynchronised at startup; without it cameras can be saved but nothing is synchronised. Camera passwords are encrypted with DOMINET_MASTER_KEY: without a key a camera password is refused PTZ_DEAD_MAN_SECS 8 a continuous PTZ move that nobody refreshes or stops (frozen tab, cut network) is stopped by the server after this delay, in addition to stopping when the link closes MEDIAMTX_RTSP_URL — MediaMTX RTSP re-stream (e.g. rtsp://mediamtx:8554) decoded by the video role (<url>/<uuid>, 2 frames/s, ffmpeg); when set, dominet serve also starts the video role. Without it: no latest image, no snapshots, no fallback for browsers without H.264 SNAPSHOTS_DIR, SNAPSHOTS_MAX_PER_CAMERA, FFMPEG_HWACCEL data/snapshots (/data/snapshots in the image), 500, auto folder of snapshots (gallery) and of each camera's latest image (latest/) — shared by the video and web roles if they are two processes; beyond the cap the oldest snapshots of a camera are deleted; VAAPI decoding if available (auto) or software (off) RECORDINGS_DIR, RECORDINGS_SEGMENT_DURATION, RECORDINGS_SCAN_SECS, RECORDINGS_GRACE_SECS /recordings, 60, 60, 15 folder where MediaMTX writes the fMP4 segments (<folder>/<uuid>/<date>.mp4, volume shared with MediaMTX), segment length (that of recordSegmentDuration), scan interval of the video role, idle time after which a segment is considered finished VIDEO_QUOTA_GB, REDUCTSTORE_VIDEO_BUCKET 50, surveillance FIFO quota (GB) and name of the ReductStore bucket for video segments; without REDUCTSTORE_URL, segments stay on disk MOTION_THRESHOLD, MOTION_INTERVAL_SECS, MOTION_ALERT_COOLDOWN, DETECTION_ALERT_COOLDOWN 0.01, 30, 600, 300 motion (cameras in motion mode): share of the image that must change, evaluation interval, minimum delays between two notifications of the same camera (motion, detection) YOLO_MODEL_PATH, YOLO_WORKERS, DETECTIONS_DIR models/yolov8n.onnx (/models/yolov8n.onnx in the image), 1, data/detections (/data/detections) detection model (make fetch-model, not committed), ONNX Runtime sessions with one thread each, folder of annotated images. The detector is switched on in the interface (/surveillance/events) EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT, EMAIL_HOST_USER, EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD, EMAIL_USE_TLS, EMAIL_USE_SSL, EMAIL_TIMEOUT_SECS, SMS_FREE_URL —, 587 (465 with SSL), —, —, true, false, 10, official API e-mail sending (usual names) and the Free Mobile API address: see notifications. Without EMAIL_HOST, no e-mail. Credentials without TLS are only allowed towards the loopback

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
dominet serve [--only web,mqtt,...]   starts the server (only `web` exists for now)
dominet migrate | seed [--dry-run] | gen-master-key | createsuperuser | passwd
dominet healthcheck [--addr h:p]      probes GET /healthz (exit 0 on 200): Docker healthcheck, needs neither the database nor the full configuration

docs.title: Probes
docs.text:
• GET /healthz: 200 as long as the process answers (no dependency).
  • GET /readyz: 200 if PostgreSQL answers within 2 s, otherwise 503 (no detail on the cause).
  • Every response carries an x-request-id header (taken from the request if present), also in the logs.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: PostgreSQL 16, accessed through sqlx. Migrations live in crates/dominet-store/migrations/, are embedded in the binary and applied by dominet migrate (never automatically at startup). Running it again has no effect.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Primary keys are BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (the WebSocket contract uses integer device_ids).
  • Timestamps are timestamptz in UTC; display uses Europe/Paris (the TZ setting).
  • No PostgreSQL enums: TEXT + CHECK constraint (easier to evolve).
  • updated_at is maintained by a trigger (set_updated_at) on mutable tables.
  • Secrets are never stored in clear: passwords use argon2id, sensitive setting values are encrypted (ADR 0011).

docs.title: Tables (R1 to R3)
docs.text:
Table Purpose users accounts (role = admin or user, mobile for SMS); case-insensitive unique username session server-side sessions (user_id lets us revoke them all) login_attempt login attempts for progressive lockout app_setting typed settings (str/int/float/bool), is_secret navbar_item navigation (admin_only, sort_order, url = path or external URL) location locations (rooms, zones) message, message_recipient internal messaging (channel, per-recipient delivery status) android_device, sms_message, call_log, sms_outbox Android relay (regenerable UUID token, stored as a SHA-256 hash; send queue with acks, ADR 0037) schedule_job in-process scheduler: interval, cron or solar dashboard an account's dashboards (at most one default, name ≤ 64) widget a dashboard's widgets: type, title, references (device_id, scene_id, camera_uuid, no foreign key until R3/R5/R6), presentation, JSON config, HTML content, rectangle grid_col/grid_row/width/height on 12 columns

| device_group, device_label | device groups (location, icon); state-key labels (name, Lucide icon, unit) | automation.DeviceGroup, DeviceLabel | | device | device: unique Zigbee2MQTT name, type, topic prefix, state (JSONB replaced on every message), last_seen, availability, exposes, tracked / hidden keys (TEXT[]) | automation.Device | | device_state_log | history of tracked keys, one row per device, key and second | automation.DeviceStateLog | | device_image | uploaded device image (resized JPEG, in the database) | image_file | | mqtt_source, weather_station | extra MQTT subscriptions (Linky, SolarMax…); Open-Meteo stations | automation.MqttSource, weather.WeatherStation |

Automations, scenes and alerts arrive in R4 (the foreign key from widget to device exists since R3, ADR 0025; scenes and cameras will follow).

docs.title: Scenes, automations, alerts, energy (R4, migration 0009, ADR 0031)
docs.text:
Table Role scene, scene_action scenes (unique name, icon, location) and their ordered commands (position) to devices automation trigger / condition / action as JSON (trigger_type + trigger_config…), Rhai script, last_triggered, trigger_count automation_run execution journal (instant, cause, status, duration, message) alert_rule, alert rules (operator, threshold, severity, cooldown, channels) and alerts (firing / resolved / acknowledged) energy_daily_log daily balance Linky HP / HC, solar, heat pump (Wh)

widget.scene_id becomes a foreign key to scene (ON DELETE SET NULL); schedule_job gains automation_id and accepts the nine solar events.

docs.title: Android relay (R5, migration 0010, ADR 0037)
docs.text:
• android_device.token is replaced by token_hash (hex SHA-256, unique): the token is generated by gen_random_uuid() in SQL and shown only once (creation or regeneration). Existing devices keep their token (hash computed by the migration).
  • sms_outbox: an SMS requested from a device (own id = the protocol's message_id, pending / sent / failed, error, ack); origin = a browser SMS or a messaging recipient, never both.

docs.title: Devices (R3, migration 0008, ADR 0025)
docs.text:
• device.state is replaced on every message (no merge); the MQTT listener's operations are repository methods, one SQL statement each, idempotent.
  • device_state_log: UNIQUE(device_id, key, ts) per second, batch write with replacement; purge by date (configurable retention).
  • widget.device_id → device(id) ON DELETE SET NULL; a reference to a non-existent device is refused.

docs.title: Dashboards and widgets (R2, migration 0007)
docs.text:
• btree_gist extension (created by the migration): enables the widget_no_overlap exclusion constraint, which forbids two widgets of the same dashboard from overlapping (rectangles in cells, bounds included; contiguous widgets are fine). The invariant is therefore guaranteed by the database, even when two moves arrive at the same time.
  • One default dashboard per account at most (partial unique index); cascade delete user → dashboards → widgets.
  • Widget writes of a dashboard are serialised by a row lock on the dashboard (otherwise PostgreSQL reports a deadlock between two concurrent inserts).
  • Details and reasons: ADR 0018 (in French).

docs.title: Access from code
docs.text:
• The domain (dominet-domain) defines the validated types (Username, SettingKey, NavbarDraft...) and the ports UserRepo, SettingRepo, NavbarRepo, LocationRepo, DashboardRepo, WidgetRepo; dominet-store implements them with PgStore (store.users(), store.settings(), store.navbar(), store.locations(), store.dashboards(), store.widgets(), store.devices(), store.device_groups(), store.device_labels(), store.state_log(), store.device_images(), store.mqtt_sources(), store.weather(), store.scenes(), store.automations(), store.automation_runs(), store.alert_rules(), store.alerts(), store.energy()).
  • Queries are checked at compile time (sqlx::query!). Offline metadata lives in .sqlx/ (tracked by git): after changing a query or a migration, run make sqlx-prepare; make sqlx-check (part of make ci) verifies they are up to date.

docs.title: Architecture decisions: index by theme
docs.text: The full records are the ADRs in adr/ (context, options, decision, consequences). Each exists in English and in French; this page is the map: what was decided in each area, which decisions were reversed or abandoned and why, and what was deliberately left for later.

docs.title: Architecture and build
docs.text:
One binary with roles; server-rendered Leptos with a WebSocket and Fluent translations; server functions under /sf/; a generic CRUD component for administration pages; an image built with cargo-leptos; a guard that retries a frozen render; browser tests on Marionette/Firefox.

ADR: 0001, 0007, 0012, 0014, 0017, 0021, 0024.

docs.title: Data and storage
docs.text:
ReductStore for raw history, PostgreSQL for current state and aggregates; one replaced state plus a per-second history; images in the database; secrets encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM; pg_dump and a ReductStore archive for backups.

ADR: 0002, 0018, 0025, 0028, 0011, 0054.

docs.title: Security and access
docs.text:
Server-side sessions with argon2id; a nonce-based CSP; MQTT with one authenticated listener and per-client accounts; hashed, scoped, revocable MCP tokens with an audit trail.

ADR: 0004, 0016, 0057, 0059.

docs.title: Real time and MQTT
docs.text:
rumqttc; typed WebSocket topics that keep the last state; a supervised client that publishes at once or refuses; Zigbee2MQTT ingestion; supervised weather and solar publishers.

ADR: 0005, 0019, 0020, 0026, 0027, 0030.

docs.title: Automation, alerts and energy
docs.text:
Sandboxed Rhai; stored in the same JSON shape the scenarios use; one engine with one queue; a single scheduler with solar events; alert evaluation and lifecycle; the daily energy balance; alerts on real channels.

ADR: 0006, 0031, 0032, 0033, 0034, 0035, 0036, 0042.

docs.title: Messaging and the phone relay
docs.text:
SMTP and SMS channels in a crate of their own; the Android relay keeps its WebSocket contract; hashed device tokens shown once; asynchronous sending with live status.

ADR: 0037, 0038, 0039, 0040, 0041.

docs.title: Surveillance and video
docs.text:
ffmpeg as a supervised subprocess behind a FrameSource trait; a minimal hand-written ONVIF client; YOLOv8n through ONNX Runtime; WHEP live view in WASM through MediaMTX; MediaMTX records and the application indexes; pure-Rust motion detection.

ADR: 0003, 0008, 0009, 0010, 0043, 0044, 0045, 0046, 0047, 0048, 0049, 0050.

docs.title: Observability and operations
docs.text:
A /metrics endpoint; Prometheus and Grafana rules stored in the database; relay of external alerts; Compose base with overlays; MkDocs served by the application; the local pre-push gate; platform alerts read-only in the alerts page.

ADR: 0013, 0015, 0051, 0052, 0053, 0055, 0056, 0061.

docs.title: MCP and the local assistant
docs.text:
An MCP server built into the binary; scoped tokens; a local model that proposes and an application that decides.

ADR: 0058, 0059, 0060.

docs.title: Decisions reversed, replaced or abandoned
docs.text: Decision What happened Why CI on GitHub Actions (initial) Replaced by a self-hosted runner (0013), then by a local gate: the pre-push hook reruns make ci on a clean copy (0015). The public repository keeps the local gate only The workflow only reran make ci, which the developer already ran on the same machine (also the development and production server): 8 to 10 minutes per push, a dedicated system user, rootless Docker, resource ceilings to maintain, and failures hard to read or reproduce. One developer gains nothing from a per-commit trace Two Mosquitto listeners, one anonymous on the LAN (0055) One listener with passwords and per-client accounts (0057) The new stack is installed fresh, with no existing MQTT client to spare; an anonymous listener, even disabled by default, reopens the broker to the LAN by one configuration slip Two assistant models, 8B daily and 14B for configuration (0060) A single Qwen3-8B Measured 98 % against 96 %, three times faster An assistant that renames and modifies existing elements Dropped; the assistant reads, controls and creates Unreliable with the 8B, and a device's name is also its MQTT topic; administration pages do it better The local assistant phase (R12) Set aside on 2026-11-18 after trials Reading, control and creation were reliable; modification was not Migrating chrono to jiff or time Rejected on 2026-11-20 sqlx 0.9 has no jiff support, and rmcp and schemars keep chrono in the tree anyway. Reopen only on a security advisory, sqlx jiff support, or a need chrono cannot meet Leptos 0.9 (0007) Stayed on 0.8.x leptos-fluent required below 0.9 at the time; reconsider when 0.9 is stable and supported A pure-Rust or linked H.264 decoder Rejected: ffmpeg subprocess (0003) No mature pure-Rust decoder exists (retina does not decode); ffmpeg-next needs development headers; openh264 cost about twice the CPU and failed on two camera families. Measured: 4 cameras at 22 % of the machine in software, 8 % with VAAPI Using an OpenCV binding for motion Rejected: pure-Rust motion (0050) No OpenCV dependency; the algorithm and OpenCV's own details are reproduced and parity is measured against it on synthetic image pairs An ONVIF crate Rejected: a minimal hand-written SOAP client (0008) No mature ONVIF crate fits; only a handful of calls are needed, and camera families use different namespace prefixes, so answers are read without relying on them Replacing MediaMTX with an all-Rust video stack Deferred (optional phase R9) Only worth it if measurements show a real gain Alert acknowledgement of platform alerts Not offered: read-only (0061) Choice of the owner (read-only, one single total in the badge); acknowledgement stays in the tools that own those alerts

docs.title: Decided and not yet done
docs.text:
• An arm64 image was never built (0017); required for the Raspberry Pi 5.
  • Short-message sending is deliberately excluded from the MCP tools.
  • Voice assistant, all-Rust video (R9) and hardware extensions (R10) are later phases.

docs.title: Conventions that cost something to learn
docs.text:
• Any non-obvious decision gets an ADR with the options rejected.
  • Never publish with -C target-cpu=native; the baseline is x86-64-v2 (0001).
  • Nothing is included from outside crates/ (the image copies only that and .sqlx/).
  • A script can reach the system only through the administration scope (0059).

docs.title: DomiNet — Production deployment
docs.text:
Clean install in three commands on an x86_64 machine with Docker (Compose v2.24 or newer):

make prod-init      # creates .env: generated secrets, detected network
$EDITOR .env        # review (e-mail, VPN); nothing else is mandatory
make prod-deploy    # certificates, build, start, administrator, initial data, check

These targets deploy the machine you run them on. Do not run them on the development machine without a separate project and shifted ports (see "Trying it on a development machine"), nor on the old production before the cut-over (R8).

docs.title: 1. Prepare the machine
docs.text:
• Debian 13 / recent Ubuntu, Docker with the Compose plugin, git, make, openssl, curl, jq (optional).
  • mkcert recommended (sudo apt install mkcert): it creates a local authority you install on your devices. Without it make certs produces a self-signed certificate (browser warning; WebRTC and WebSocket still work once accepted).
  • Host name: hostnamectl set-hostname dominet gives dominet.local (mDNS: avahi-daemon). Otherwise make prod-init uses $(hostname).local; force one with LAN_DOMAIN=my-name make prod-init.
  • The detection model is not in the repository: make fetch-model (official Ultralytics export in a throw-away container) — make prod-up does it for you if the file is missing.
  • Zigbee dongle (optional): plugged in before make prod-init, it is detected (/dev/ttyUSB0 or /dev/ttyACM0) and Zigbee2MQTT is enabled.

docs.title: 2. Configure
docs.text:
make prod-init copies .env.example.prod to .env (mode 600, never committed), generates the database, ReductStore, MQTT and Grafana passwords and the Zigbee token, detects the host name and address, and prints the Grafana password. It refuses to overwrite an existing .env.

To review in .env (see .env.example.prod, which comments every variable, and docs/configuration.md):

Variable Role EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_HOST_USER, EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD, EMAIL_RECIPIENT, DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL e-mail alerts (application and Grafana). Without EMAIL_RECIPIENT, Grafana alerts have no recipient DYNDNS_HOST, WG_ADMIN_HASH WireGuard VPN (vpn profile), see §5 MQTT_USER, MQTT_PASSWORD internal MQTT account (DomiNet, Zigbee2MQTT), generated by prod-init. No anonymous access: every LAN client has its own account (§ 7) VIDEO_DEVICE, RENDER_GID hardware video decoding (VAAPI, Intel): written by prod-init when /dev/dri/renderD128 exists; on an existing installation, make prod-video then make prod-up. Without them decoding is in software (about three times more CPU per camera, see docs/R6-mesures.en.md) DOMINET_MASTER_KEY encrypts secrets in the database (camera passwords). Generated on first deployment if empty. Copy it off the machine: without it a restore loses these secrets

make prod-guard (run by the deployment) refuses a missing, empty or default .env.

docs.title: 3. Deploy
docs.text:
make prod-deploy

Runs: prod-guard, certs (if certs/cert.pem is missing), export-ca, prod-up (builds the image, starts the stack and waits until every service is healthy), prod-superuser (asks for the administrator name and password, or reads DOMINET_ADMIN_USER / DOMINET_ADMIN_PASSWORD), prod-seed (initial data, alert rules) and prod-health (nginx → application, no service in a restart loop).

Migrations are applied at start-up by the migrate service. Then open https://<LAN_DOMAIN>.

docs.title: Devices: trust the certificate
docs.text: With mkcert, install the authority on each device by opening http://<LAN_DOMAIN>/dominet-ca.crt (deliberately also served over HTTP, a new device not having the CA yet), then accept it (Android: Settings → Security → Install a CA certificate).

docs.title: 4. Update
docs.text:
make prod-update          # backup, git pull --ff-only, rebuild, restart, check
NOBACKUP=1 make prod-update   # no backup      NOPULL=1: no git pull

A failed backup cancels the update. Migrations are replayed by migrate.

docs.title: 5. Remote access — WireGuard VPN (optional)
docs.text: Set DYNDNS_HOST (public name of your router) and WG_ADMIN_HASH (wg-easy UI password: docker run --rm ghcr.io/wg-easy/wg-easy:14 wgpw 'password', doubling the $ in .env), forward UDP 51820 on the router, then make prod-up. The vpn profile is enabled only when WG_ADMIN_HASH is set. wg-easy uses the host network (iptables-nft); UI on port 51821. If needed add the tunnel addresses to WEBRTC_ADDITIONAL_HOSTS and CERT_EXTRA_SANS (then make certs).

docs.title: 6. Backups and restore
docs.text: An automatic backup runs daily at 03:00 (BACKUP_HOUR): PostgreSQL (pg_dump) and an archive of the ReductStore volume, SHA-256 sums, 7 days kept (BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS), in the backups-data volume. make prod-backup runs one now. Full restore procedures: docs/backups.md. Regularly copy the backups-data volume and DOMINET_MASTER_KEY off the machine.

docs.title: 7. Services and access
docs.text:
Access Address Application https://<LAN_DOMAIN> Documentation https://<LAN_DOMAIN>/docs/ (behind the login, FR/EN) Grafana https://<LAN_DOMAIN>/grafana/ (anonymous viewer; administrator admin / GRAFANA_PASSWORD) WebRTC video https://<LAN_DOMAIN>/webrtc/ (through nginx); RTSP rtsp://<host>:8554/<uuid> Zigbee2MQTT (zigbee profile) http://<host>:8080, token ZIGBEE_AUTH_TOKEN Adminer ADMINER=1 make prod-up, then http://127.0.0.1:8181 (SSH tunnel: ssh -L 8181:127.0.0.1:8181 user@server) MQTT host port 1883, password required; one account per client: make prod-mqtt-user NAME=linky (prints the password once; topic linky/# by default), prod-mqtt-users, prod-mqtt-del

Prometheus and ReductStore are not published on the host. DomiNet's /metrics stays internal.

docs.title: 8. Handy commands
docs.text:
make prod-ps                     # status      make prod-logs S=dominet   # one service's logs
make prod-logs S=dominet N=100   # the last 100 lines, without following (without N: continuous follow, not to be piped into grep or tail)
make prod-passwd U=name          # password (interactive)
make prod-seed-energy            # tracks the keys of the balance and Energy dashboard (DRY=1: simulate)
make prod-dump-context           # YAML snapshot of the installation
make prod-health                 # end-to-end check
make prod-down                   # stop (volumes kept)

docs.title: 9. Trying it on a development machine
docs.text: To check the installation without touching anything else: tools/check-stack.sh <image> (Compose project dominet-chk, shifted ports, throw-away secrets, volumes destroyed afterwards; stop the dev stack first: make dev-down). For a real trial deployment use ENV_FILE, PROJECT and CERTS_DIR and shift the ports in .env (NGINX_HTTP_PORT, NGINX_HTTPS_PORT, POSTGRES_HOST_PORT, MQTT_LAN_PORT); the WebRTC ICE port 8189 is fixed (one stack at a time).

docs.title: 10. Demo
docs.text: cp .env.example.demo .env.demo, edit the passwords, then make demo-up: application over HTTP on :8080, Grafana :3001, a fake camera rtsp://mediamtx:8554/demo-cam-1 to declare in the interface. make demo-down stops it.

docs.title: Dev / prod differences
docs.text: dev (make dev-up) prod (make prod-deploy) Services PostgreSQL, ReductStore, Mosquitto, MediaMTX full stack + nginx DomiNet run from sources (make dev-run) container, non-root user Ports loopback, shifted (1xxxx) nginx 80/443, LAN MQTT, RTSP, ICE Secrets throw-away, set by the Makefile generated .env, mode 600

docs.title: Development machine
docs.text: This page prepares a machine for developing the application. Develop preferably on a fast machine (at least 8 cores and 16 GB); the machine that runs the application every day can be far more modest (see Measurements).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:deunix-educ/domia-automation.git
cd domia-automation && tools/setup-dev-host.sh --ci

tools/setup-dev-host.sh checks the system packages (and prints the apt command if some are missing), installs Rust at the pinned version and the gate tools (cargo-deny, cargo-audit, sqlx-cli, cargo-leptos), enables the pre-push hook, starts the development stack and applies the migrations; with --ci it then runs make ci. tools/check-tools.sh prints the versions of the expected tools.

Prerequisites it cannot install: Docker (with the compose plugin and your user in the docker group) and Firefox (end-to-end tests).

docs.title: Run the application in development
docs.text:
make dev-up        # development stack: PostgreSQL, MediaMTX, Mosquitto, ReductStore
make dev-run       # http://127.0.0.1:8080 (DISCOVERY=1 make dev-run: with the discovery role)

make dev-run (tools/dev-run.sh) builds the binary and the interface if they are missing, applies the migrations, creates the master key and an administrator account on first launch, then starts dominet serve. The credentials are kept in deploy/.env.dev-run (ignored by git, mode 600): never commit it and never print it.

docs.title: The gate before commit and before push
docs.text:
• make ci: format, lints as errors, tests, WASM, cargo deny, cargo audit, SQL metadata. The development stack must be running (make dev-up).
  • make ci-full: adds the Docker image build and the browser tests on that image; run it before a milestone or when the Dockerfile or a native dependency changes.
  • The pre-push hook (make hooks) reruns make ci on a clean copy of the pushed commit. It uses the development stack: do not stop it during a push. If your host drops the connection meanwhile: git -c core.sshCommand="ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30" push.

There is no automatic CI: the gate is local (see Decisions by theme).

docs.title: Disk space
docs.text: target/ grows fast (the hook builds a clean copy in target/prepush, the test profile in target/debug) and can pass several hundred GB. rm -rf target/prepush frees the largest part at no cost (it is rebuilt on the next push). Never build on the production machine.

docs.title: Devices
docs.text: Device pages, commands and administration (R3 lot 5). Decisions: ADR 0025 (schema), ADR 0027 and ADR 0028 (where devices come from), ADR 0029 (this document).

docs.title: For every account
docs.text:
• /automation/ ("Devices" entry of the navigation): active devices as cards following the state live. Filters by group, location and type (a form: the address can be shared).
  • Commands on the cards and on dashboard widgets: ON/OFF, brightness, colour temperature, covers (open, stop, close, position), thermostat set-point (0.5 °C steps), fan modes, lock. They are published on <prefix>/<name>/set; the device confirms by publishing its state again. Buttons are disabled ("source unavailable") when the device is offline or the server is not connected to the broker.
  • /automation/scenes: scenes and their activation, see scenes.md.
  • /automation/devices/<id>: identity (type, group, location, IEEE address, model), state and command topics, last message, last 24 h curves of the tracked keys.

docs.title: For administrators
docs.text:
• Zigbee2MQTT pairing: button on /automation/ (publishes {"time": 254} to open, {"time": 0} to close, on <prefix>/bridge/request/permit_join; Zigbee2MQTT 2.x format, pairing closes by itself after 254 s).
  • /admin/devices, /admin/device-groups, /admin/device-labels: devices (type, group, location, tracked and hidden keys…), groups, state key labels (display name, icon, unit; dominet seed-labels creates the usual ones). Tracked keys are comma-separated; what Zigbee2MQTT discovers (IEEE address, model) and the state cannot be edited by hand.
  • Device image (device page): JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF up to 5 MB; it is reduced to 400 × 300 at most and stored in the database.
  • Device Grafana dashboard (button on its page): one panel per tracked key, written to GRAFANA_DASHBOARDS_DIR (the folder Grafana watches).
  • Widgets (/admin/widgets): the device is picked from a list.
  • Simulator (/admin/settings): injects a state for an existing device (broadcast only, nothing is written to the database).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: cargo test -p dominet --test ui (pages, permissions, commands, administration, Grafana), -p dominet-server --test media (images), --test mqtt_role (commands published on the dev broker), -p dominet-server --lib media grafana, -p dominet-domain (command validation, labels, Grafana dashboard); E2E devices (full journey in Firefox: administration, cards, commands received by the broker, image, curve, Grafana).

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
Daily energy balance, page and API (R4 lot 7). Decisions: ADR 0036, R4 plan (D9).

Every night at 00:05 (local time, TZ setting), the system job compute_daily_energy of the scheduler computes yesterday's balance (local day) from the counters' history and stores it (a recomputed day is replaced).

Balance column Computation (reference) Linky peak / off-peak (Wh) max − min of the day for the cumulative counters HCHP / HCHC, truncated toward zero, never negative Solar production (Wh) day maximum of qdy (kWh, reset every night) × 1000, truncated Heat pump (Wh) max − min of energy_a + max − min of energy_b Net balance production − (Linky + heat pump): positive = surplus

The day is the local day: 23 h on the day of the switch to summer time, 25 h on the day of the return. A missing device counts as zero.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. The three devices must exist (names: ENERGY_LINKY_DEVICE, ENERGY_SOLAR_DEVICE, ENERGY_PAC_DEVICE, defaults consommation, prod, PAC-CE): they come from the Linky / SolarMax / heat pump MQTT sources.
  2. dominet seed-energy (option --dry-run) adds to these devices' tracked keys the ones the computation needs (HCHP, HCHC, qdy, energy_a, energy_b) and the powers of the Grafana "Energy" dashboard (PAPP, pac, power_ab); without history the balance stays at zero. It removes nothing.
  3. dominet aggregate-energy --days 30 (or --date 2026-06-01) computes past days; after that the night job does it.

docs.title: Page and API
docs.text:
• /automation/energy (the "Energy" link on the devices page): four live cards (solar production in W and today's production in kWh; Linky consumption in VA and tariff; heat pump in W; net balance in W, "surplus" or "deficit"), a histogram (solar, Linky, heat pump as bars, net balance as a line) computed by the server as SVG — no JavaScript library —, the 7 / 14 / 30 / 90 day ranges, and the table (most recent first).
  • GET /api/energy/?days=N (signed-in account; 30 by default, 365 at most): {"data": [{"date", "linky_hp_wh", "linky_hc_wh", "linky_total_wh", "solar_wh", "pac_wh", "net_wh"}]}, oldest first.

docs.title: Notable behaviors
docs.text:
• The last N days (not the first N recorded, which would freeze the page after thirty days).
  • Today's production is shown in kWh.
  • The chart is a server-drawn SVG (no external script); the API is at /api/energy/.

docs.title: Grafana dashboard
docs.text: A "DomiNet — Energy" dashboard shows this balance in Grafana, with the self-consumption rate: see observability.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: cargo test -p dominet-automation --test energy (13 days compared with frozen reference values compute_daily_energy: daylight-saving nights, local-day edges, counter reset, day without data, int(1.005 × 1000) truncation), -p dominet-domain --lib energy (SVG without script or style, ticks), -p dominet-server --test energy (seed-energy, the 00:05 job) and --lib (days parameter), -p dominet --test ui energy (API, page), E2E energy (the real scheduler computes yesterday; page, ranges, API, live without reload).

docs.title: Fresh install on the EliteDesk — step by step
docs.text: Production install procedure. You are at the keyboard; each step says what it does and how to check it. Nothing is deleted: containers and volumes of another installation, if any, are left alone (Compose project dominet). Duration: about 1 h, 15 to 20 min of which is the image build.

docs.title: 0. Before starting
docs.text:
• A session on the EliteDesk (SSH or screen), with an account in the docker group.
  • Zigbee dongle plugged in (detected at make prod-init). No other process may hold it.
  • The original mkcert authority, if you want your devices to install nothing: copy rootCA.pem and rootCA-key.pem into the folder given by mkcert -CAROOT (created by mkcert -install if needed) before step 4. Otherwise a new authority is created and each device installs /dominet-ca.crt once.
  • A sheet of paper or a password manager for: the administrator password, the Grafana password, DOMINET_MASTER_KEY.

docs.title: 1. Get the code
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:deunix-educ/domia-automation.git && cd domia-automation
git checkout r8-termine 2>/dev/null || git checkout main      # the tag will exist at the end of the phase

docs.title: 2. Check the machine (read only)
docs.text:
make preflight

It checks architecture, Docker and Compose (2.24 or newer), disk space, ports 80, 443, 1883, 8554, 8189 (TCP and UDP) and 5432 (loopback), the dongle, the GPU, mkcert and its authority, .local name resolution, and lists (without touching them) existing containers and volumes. No BLOQUANT (blocking) item may remain; ATTENTION items are read and judged. A port held by another service is dealt with first (stop that service, or change NGINX_HTTP_PORT, NGINX_HTTPS_PORT, MQTT_LAN_PORT in .env at step 3 — ICE port 8189 and RTSP 8554 are fixed).

docs.title: 3. Initialise and review the configuration
docs.text:
make prod-init       # creates .env (mode 600): generated secrets, detected name and address, detected dongle
$EDITOR .env         # review: EMAIL_* and EMAIL_RECIPIENT (alerts), LAN_DOMAIN, optionally DYNDNS_HOST + WG_ADMIN_HASH (VPN)
make prod-guard      # refuses an empty .env or one left at defaults

make prod-init prints the Grafana password: note it. It refuses to overwrite an existing .env. The detected host name must be the one your devices use (LAN_DOMAIN).

docs.title: 4. Deploy
docs.text:
make prod-deploy     # certificate, build, start, administrator (prompt), initial data, check

The step asks for the administrator's name and password. At the end: DomiNet est prêt : https://<LAN_DOMAIN>. Right after: copy DOMINET_MASTER_KEY (in .env) off the machine. Without it, a restore loses the encrypted camera passwords.

Checks: make prod-ps (all healthy, migrate and init finished), open https://<LAN_DOMAIN> and log in, https://<LAN_DOMAIN>/docs/ (documentation), https://<LAN_DOMAIN>/grafana/ (anonymous viewer; admin + the step-3 password).

docs.title: 5. Devices: trust the certificate
docs.text: On each device that does not know the authority yet, open http://<LAN_DOMAIN>/dominet-ca.crt and install it (Android: Settings → Security → Install a CA certificate). With the original authority reused (step 0), there is nothing to do.

docs.title: 6. Zigbee2MQTT
docs.text: With the dongle detected, Zigbee2MQTT starts by itself (profile zigbee, interface on http://<host>:8080, ZIGBEE_AUTH_TOKEN from .env). If deploy/zigbee2mqtt/ already held a pairing it is kept; otherwise pair your devices (permit join). They then appear under Automation → Devices (DomiNet's MQTT role).

docs.title: 7. LAN MQTT clients
docs.text:
MQTT accepts no anonymous access. Each external client gets its own account:

make prod-mqtt-user NAME=linky       # prints the password ONCE; topic linky/# by default
make prod-mqtt-users                 # lists accounts and their rights

In the client: host LAN_DOMAIN, port 1883 (or MQTT_LAN_PORT), the user name and password. SolarMax is read by DomiNet itself (SOLARMAX_HOST setting), it needs no account.

docs.title: 8. Cameras, scenes, automations, alerts
docs.text:
• Cameras: Administration → Cameras, or Surveillance → Discovery (ONVIF on the LAN); enter the cameras' credentials.
  • Scenes, automations, alert rule: recreate them in the interface from your own configuration. make prod-dump-context produces the new installation's YAML snapshot to compare.
  • Android: Android → add the device, token shown once, to enter in the app.
  • Settings: e-mail (SMTP) and SMS (Free Mobile) in Settings; dominet notify-test (you only) for a real send.

docs.title: 9. Check the result
docs.text: Open the application, sign in, and check the dashboard and the Operations pages (make prod-health does the same end to end).

docs.title: 10. If something goes wrong
docs.text: Symptom What to do prod-deploy stops read the message; make prod-logs S=<service>; fix; rerun make prod-deploy (rerunnable) additional privileges requested: pass "--allow=network.host" during the build old checkout (Compose 5.6+ rejects network: host in build): git pull, then rerun make prod-deploy A service restarts in a loop make prod-ps, then make prod-logs S=<service> Page unreachable curl -k https://127.0.0.1/healthz on the machine; make prod-logs S=nginx; check ALLOWED_HOSTS and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS The "Sign in" button does not react (the page shows, a private window or another browser works) the interface did not start in that tab. In order: Ctrl+Shift+R; Brave: lion icon → turn Shields off for this site (harmless: the site loads no third-party content), sign in, Shields can then be turned back on; Firefox: clear the site cache (padlock → Clear cookies and site data) Firefox refuses the certificate while another browser accepts it Firefox has its own store: Settings → Privacy & Security → Certificates → View Certificates → Authorities → Import dominet-ca.crt (downloaded from http://<LAN_DOMAIN>/dominet-ca.crt) Start over cleanly make prod-down (volumes kept); to erase the Rust stack only: docker compose -p dominet --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml down -v — never docker volume prune, which would touch other stacks

docs.title: 11. After the installation: 48 h of monitoring
docs.text:
Twice a day (morning and evening):

make prod-report                 # READ-ONLY report: services, resources, logs, devices, automations, alerts, backups
HOURS=24 make prod-report        # 24 h window instead of 12
make prod-logs S=dominet N=100   # last 100 lines of one service, without following (without N: continuous follow, Ctrl+C to quit)
make prod-logs S=dominet SINCE=3h | grep -i zigbee2mqtt   # everything since 3 h ago (better than N when looking for a specific event)

The report writes nothing and prints no secret; paste it as is so we can read it together. Look for: no service with growing redemarrages or unhealthy; stable memory and swap; few repeated errors; expected "no message" devices (batteries); explained automation errors; the 03:00 backup present. Grafana → DomiNet — Vue générale shows the curves. Reference values: docs/R8-charge.md.

docs.title: Web interface
docs.text: Server-side rendering (SSR) then WASM hydration, with Leptos 0.8. Decisions: ADR 0007 and ADR 0012 (in French).

docs.title: Code layout
docs.text: Crate Role dominet-server library: configuration, state, authentication, settings, JSON API /api, CLI dominet-web interface: components, pages, Fluent translations, server functions (/sf/…), CSS dominet the dominet binary: assembles the server and the interface dominet-proto types shared between server and browser (DTOs)

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
make dev-up && make db-migrate             # dev database
cargo run -p dominet -- migrate
DOMINET_PASSWORD='a solid password' cargo run -p dominet -- createsuperuser --username admin
make front                                 # cargo leptos build: WASM + JS + CSS in target/site, binary in target/debug
COOKIE_SECURE=false DATABASE_URL=postgres://dominet:dominet-dev@127.0.0.1:15432/dominet target/debug/dominet serve
# http://127.0.0.1:8000

Pitfall: the server and the WASM must be compiled with the same settings, otherwise the page renders but stays inert (disabled buttons). .cargo/config.toml fixes them for every command (--cfg erase_components, LEPTOS_OUTPUT_NAME); do not remove them.

SITE_ROOT (default target/site) is the static files folder. No hot reload: re-run make front then restart the server after a change.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
• make ci: formatting, clippy (server and WASM), tests, cargo deny, cargo audit, sqlx metadata.
  • crates/dominet/tests/ui.rs: full router (FR/EN rendered page, 404, security headers, server function with session, CSRF).
  • Browser E2E (hydration, live translations, session): bash firefox --headless --marionette --profile <folder> -no-remote about:blank & python3 tests/e2e/home.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password' python3 tests/e2e/layout.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password' python3 tests/e2e/auth.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password' python3 tests/e2e/locations.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password' python3 tests/e2e/admin.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password' python3 tests/e2e/users.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password' python3 tests/e2e/realtime.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password' SYSTEM_STATS_SECS=1 … # server started like this for: python3 tests/e2e/system.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/ admin 'a solid password'

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
layout.rs wraps every page (404 included). For a signed-in account the sidebar is part of the server-rendered HTML (blocking layout_data resource), so nothing jumps at hydration. The content offset comes from CSS (.vc-sidebar + .vc-main-wrap), not from a class set in JavaScript.

  • Dynamic navigation: /sf/layout reads the navbar table, drops admin_only entries for a user account and splits top/bottom. An anonymous visitor gets an empty answer (no sidebar).
  • Lucide icons: generated server-side (crates/dominet-server/src/icons.rs, shared with the MCP server) from data/lucide.tsv, built by tools/gen-lucide.py from the the official lucide.min.js (ISC, see data/LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt). Only whitelisted graphic tags are kept; an unknown or invalid name yields the circle-help icon, never free-form HTML.
  • Collapse remembered in localStorage (vc-sidebar-collapsed), mobile menu, full screen, language switcher, sign-out (/sf/logout, which closes the session server-side).
  • SsrMode::Async rendering on routes: everything is resolved server-side before sending. With out-of-order streaming (the default) the sidebar arrived in a <template> inserted by JS after </html> and the content slid from 0 to 220 px (seen in ~2 of 12 loads). ui.rs checks that <aside> precedes the content and that there is no <template>.
  • The ui.rs tests run one at a time (static lock): several Leptos applications rendered in parallel inside one test process disturb each other (frozen render or AppState context not found, ~15% of runs, 0 of 25 when serial). Concurrency on a single application was checked on the real server: 3000 requests, 64 in parallel, all correct.
  • The "Administration" link and the system gauges are deliberately absent: admin pages come in 7d-7f, statistics in R2.

docs.title: Sign-in, guards and account
docs.text:
• /login: form (username, password) calling the login server function. Expected refusals are values of the result (InvalidCredentials, Locked { retry_after_s }), translated in the UI; only an outage is an error (logged, never detailed to the browser). An unknown username and a wrong password give the same answer. Brute-force lockout (5 failures per account+IP pair, 20 per account, 30 per IP over 15 min) applies. The ?next= parameter is filtered by nav::safe_next (internal paths only): no open redirect.
  • Guards: RequireAuth wraps / and /account. For a browser (Accept: text/html) an anonymous visitor gets a real 302 to /login?next=...; the protected page is never sent. An already signed-in account opening /login is sent to its target. These guards are for display: every server function re-checks the session.
  • /account: identity (name, username, email, role, last sign-in) and password change. The current password is required; the policy (10 to 128 characters, not only digits, different from the username) is enforced server-side and each refusal reason is translated. The same lockout as sign-in applies (a stolen session cannot be used to guess the old password): checks are logged as sign-in attempts. A successful change closes every session of the account and sends to /login?notice=password-changed.
  • Before hydration submit buttons are disabled (use_hydrated): otherwise a too-quick submit would go out as a plain HTML form. Forms also use method="post" so a password never ends up in the address.
  • Voluntary leave (leave_session): sign-out and password change navigate to /login and declare the anonymous state before reloading; without this flag the guard of the page being left redirected to /login?next=... and the login page sent back to the home page.
  • E2E: python3 tests/e2e/auth.py url username password (guard, failure then success, live translation, open redirect refused, round-trip password change, sign-out).

docs.title: Administration and generic CRUD
docs.text:
Decision: ADR 0014 (in French). crud.rs provides CrudTable; a page describes its fields (FieldSpec), its list and two actions (save, delete). Admin pages: "Administration" drawer that can be hidden, on the right (tab on the right edge of the screen; administrators only; closes with the arrow, Escape, a click outside or by choosing a page). The links stay in the HTML even when closed (#vc-nav-admin), only hidden. - Logs: /admin/logs (administrators) browses the application log since its last start (in-memory buffer of 20,000 lines, dominet_server::logbuf), newest first, with filters: minimum level, module, text, period, number of lines, refresh every 5 s. The other services stay in make prod-logs. - Tables: a truncated cell (narrow column) carries its full value in its title (tooltip); "Edit" and "Add" bring you back to the top of the page, where the form opens, even from the bottom of a long list.

  • /admin/locations: filterable list (case-insensitive search), add and edit in a form, delete with in-place confirmation. Validation errors come from the server field by field and are translated under the field. An item deleted in the meantime gives a message and a refreshed list, not an error.
  • Permissions: RequireAdmin shows an ordinary account an "Access denied" page (status 403, no data at all); an anonymous visitor is sent to sign-in. Every server function (/sf/locations/{list,save,delete}) re-checks the role.
  • E2E: python3 tests/e2e/locations.py url admin_user password (deletes what it creates).
  • /admin/navbar: same component, with dropdown (position, opens in) and number (order) field types and a help text under the fields. Server-side field-by-field validation (NavbarDraft::problems): icon in lowercase with dashes and existing in Lucide (otherwise the entry would show the fallback icon), internal URL or http(s):// without spaces (javascript: refused), target _self/_blank, order between 0 and 32767. The sidebar updates immediately (navigation reloaded after every write). An internal entry opened in a new tab is a plain HTML link (the router would ignore the target).
  • /admin/settings: the 17 settings are fixed (registry): no CRUD table but one card per category and one editor per type (text, integer, decimal, checkbox). A value incompatible with the type is refused with a translated message. A secret never reaches the browser: it shows "Set / Not set", the field is a password input that is always empty, entering a value replaces it, "Clear" empties it; without DOMINET_MASTER_KEY saving a secret is refused (dedicated message). Descriptions come from the registry and stay in French in both languages. A change applies immediately (service cache and subscribers).
  • Guards and reloads: RequireAuth/RequireAdmin use a Gate component that reads the resource under a Transition (otherwise server rendering does not wait for it) and reacts only to a status change (anonymous / account / administrator) through a memo. Without it, reloading the navigation (what the Navigation page does) re-created the displayed page, which then re-read the stale value serialised in the initial HTML instead of reloading. Every Suspense is a Transition: the old content stays visible during a reload.
  • E2E: python3 tests/e2e/admin.py url admin_user password (navigation and settings; restores everything it changes).

docs.title: Users (/admin/users)
docs.text:
Same CRUD component, with three more field types: password (never prefilled or displayed), display-only column (full name, last sign-in) and a field that is read-only after creation (username). Everything is validated server-side, field by field: username (1 to 150 characters, letters, digits and @ . + - _, case-insensitive uniqueness), email, mobile (normalised), role, password (same policy as My account).

  • "Last administrator" rule: enforced in the repository (update_profile and delete), not only in the screen. A transaction takes a PostgreSQL advisory lock on the administrator set, re-reads the target account and refuses (RepoError::LastAdmin) any operation that would leave zero active administrators: delete, deactivate, demote. Without the lock, two administrators demoting each other at the same time would each see "one remains" and both succeed (race test in repos.rs and ui.rs, verified by disabling the lock).
  • Protections on your own account (deliberately stricter than the rule above): an administrator cannot delete, deactivate, demote themselves or change their password from this screen (My account is for that): their session would be cut mid-page. To lift it, remove the Blocked::Yourself / Blocked::OwnPassword checks in save_user and delete_user.
  • Immediate effect: deactivating an account cuts its current session (the account is re-read on every request); resetting its password closes all its sessions; deleting an account deletes its sessions (cascade).
  • Passwords are never returned or logged (UserInput and NewAccount hide the field in Debug).
  • E2E: python3 tests/e2e/users.py url admin_user password (deletes the account it creates).

docs.title: Server integration, CSP and real time
docs.text:
Decisions: ADR 0016 (in French).

  • Nonce-based CSP, set during rendering (csp.rs, called by App): a different nonce per response, on Leptos's scripts and in the header. No inline script or style: write neither style="…" nor on…="…" in views (use classes and on:).
