If a feature needs a third-party resource (Grafana iframe, camera stream), add the matching directive in csp::policy.
  • Page rendering: a GET whose render does not answer within 5 s is abandoned and retried (3 attempts, then 503 with Retry-After), a workaround for a Leptos 0.8.23 defect (ADR 0021, in French); tools/stress-cold-render.sh measures the defect on the image.
  • Static files: /pkg/* revalidated on every load (no-cache), pages and server functions no-store, gzip, COOP/CORP same-origin.
  • WebSocket /ws/notifications/: session required, Origin checked, ping/pong heartbeat (WS_HEARTBEAT_SECS), session re-validated at every beat (sign-out, deactivation, deletion or password change cut the connection), at most 8 connections per account.
  • Browser: the "Real time" indicator in the sidebar shows the state (connecting, connected, offline); the connection comes back by itself with an increasing delay. Notifications are shown as plain text. Settings → Broadcast a message (administrators) sends a message to every signed-in user: it also checks the chain.
  • Per-topic subscriptions (ADR 0019, in French): on the same connection the client sends {"type":"subscribe","topic":"device:7"} (or unsubscribe); topics are notifications (automatic), system, device:<id>, camera:<uuid> (refused until R6). The server answers subscribed, then sends the topic's last known state, or refused (invalid, forbidden, limit at 128 subscriptions). In the browser: Realtime::subscribe(&Topic::Device(7)) / unsubscribe (reference-counted, restored on every reconnection) and Realtime::device(id) to read the state.
  • System gauges (ADR 0020, in French): processor, memory, disk and temperature in the sidebar, fed by the system topic (measured every SYSTEM_STATS_SECS s). GET /api/system-stats/ (signed-in account) returns the document described here (cpu, memory, disk, updated_at) plus temperature; disk and temperature are null when the machine does not expose them, and the API answers 503 until a first measure exists. Bars get their width through the CSSOM (style:width): the CSP forbids a rendered style attribute.
  • Settings → Device state simulator (administrators): publishes a JSON state for a device number and shows live what the browser receives; it is the source until MQTT (R3) lands.
  • Extending: add a variant to WsServerMsg (dominet-proto) and, for a new topic, a Topic variant and a rule in authorize (web/ws.rs); publish with state.hub.publish(&topic, message) (or publish_retained to keep the last state); handle the message in realtime.rs.
  • Tests: crates/dominet/tests/ws.rs (real server and WebSocket client: authentication, foreign origin, limit, heartbeats, cut on sign-out/deactivation, subscriptions, last state, refusals, 128 limit), ui.rs (CSP and nonce on every page, cache, compression), E2E python3 tests/e2e/realtime.py url admin_user password ["server restart command"] (nonce-less script blocked, WebSocket connected, broadcast, sign-out, reconnection after restart, device state simulator, resubscription after restart).

docs.title: Dashboard (/)
docs.text:
Decisions: ADR 0022 (in French). Read-only (editing arrives in lot 5).

  • Data: dashboard_page(d) (server function) returns the account's own dashboards (never another account's), the open one (?d=<id> if it belongs to the account, else the default, else the first) and its widgets ready to display: HTML already sanitized, iframe address already checked, last known device state. create_dashboard(name) creates a dashboard (the first one becomes the default). An account without a dashboard sees an invitation to create one.
  • Placement: a widget carries the classes vc-c-N, vc-r-N, vc-w-N, vc-h-N (column 1–12, row 1–100, width and height 1–12). Never a style attribute (CSP). On medium and narrow screens widgets flow one after the other. Maximum row in the domain: 99.
  • Types: text (HTML sanitized by ammonia), grille, grafana (iframe only towards the origin of GRAFANA_PUBLIC_URL, otherwise "address refused"; the CSP gets frame-src for that origin), device (below), camera (R6) announced and scene (scenes: name and activation button).
  • Devices: the widget subscribes to device:<id> (ADR 0019) and follows the state live; the frame is green when the device is on, dimmed when unavailable. The requested presentation (device/light…) wins; when automatic it is inferred from the state keys (dominet_domain::widget_view). Controls (ON/OFF, sliders, +/−) are present but disabled until R3. Before R3 the state comes from the simulator (Settings → Device state simulator).
  • Extending: a new presentation = a Presentation variant (domain), a case in resolve_presentation if it must be inferred, a *_view function in dashboard.rs.
  • Editing (ADR 0023, in French) — administrators only (every server function refuses the others: 403):
  • Move: drag a widget's header (mouse, finger or stylus) on wide screens (≥ 1201 px). A dashed frame shows the target cell; on release move_widget saves, or refuses (outside the grid, position taken) and the widget snaps back with a message. Persistent (reload).
  • Dashboards: /admin/dashboards (all accounts; owner = user name, fixed at creation).
  • Widgets: /admin/widgets?d=<id>; the form only shows the fields of the chosen type (field_visible of the generic CRUD); overlap reported on "Column"; text widget HTML sanitized when saving; an "Edit widgets" button on the dashboard.
  • An ordinary account sees its dashboards without editing them: an administrator fills them for it.
  • Pitfalls: no StoredValue::new_local in a server-rendered component (panic, stalled page); no resource whose source depends on another resource (out-of-order loads at hydration); no braces {…} in a .ftl; wait for hydration ("Real time: connected") before clicking in an E2E.
  • Tests: ui.rs (invitation, creation, placement, sanitizing, Grafana and CSP, selector and account isolation, editing rights, per-field validation, refused moves), widget_view and html (unit), E2E dashboard.py (prepares its widgets in SQL through E2E_DB_SHELL, set by tools/e2e.sh).

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: Fluent (crates/dominet-web/locales/{fr,en}/main.ftl). English by default; the language comes from the lang cookie, then Accept-Language; the switcher changes it without reloading. <html lang> is kept in sync.

docs.title: Adding a language
docs.text:
French and English are the reference languages (documentation, E2E tests); another language is added without touching the code:

make i18n-new LANGUE=es          # creates crates/dominet-web/locales/es/main.ftl from English (FROM=fr to start from French)
make i18n-status                 # per language: messages still identical to English, missing or extra keys, differing variables
make i18n-status LIST=1          # ... and the list of keys to translate
make front                       # rebuilds the interface: the language shows up in the selector

Translate each value without touching the keys or the variables ({ $minutes }); texts that French shares with English ("OK", "Grafana"…) stay as they are. The name shown in the selector ("Español") comes from the code: it must be known to leptos-fluent (es, de, it, pt-BR…), otherwise the build stops and says so. The language is then chosen like the others: lang cookie, then Accept-Language; an unknown language falls back to French.

Translations are compiled into the binary: a new language requires rebuilding the image (make prod-up). The test cargo test -p dominet-web --test i18n, replayed by make ci, requires every language to define exactly the keys of English, with the same variables: an incomplete file or a renamed variable fails the push. The documentation (this site) stays in French and English.

docs.title: Supported machines
docs.text:
What was tested, what was not, and how to add your own measurements. Nothing here is promised beyond what the "Status" column says.

Machine Status Notes Intel Core i5-6500 mini PC, 8 GB (reference) tested and measured 12 cameras in 1080p with hardware decoding (VAAPI): see Measurements amd64 mini PC, 16 GB (for example a one-amd8 class machine) not tested yet Same image as the reference. Expected to do at least as well; hardware decoding needs an Intel GPU with VAAPI Raspberry Pi 5, 8 GB, NVMe SSD installs and runs (2026-11-23) arm64 image built and started on the machine, then published; 6 cameras in 1080p measured at 40 % of the machine (software decoding); see below Other arm64 or amd64 Linux with Docker untested The installer does not refuse them; it warns on arm64

docs.title: Raspberry Pi 5: what to expect, what is unknown
docs.text:
What was verified on a Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB, NVMe SSD, Debian 13 arm64, Docker 29): the image builds natively in about 67 minutes (no swap problem with 2 GB of swap), the whole stack starts, the database schema is applied, an administrator account is created, and the interface answers in about 10 ms (median) with the stack idle, at 55 °C and never throttled. The ten services at rest hold about 310 MiB, the whole machine 1.1 GB of its 8 GB, and a start from cold takes about 22 s. Cameras: 6 in 1080p occupy 40 % of the four cores in full mode (Measurements, section 2); nothing above 6 was measured.

Known from the design (not from measurements):

  • Operating system: 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS (Debian 13 based) or Debian 13 arm64; Docker with the Compose plugin 2.24 or newer. A 32-bit system cannot run the images.
  • Storage: use an SSD (USB 3 or NVMe), not an SD card. The database and the video recordings write continuously; an SD card wears out. The installer warns when / is on an SD card.
  • Video decoding: the Intel hardware decoder (VAAPI) is not available on arm64; video is decoded by the processor, so it holds fewer cameras than the reference machine: about 0.25 core per camera in software, against 0.12 with VAAPI.
  • Object detection (YOLO on CPU): not measured on arm64. Keep it off at first, then enable it on one camera and watch the load.
  • First installation: the published image now exists for arm64, so the installer downloads it instead of building (a local build took about 67 minutes on a Pi 5; it remains the fallback, ADR 0062).
  • Memory figures: for docker stats to show the memory of the containers, the kernel needs the memory cgroup: add cgroup_enable=memory cgroup_memory=1 to the line of /boot/firmware/cmdline.txt and reboot. Without it the machine card shows 0B for every service.
  • Zigbee dongle: works the same way (/dev/ttyUSB0 or /dev/ttyACM0).
  • Power and cooling: use the official power supply and a heat sink or fan; vcgencmd get_throttled (reported by the machine card) shows whether the Pi was ever throttled.

docs.title: Measure your machine
docs.text:
After make prod-deploy (or ./install.sh) and a few idle minutes:

tools/machine-card.sh > card.md          # add --with-backup to time a backup too

The card lists the hardware, the architecture of the image, the memory and CPU of each service at rest, the interface latency (median and 95th percentile over 50 requests) and, on a Pi, temperature and throttling. It is read-only and contains no password. Add the cold start time (make prod-down, then time make prod-up) and the number of cameras you hold, then paste the result in Measurements or share it in an issue: a result on a machine that is not listed is the most useful contribution to this table.

docs.title: Dropping what a small machine cannot carry
docs.text:
• Fewer cameras, or lower stream resolution on the camera side.
  • VIDEO_QUOTA_GB and IOT_QUOTA_GB in .env bound the history kept on disk.
  • Grafana and Prometheus can be stopped (docker compose stop grafana prometheus) if memory is short; the application keeps working, you lose the dashboards.
  • The local assistant (an LLM) is a separate, optional program that needs far more than a Pi 5 offers; do not plan on it there.

docs.title: R11 — M0: server function audit and framing (2026-11-15)
docs.text: Work package M0 of the MCP roadmap (not kept): find out where the interface logic lives, how much of it the assistant can reuse, and settle the technology (SDK, mounting, transport, tokens). Decisions: ADR 0058 (server) and ADR 0059 (tokens), written in French like all ADRs. The full table is in tests/mcp/coverage.tsv; a make ci test fails if a server function is not classified there.

docs.title: What the audit measured
docs.text:
• 107 server functions in 20 files of dominet-web (3,482 body lines in total): 75 restricted to administrators, 25 open to any signed-in account, 7 tied to the session or the current account (sign in, sign out, password, personal dashboard).
  • The pattern is uniform: expect_context::<AppState>(), an access check (require_admin / require_user), then logic that calls AppState and the repositories directly. Only 7 functions call leptos_axum directly: the session and current-account ones. No deep coupling: the logic can be extracted.
  • Control is already reusable: send_device_command and set_permit_join call dominet_server::control. Configuration is not yet: the save_* functions (up to 98 lines) hold validation, writing and the reload signal. They will have to move into dominet-server as service(&AppState, &Actor, input) so the interface and MCP share one code path (work packages M2 to M5).
  • Technology: rmcp 3.10.0 (official SDK, Apache-2.0, Rust 1.88 minimum) passes cargo deny and adds no cargo audit warning. The server is session-less (plain JSON responses), protected against DNS rebinding (Host header limited to localhost and ALLOWED_HOSTS) and works with a client on the previous protocol revision (tested).

docs.title: Findings that change the roadmap
docs.text:
1. Rhai scripts get in through the back door. save_automation ("script" action) and save_mqtt_source (handler code) accept Rhai code. With a config_upsert at configuration scope, a configuration token would write scripts, bypassing the 2026-11-13 choice "scripts = administration". Proposed rule: any config_upsert whose payload contains a script requires the administration scope.
  2. Reading configuration requires admin today. All 75 administrator-only functions, configuration listings included, require that role. For MCP, config_list and config_get at read scope (like automations_list) allow a diagnostic token with no right to change anything; secrets stay masked. Validated on 2026-11-16.
  3. The built-in assistant (R12) has no token: it acts on behalf of the session. The common service must therefore receive an actor (Token{scopes} or Session{account}), not just an account. To plan from M1 to avoid redoing the extraction.
  4. dry_run on control. R12 requires a dry run for every action; ROADMAP-mcp.md only plans it for deletions and configuration. To add to device_command and scene_run (M3).
  5. No way back. dominet dump-context exports the configuration but nothing re-imports it: R12's rollback tool needs a reliable restore that R11's catalogue does not have.
  6. Error messages. Server functions answer "internal error" or "access denied": fine for a browser, poor for an assistant. Domain validation already returns an error per field; the tools must pass it on as is.
  7. 30 s timeout on the whole router: enough for tools that answer in milliseconds; to watch for automation_test and logs_query.

docs.title: Delivered in this work package
docs.text: dominet-mcp crate (system_status tool, temporary Bearer authentication MCP_SPIKE_TOKEN, off by default MCP_ENABLED=false), mounting through serve(.., dominet_mcp::routes), end-to-end tests with a real MCP client (cargo test -p dominet-mcp), the coverage guard, ADR 0058 and 0059. See MCP server for the trial with Claude Code.

docs.title: MCP server (R11, in progress)
docs.text:
DomiNet's MCP server lets an assistant (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or any MCP client) read, drive and configure the application under the same rules as the interface, without ever seeing a secret. Roadmap: ROADMAP-mcp.md; decisions: ADR 0058 and ADR 0059 (in French); audit: R11-audit.

State: work package M4d (configuration)

Tokens and audit (M1), read (M2), control and cameras (M3) and configuration (M4 to M4e, sixteen kinds) and administration (M5) are in place. Still to come: acceptance (M6).

docs.title: Enable
docs.text:
In .env (the server is off by default):

MCP_ENABLED=true

Then recreate the dominet service (make prod-up). The endpoint is https://dominet.local/mcp; it is reachable from the LAN and the VPN only. The Host header must be localhost or listed in ALLOWED_HOSTS (protection against DNS rebinding). Without a token, nobody gets in.

docs.title: Create a token
docs.text:
Page Administration › Assistants (MCP) (/admin/mcp): a name, the scopes and a validity period (30 to 365 days: a token without an end date does not exist). The token value, dnm_…, is shown once, with the command ready to paste into Claude Code; only its hash is kept, it cannot be read back. A lost token is revoked and created again.

Scope Allows lecture (read) look at devices, history, logs, alerts and configuration (secrets masked) pilotage (control) command devices, run scenes, acknowledge alerts configuration change automations, rules, dashboards and sources administration settings, cameras and Rhai scripts

Scopes are independent: configuration does not grant lecture. Use a lecture token for everyday diagnosis and a wider one only for the time of a change.

docs.title: Connect Claude Code
docs.text:
claude mcp add --transport http dominet https://dominet.local/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

The workstation must trust DomiNet's certificate authority (/dominet-ca.crt). The command was verified with Claude Code on the development stack (address http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp); the https://dominet.local trial on the EliteDesk is still to do (M6). To connect the assistant for one folder only, add --scope local; claude mcp list must show dominet … ✔ Connected, claude mcp remove dominet removes it.

docs.title: Step-by-step trial (development stack)
docs.text:
A complete trial that never touches production: the development stack is disposable.

  1. Start the stack and the server, MCP on: bash make dev-up cargo leptos build # the first time, or after a change MCP_ENABLED=true tools/dev-run.sh # server on http://127.0.0.1:8080, log line "serveur MCP monte sur /mcp"
  2. Create a token: sign in at http://127.0.0.1:8080 (development account and password in deploy/.env.dev-run), page Administration › Assistants (MCP), name trial, the four scopes, 30 days. Copy the dnm_… value (shown once). Without the interface, for a trial only: insert into the development database the SHA-256 hash of a token of your choice (mcp_token, columns name, token_hash, prefix, scopes, expires_at).
  3. Connect Claude Code, in a trial folder: bash mkdir -p ~/essai-mcp && cd ~/essai-mcp claude mcp add --transport http --scope local dominet http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer dnm_…" claude mcp list # dominet … ✔ Connected
  4. Ask questions (interactive claude, or claude -p "…" --allowedTools "mcp__dominet"):
  5. Read: "Give me the overall system status and which devices have been silent for 24 hours." (system_status, devices_list).
  6. Simulation: "Propose, without writing anything, creating a place called 'Essai MCP'." (config_schema, config_upsert with dry_run).
  7. Write: "Create the place, a 'Lampe-essai' device of type light attached to it, then an automation that sends a notification when a message arrives on essai/bouton." Then "Read the automation back with config_get".
  8. Secrets: "Create a camera 'Cam essai' with the password …, then read it back." The password cannot be read back: only has_rtsp_pass: true.
  9. Safeguards: "Delete the place without confirming." The call is refused (confirm = true required); dry_run says first what depends on the item.
  10. Check: the Administration › Assistants (MCP) page shows the audit trail (one line per write or refusal, never a token value or a secret). The created items show up in the interface.
  11. Clean up: claude mcp remove dominet, revoke the token on the MCP page, stop the server (Ctrl+C), make dev-reset to start again from an empty database.

Result of the 2026-11-16 trial (Claude Code, development stack): the assistant read the system status, simulated then really created a place, a device, an automation and a camera, read the automation back, noted it could not see the camera password, and was refused a deletion without confirm. The audit trail holds the four writes and no secret. Claude Code prints unknown format "uint32" ignored in schema warnings: harmless, they come from the output schemas.

docs.title: Claude Desktop (to be verified)
docs.text:
Claude Desktop cannot send an Authorization header to a remote server declared in its interface: use the mcp-remote bridge (Node.js required), in claude_desktop_config.json:

{ "mcpServers": { "dominet": {
    "command": "npx",
    "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://dominet.local/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${DOMINET_AUTH}"],
    "env": { "DOMINET_AUTH": "Bearer dnm_…", "NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS": "/path/dominet-ca.crt" }
} } }

This setup has not been tried here (no Claude Desktop on the development machine); it follows the usual mcp-remote method. A narrower token (lecture only) is the right choice for a mainstream client.

docs.title: Ready-made prompts
docs.text:
Three templates, offered with the lecture scope (they are plain text: they grant no right the token does not have). In Claude Code they are called /mcp__dominet__diagnostic, /mcp__dominet__nouvelle_automation and /mcp__dominet__bilan_surveillance.

Prompt Argument What it makes the assistant do diagnostic hours (12) system status, silent devices, alerts, recent errors, failing automations, then a 5-line summary nouvelle_automation need (required) read the real devices and scenes, read the schema, propose in plain words, simulate (dry_run), create only after your agreement bilan_surveillance hours (24) cameras, detections, recordings, energy, alerts; no snapshot or camera move unless asked

docs.title: Check a server read-only
docs.text:
MCP_TOKEN=dnm_… tools/check-mcp.sh http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp                   # development stack
CACERT=dominet-ca.crt MCP_TOKEN=dnm_… tools/check-mcp.sh https://dominet.local/mcp   # EliteDesk

The script checks the refusal without a token (401), counts the tools and prompts offered to the token and calls system_status. It writes nothing and never prints the token.

docs.title: Acceptance on the EliteDesk (for you to run)
docs.text:
Nothing is run on production without you. In order:

  1. Enable: add MCP_ENABLED=true to the EliteDesk's .env, then make prod-up (the MCP server is off by default).
  2. Check the refusal: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST --cacert dominet-ca.crt https://dominet.local/mcp must answer 401.
  3. Create a lecture token, 30 days, page Administration › Assistants (MCP).
  4. Check: CACERT=dominet-ca.crt MCP_TOKEN=dnm_… tools/check-mcp.sh https://dominet.local/mcp.
  5. Connect Claude Code (trusted workstation: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/dominet-ca.crt if the CA is not installed) then claude mcp add --transport http dominet https://dominet.local/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer dnm_…".
  6. Diagnostic: run /mcp__dominet__diagnostic. Compare with the home page and the Logs page.
  7. One reversible action (a pilotage token, created for the occasion): ask to switch a lamp on then off; check the two audit-trail lines.
  8. Revoke the trial tokens; keep MCP_ENABLED=true or remove it, as you prefer.

Note what differs from the development trial: certificate, host name (ALLOWED_HOSTS), real devices.

docs.title: Available tools (read)
docs.text:
Twenty tools, all at lecture (read) scope; an assistant only sees those its token allows.

Tool Purpose system_status version, database, active and unreachable devices, alerts firing, Zigbee pairing, machine load devices_list devices: reachable, last message, silence in hours, place, group; filters (silent_for_hours, reachable, type, name, inactive) device_get one device (name or number): current state, MQTT topics, recorded keys device_history history of a key (temperature, power…): points, minimum, maximum, average automations_list automations: trigger, action, last firing, firing count automation_get one automation in detail, without a script's code automation_runs run journal: when, outcome (ok, error, skipped, limited) and message; filter by automation and outcome scenes_list scenes and what each sends to each device alerts_list alerts (firing, acknowledged, resolved), severity, triggering value cameras_list cameras: active, priority, address, PTZ, ONVIF, last seen; no credential logs_query the application log since it started: level, module, text, window snapshots_list picture captures: number, camera, date, size; filter by camera and day snapshot_get the image of a capture (JPEG, 2 MB at most) recordings_list video recordings: camera, start, length, trigger, state detections_list motion and object detections (person, car…) energy_summary daily energy balance: Linky (peak and off-peak), solar, heat pump, with totals

Resource dominet://context: the configuration snapshot (what dominet dump-context writes) as YAML, without secrets and without script code (replaced by a marker). The best starting point to understand an installation.

Questions that work: "Which devices have said nothing for 24 hours?" (devices_list with silent_for_hours: devices that never spoke are included, first), "Why did the Ouvrir le volet automation fail?" (automation_runs with error: the message gives the cause), "What has the office temperature been since this morning?" (device_history).

Output rules: local times, never UTC; no secret; a Rhai script's code is only readable at administration scope; text that comes from outside (names, messages, log lines) is marked as data (notice), never as instructions. Coming: control (M3), configuration (M4), settings and scripts (M5).

docs.title: Control tools (pilotage scope)
docs.text:
Nine tools act on the house. Each accepts dry_run = true: it then says what it would do, changing nothing and writing nothing to the audit trail.

Tool Purpose device_command sends a JSON command to an active device ({"state": "OPEN"}, {"position": 40}…); a deactivated device is not drivable scene_run runs an active scene: its commands go out in order, failures are reported alert_ack acknowledges one firing alert (alert) or all (all); the acknowledgement is attributed to the account that created the token notify_broadcast shows a banner (200 characters) to every signed-in account notify_test sends a test e-mail to the alert recipient (address never shown); SMS do not go through MCP camera_ptz moves a PTZ camera for 100 to 3,000 ms (up, down, left, right, zoom_in, zoom_out) then stops it by itself; the stop is guaranteed even if the connection drops camera_night switches day / night, infrared filter or light, through the method set for the camera camera_record starts or stops recording on a camera set to manual mode (otherwise refused with a reason) camera_snapshot takes a picture now (the video role must be running) and returns its number

No action without a trace. Every call that changes something writes its line to the audit trail before it runs (outcome pending), then closes it with what happened (ok or error). If the trail cannot be written, the call is refused and nothing is sent. A call refused for lack of scope, an inactive device or an invalid command leaves no action: only the scope refusal is recorded (denied). Decisions taken on the built-in assistant (R12) have their own type, agent: the request in clear, the action confirmed or turned down, and what it takes to undo it (ROADMAP-agent.md section 14).

docs.title: Configuration (lecture and configuration scopes)
docs.text:
Seven tools read and write the configuration, for sixteen kinds: place (location), scene (scene), automation (automation), alert rule (alert_rule), device group (device_group), state-key label (device_label), MQTT source (mqtt_source) weather station (weather_station), Prometheus rule (prometheus_rule) Grafana rule (grafana_rule), dashboard (dashboard, named owner/name) widget (widget, placed on the 12-column grid), device (device: its parameters, never its state), navigation-bar entry (navbar, Lucide icon checked) and camera (camera, administration scope) and the object detector (detector: a single item, changed but never created or deleted). A widget that would leave the grid or overlap another is refused at dry_run; its text content is sanitised; deleting a dashboard deletes its widgets (the dry_run gives the count); deleting a device deletes its history and leaves its widgets without a device. Saving or deleting a rule rewrites rules.yml or rules.yaml and reloads the service (best effort: a failed reload does not undo the save, the rules page shows the state).

Tool Scope Purpose config_kinds read the configurable kinds, with their read and write scopes config_schema read what config_upsert accepts for a kind: JSON schema, full example and notes (the keys of each trigger and action) config_list, config_get read the items of a kind, in the exact shape config_upsert accepts: read, change a field, write config_upsert configuration creates (no id) or replaces (with id) an item; dry_run shows the fields that would change config_delete configuration deletes; confirm = true required, dry_run says what depends on it zigbee_pairing configuration opens (254 s at most) or closes Zigbee pairing

The same checks as the interface, because the path is the same: a shared service (dominet_server::config_service) validates the domain draft, checks that a Rhai script compiles and that the target scene exists, turns name conflicts into field errors, then reloads the automation engine, the scheduler or the alert evaluation. A dry_run therefore announces exactly the refusals of a real write. Unknown fields are refused (a typo is not silently ignored).

Rhai code (an automation's script, an MQTT source's handler_code) and a Grafana rule's SQL query (any datasource other than prometheus): never readable (script is null, has_script says so). Writing, changing or removing it needs the administration scope in addition. An update that does not mention script keeps the existing code: reading an automation, changing one field and writing it back never erases its code.

Example, end to end: "close the shutters at sunset" → config_schema (kind automation) → config_upsert with dry_run, then without. The dominet://context snapshot before and after differs by that automation only (it is a test).

docs.title: Administration (administration scope)
docs.text:
The administration scope opens what is sensitive: settings, script code, cameras. It is independent of the others and rarely given.

  • Settings: settings_list (the value of a secret is never returned, only is_set) and setting_set (value validated against the setting's type; a secret is encrypted; dry_run says whether the value would be accepted).
  • Rhai scripts: script_get reads the code of an automation (script action) or of an MQTT source; script_check compiles it and, given a topic, tries it on a sample message in the real sandbox, publishing nothing; script_set replaces it after the same checks as the interface. No other tool ever shows that code.
  • Cameras: the camera kind of config_* (reading, writing and deleting all need administration, since it holds addresses and user names). The passwords (rtsp_pass, onvif_pass, web_pass) and the API key (web_api_key) are write-only: config_get only says has_rtsp_pass…; a field left out keeps the secret in place. cameras_sync updates MediaMTX (target = mediamtx) or learns what a camera announces (target = onvif).

No secret appears in any answer or in the audit trail: a test sweeps the outputs.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Immediate revocation: a revoked or expired token is refused from the next call.
  • Rate limit per token (MCP_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN, 120 by default): beyond it, 429 with Retry-After.
  • Audit trail (same page): token creation and revocation, refused calls and, from work package M3, calls that change something. Secrets are masked there; purged after MCP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (365 days by default).
  • Without a token, or with a wrong, expired or revoked one, the answer is 401 (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer); with an unknown Host, 403; server disabled, 404. Neither the Authorization header nor a token value is logged.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: cargo test -p dominet-mcp: a real MCP client (rmcp) against a real server and the test database, every read tool on real data (--test read), token read from the database, revocation, expiry, refused and audited scope, rate limit, Host protection, a client on the previous protocol revision, disabled server; --test coverage: every server function of the interface must be classified in tests/mcp/coverage.tsv. Repositories: cargo test -p dominet-store --test mcp.

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
Every figure that drove a decision, with the machine, the method and how to redo it. Use it as a baseline: a result far from these numbers means something changed.

Reference machines. Target: Intel Core i5-6500 (Skylake, 4 cores, no AVX-512), 7.8 GB RAM, Intel HD 530 (VAAPI), Debian 13. Development: 20 threads, 48 GB RAM, RTX 4060 8 GB, no usable VAAPI.

docs.title: 1. Feasibility spikes (phase R0)
docs.text: Topic Verdict Key figure Server-rendered Leptos with hydration, WebSocket and translations go 16 of 16 browser checks; WASM 448 KB (190 KB gzip) Time-series store, 1 million records go 1 680 writes/s; threshold query 99 ms per device WHEP live view in WASM go 40 ms latency (VP8, local loop); real 720p live validated H.264 decoding go, with ffmpeg 4 cameras: 22 % of the machine in software, 8 % with VAAPI ONNX Runtime with YOLOv8n go with reservations 43 to 106 ms per image; detections identical to the reference model on 10 of 10 images ONVIF against 4 real cameras go authentication, profiles, PTZ and IR-cut work; one camera absent from multicast discovery Sandboxed Rhai scripts go 18 of 18; a hostile script is cut in under 45 ms MQTT client go no loss at 2 000 msg/s; reconnection in 0.6 s

docs.title: 2. Video load (phase R6)
docs.text:
Tool: tools/bench-video.py. Nothing shared with a running system: throw-away PostgreSQL, MediaMTX and ReductStore on shifted ports, no real camera.

Protocol. Simulated cameras are one 1080p, 15 fps, 3 Mbit/s H.264 clip encoded once and republished with -c copy (their own cost is 0.01 to 0.08 core in total). Three scenarios, 20 s warm-up then 60 s measured, a sample every 5 s: decode only (2 decoded frames per second); full (continuous recording in 60 s fMP4 segments, indexing and archiving, motion every 30 s, YOLO on each motion); stress (motion every 5 s, six times more YOLO). "Cores" counts the application, its decoding ffmpeg processes, MediaMTX, ReductStore and PostgreSQL together, in average whole cores.

Target machine Cameras Cores Memory (MB) Machine busy VAAPI, decode only 4 0.46 673 15 % VAAPI, decode only 12 1.35 1 782 45 % VAAPI, full 4 0.55 863 18 % VAAPI, full 12 1.47 1 885 45 % VAAPI, stress 12 1.34 1 826 43 % Software, decode only 4 1.12 747 30 % Software, full 8 2.20 1 445 60 %

What it says:

  • A camera costs about 0.11 core with VAAPI (0.12 in full mode) and 0.28 core in software. VAAPI divides the video cost by about three (decoder ffmpeg: 0.31 against 0.98 core for 4 cameras; on a file, 3.5 s of CPU against 10.4 s for 100 s of video).
  • 12 cameras in 1080p are held at 45 % of the target machine with VAAPI (1.5 cores, 1.9 GB), 8 in software (60 %). Cost is linear, so half the machine stays free for the rest.
  • YOLO is not the limiting factor: the application stays under 0.6 core even in stress at 12 cameras (about 105 ms per image on one core).
  • Memory is about 150 MB per camera plus about 0.3 GB of base (PostgreSQL, ReductStore, the application).
  • On the real machine, once VAAPI was enabled in the container, the application's CPU fell from 85-90 % of a core to about 36 % (41 to 49 % over the 48 h watch with every service running).

Limits: identical synthetic streams (real ones may cost more: 5 megapixels, some H.265 profiles not decoded by Skylake VAAPI, variable bitrate); no web, Zigbee, Grafana or MQTT traffic during the run; live WebRTC to browsers not measured (it depends on viewers; MediaMTX does not re-encode).

Redo it:

make fetch-model && cargo leptos build --release
python3 tools/bench-video.py --bin target/release/dominet --site target/site --model models/yolov8n.onnx \
  --bus crates/dominet-surveillance/fixtures/yolo/bus.jpg --workdir /tmp/bench --counts 1,4,8,12 --seconds 60

Use --nice 19 on a shared machine and FFMPEG_HWACCEL=off for the software series.

docs.title: Raspberry Pi 5 (2026-11-23)
docs.text:
Same tool and protocol, on a Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB, NVMe SSD, Debian 13 arm64, 4 cores), image 1.0.2, software decoding only (FFMPEG_HWACCEL=off: the Pi has no usable hardware decoder), 60 s measured per point, --nice 10, the installed stack idle next to the test. "Machine" is the share of the four cores in use.

Scenario Cameras Cores Memory (MB) Machine busy Decode only 1 0.23 311 8 % Decode only 2 0.44 434 14 % Decode only 4 0.84 683 25 % Decode only 6 1.30 943 36 % Full 1 0.26 434 9 % Full 2 0.50 578 17 % Full 4 1.00 846 27 % Full 6 1.48 1 146 40 %

What it says:

  • A camera costs about 0.22 core decoding only and 0.25 core in full mode (recording, indexing, motion, YOLO), almost all of it the decoding ffmpeg; the application itself stays at 0.17 core with 6 cameras. The cost is linear over the measured range, and no frame was dropped (no fallback in any run).
  • 6 cameras in 1080p fill 40 % of the machine in full mode, using about 1.1 GB of memory (about 140 MB per camera plus 0.3 GB of base).
  • Extending the line suggests that around 10 cameras would leave the Pi a margin of about 30 %. This is an extrapolation: nothing above 6 cameras was measured, and the synthetic streams are lighter than real ones (see the limits above). Do not plan on more than 6 to 8 cameras before measuring with yours.

Stack at rest (machine card, after a few minutes idle, ten services): about 310 MiB for the containers (zigbee2mqtt 87, PostgreSQL 70, Grafana 58, Prometheus 31, the application 28, MediaMTX 15, nginx 8, ReductStore 7, discovery 7, Mosquitto 3) and under 2 % of one core in total; the whole machine uses 1.1 GB of its 8 GB, at 48 °C. The interface answers in 9 to 10 ms (median) and 11 ms (95th percentile). A backup of the nearly empty database takes under a second: it says nothing about a database that has run for months.

Start from cold: make prod-down takes about 14 s and make prod-up 22 to 24 s until every service reports healthy (images already present).

Not measured on the Pi: the stress scenario (YOLO six times as often), live viewers (WebRTC), the other services under load, a backup of a database of realistic size.

docs.title: 3. MQTT and WebSocket load (phase R8)
docs.text:
Measured on the development machine, never on production.

  • MQTT: cargo test -p dominet-server --test throughput: 50 devices, 2 000 messages/s sustained for 5 s against the development Mosquitto, no final state lost, publication refused cleanly (never blocked) when the client is saturated. 7 s.
  • WebSocket: cargo test --release -p dominet --test ws_load -- --nocapture (variables WS_LOAD_USERS, WS_LOAD_RATE, WS_LOAD_MESSAGES, WS_LOAD_P99_MS).
Clients Rate States delivered Latency p50 / p99 / max Process memory 200 (25 accounts × 8) 200 /s 120 000 / 120 000 4 / 13 / 15 ms 15 to 78 MB 1 000 (125 accounts × 8) 100 /s 600 000 / 600 000 79 / 108 / 128 ms 15 to 315 MB

The memory includes the 1 000 test clients living in the same process. A debug build is about 100 times slower (p99 of 1.1 s with 200 clients): the default bound of the test accounts for it. A household has a handful of open browsers, far below these loads. Mosquitto drops messages beyond 1 000 queued per client unless max_queued_messages is raised (see the pitfalls page).

docs.title: 4. Production watch (phase R8, 48 hours)
docs.text: 13 services healthy, no automatic restart, no alert, all backups present. Memory 2.6 to 2.9 GB, load 1.3 to 3, database 58 MB growing by about 60 to 70 MB a day (about 3 readings per second). Solar-event automations ran at the computed time with the site's coordinates. 863 Rust tests and 29 E2E scripts (783 checks) on the image at the time.

docs.title: 5. Local assistant (phase R12)
docs.text:
Machine: development, llama.cpp b12078 with CUDA 12, context 16 384, temperature 0, reasoning disabled. Thresholds: a daily action card under 8 s, a configuration step under 30 s.

Model Mode Generation (tok/s) Action card, median (s) Right tool Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M GPU 16.2 1.8 96 % Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M CPU 3.6 8.3 100 % Qwen3-14B Q4_K_M GPU 3.9 7.4 92 % Qwen3-4B Instruct Q4_K_M GPU 67.7 0.4 76 % Qwen3-30B-A3B Instruct Q4_K_M GPU 21.2 1.2 80 % (failed the spike)

End-to-end evaluation, 50 requests played through the real agent loop and tools against a test database with three deliberately confusing device names: Qwen3-8B 49 of 50 (98 %) in 237 s, Qwen3-14B 48 of 50 (96 %) in 783 s, no wrong card in either (threshold: 85 % and zero wrong card). The 8B is about three times faster for the same quality, so a single model was kept. The set is now 51 requests (49 pass). It is played with cargo test -p dominet-agent --test eval -- --ignored against a running llama-server (variables AGENT_LIVE_URL, AGENT_LIVE_MODEL, AGENT_EVAL_OUT); raw results are in docs/bench/.

docs.title: 6. Build and test times
docs.text:
• make ci (format, lints, tests, WASM, deny, audit): about 4 min when warm; the pre-push hook replays it on a clean copy of the pushed commit in about 16 min (956 to 1 029 s over recent pushes).
  • Tests are bounded to 8 threads; at 20 threads PoolTimedOut appears about one run in three.
  • Release WASM about 3 MB; development WASM 48 MB. Image about 713 MB.
  • Disk on the target: the application's own growth is small (about 65 MB a day of history); video dominates, so size the recordings volume first.

docs.title: Internal messaging
docs.text:
R5 lot 5, ADR 0041 (model: ADR 0037, channels: ADR 0038, SMS: ADR 0039).

An administrator writes a message to accounts; it goes out by email, by SMS (through a connected Android phone) or both.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Address Who Content /messaging/compose administrators subject, message, channel (email / SMS / both), recipients: all active accounts, administrators, or chosen accounts /messaging administrators the 100 latest sent messages /messaging/inbox any account the 100 latest received messages, with your own email / SMS status /messaging/<id> sender, recipients, administrators the message; the sender and administrators see the full delivery table, a recipient only their own status

docs.title: How a message goes out
docs.text:
"Send" saves the message and opens its page right away; sending then runs in the background and statuses change live:

  1. Email: one message per recipient who has an address (subject = message subject, plain text). SMTP server: EMAIL_* variables; sender: the DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL setting.
  2. SMS: handed to the most recently seen online Android device. The status stays "pending" until the app acknowledges; with no acknowledgement after 60 s it turns into a failure.
  3. The message is "done" when nothing is pending any more. "Done" does not mean "everything succeeded": the table shows each failure with its reason (email: …, sms: aucun appareil Android connecte, sms: pas d'accuse de l'appareil…).

A recipient without an address (or without a mobile number) for the chosen channel is "not applicable" for that channel. The form flags these accounts and warns when no email server is configured or no phone is online.

docs.title: Rights and privacy
docs.text:
• Writing and listing sent messages: administrators only.
  • A message that does not exist and a message that does not concern you get the same answer: "not found".
  • Live follow: WebSocket topic message:<id>, same rights as the page.

docs.title: After a server stop
docs.text: A message left "in progress" by a hard stop is closed at restart: its pending sends are marked failed ("interrompu par un redemarrage du serveur"). Nothing restarts by itself; the sender can send again.

docs.title: Notable behaviors
docs.text:
• Asynchronous sending (the request does not wait).
  • SMS: 60 s delay.
  • Recipient without address or mobile: "not applicable".
  • Lists of 100 rows instead of pages of 20; no drafts.

docs.title: Moving to another machine
docs.text: One archive carries everything: the database, the video and history (ReductStore), and, encrypted with a passphrase, the keys and files you would otherwise lose. The old machine is only read (plus one normal backup); you decide when to switch over.

docs.title: What moves, and what does not
docs.text:
Moves Where it comes from Notes Accounts, devices, rules, automations, scenes, cameras, settings database backup same passwords: the hashes are restored History and archived video ReductStore backup --skip-reductstore leaves it out (large) .env and DOMINET_MASTER_KEY encrypted part without the key, stored camera passwords are unreadable The mkcert authority (key included) and the certificate encrypted part devices keep trusting the new machine, nothing to reinstall Zigbee2MQTT folder encrypted part the pairing is kept, no device to pair again MQTT accounts of your LAN clients encrypted part VPN keys, Grafana data encrypted part Grafana only with --with-grafana

Not moved: live recordings in progress (the recordings volume holds fragments not yet archived), container logs, and the Docker images themselves (the new machine pulls or builds them).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. On the old machine (stack running):

make prod-export OUT=/path/to/usb      # asks a passphrase twice

It runs one normal backup, copies the newest backups, gathers the files, encrypts the keys (AES-256, PBKDF2 600 000 rounds) and writes dominet-migration-<date>.tar with its .sha256. Keep the passphrase apart from the archive.

2. On the new machine: install the prerequisites (Docker, Compose, git, make, openssl, curl, mkcert for the authority), git clone the repository at a version at least as recent as the old one, copy the archive, then try without changing anything:

make prod-import FILE=/path/to/dominet-migration-….tar DRY=1

It checks the archive and the passphrase, shows what it contains, compares the architecture, the PostgreSQL major and the schema version, and lists what it would do.

3. Import for real:

make prod-import FILE=/path/to/dominet-migration-….tar

The importer writes the configuration (adapting the address, the Zigbee dongle port and hardware video to this machine), restores the authority and certificates (issuing a new certificate from the same authority if the address changed), starts the stack, restores the MQTT accounts, the database then ReductStore, applies the migrations the old machine did not have, restarts and checks. It refuses to overwrite an existing installation unless you add YES=1 (the old .env is then kept as .env.before-import-<date>).

Rehearsal on a second machine while the old one keeps running: use --no-zigbee (tools/migrate-pack.sh import FILE --no-zigbee). The archive carries the same Zigbee network as the old machine (same key, same identifiers): two coordinators with that identity on one LAN confuse the devices. Never plug the production dongle and a test dongle running that network at the same time. If the machine already holds a database volume of an earlier installation (even stopped), the importer refuses without --yes; with --yes it removes that volume and the project's containers first (their data is erased), because the old database keeps the old password.

4. Switch over. Point the name your devices use (LAN_DOMAIN, for example dominet.local) at the new machine: give it the old host name, or change the entry on your router. If you use a Zigbee dongle, move it, set ZIGBEE_DEVICE in .env if the importer did not find it, and make prod-up. Check with make prod-doctor.

docs.title: Between architectures and versions
docs.text:
• amd64 to arm64 (and back) is supported by the data formats: the database is a logical dump, ReductStore data files do not depend on the processor. Only the image differs, and the importer uses the one of the machine it runs on. This is untested on real arm64 hardware (see Supported machines).
  • The PostgreSQL major version must match (the importer refuses otherwise). A newer code than the archive is fine: missing migrations are applied. An older code than the archive is refused: update the repository first.

docs.title: Rehearsal
docs.text:
make check-migrate plays the whole procedure on two throw-away stacks on one machine: administrator, data, a ReductStore record, an MQTT account and Zigbee files are exported, the source is destroyed, a target imports, and everything is compared (accounts and password hashes, rows, record, keys, authority, certificate signature, accounts, files). It also checks the refusals (wrong passphrase, damaged archive, existing installation, dry run). Stop the development stack first (make dev-down), restart it after (make dev-up).

Before relying on a move, rehearse it with your own data: old machine → new machine, in dry-run mode, then for real on the new one while the old one keeps running; only then switch the name over.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The passphrase protects the keys against theft of the archive; it does not authenticate the archive against someone who can modify it. Keep it in your own custody.
  • The archive holds your data: video and history in clear. Encrypt the place where you store it.
  • A database restore replaces the target's data; there is no merge.

docs.title: MQTT
docs.text: The server's supervised MQTT client (R3). Decisions: ADR 0005 (choice of rumqttc) and ADR 0026 (behaviour), both in French.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: MQTT_HOST (required to enable the client), MQTT_PORT (1883), MQTT_USER, MQTT_PASSWORD, MQTT_CLIENT_ID (dominet): see configuration. The password never appears in logs.

docs.title: Broker (production Mosquitto)
docs.text:
A single listener, no anonymous access (ADR 0057). DomiNet and Zigbee2MQTT use the internal account (MQTT_USER / MQTT_PASSWORD). Each LAN client (Linky, an external SolarMax, Tasmota…) has its own account and rights: make prod-mqtt-user NAME=linky [TOPIC=linky/#] [ACCESS=read|write|readwrite] (generated password, shown once), make prod-mqtt-users, make prod-mqtt-del NAME=linky. No restart: connected clients are not cut. In the client: host LAN_DOMAIN, port 1883, user and password; it only writes under its own topic. A refusal shows in the Mosquitto log (not authorised).

Per-client queue: max_queued_messages 100000 (production and development). Mosquitto keeps only 1,000 by default and then drops the QoS 1 messages of a subscriber slower than the flow (log: Outgoing messages are being dropped for client …). DomiNet deliberately slows its reading when loaded: this queue absorbs the burst. Found on 2026-11-13: the throughput test lost the final states on a loaded machine.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
• dominet serve: web and the MQTT client when MQTT_HOST is set. dominet serve --only mqtt: the client alone. --only web: without MQTT.
  • Log: MQTT connecte / MQTT deconnecte, reconnexion en cours (one line per state change, not one per attempt).

docs.title: Behaviour to know
docs.text:
• Automatic reconnection (250 ms up to 5 s); all subscriptions are resumed on every connection.
  • A publication is refused immediately when the broker is unreachable (NotConnected): no queue of stale commands.
  • Subscriptions change live (MqttClient::set_subscriptions), without a restart.
  • Payloads are decoded as UTF-8 (else Latin-1), as JSON when possible, otherwise as text.

docs.title: Code
docs.text: crates/dominet-mqtt (start, MqttClient, topic_matches, decode_payload); crates/dominet-server/src/mqtt.rs (configuration adapter, role).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: cargo test -p dominet-mqtt: unit, then integration on the dev Mosquitto (make dev-up, port 11883, MQTT_TEST_PORT to change it) and on a throwaway Mosquitto for outages (Docker required, image eclipse-mosquitto:2.0): no accepted message is lost when the broker stops for 3 s and comes back, publications are refused during the outage, a broker that appears after the client is joined with the subscriptions already requested.

docs.title: Zigbee2MQTT device ingestion (lot 3, ADR 0027)
docs.text:
• The client subscribes to <prefix>/# (QoS 1). The prefix is the Z2M_BASE_TOPIC setting (zigbee2mqtt by default); changing it in Settings changes the subscription live.
  • <prefix>/bridge/devices: devices are created or updated (type inferred from exposes, hidden key update); <prefix>/bridge/info: permit_join; <prefix>/<name>/availability: availability; <prefix>/<name>: state (JSON object) that replaces the active device's state, updates last_seen, feeds the tracked-key history and is broadcast live (topic device:<id>, last state kept). bridge/…, …/set, …/get topics and non-JSON or non-object payloads are ignored.
  • <prefix>/bridge/logging: errors reported by Zigbee2MQTT (error level only). A published command always succeeds from the broker's point of view; if Zigbee2MQTT cannot deliver it (unreachable device, ZCL error), it says so here: Publish 'set' 'state' to 'Volet-salon' failed…. DomiNet writes the line to its log (warning "erreur signalee par Zigbee2MQTT", visible in /admin/logs and counted by make prod-report) and shows a banner to connected accounts; the same error is not shown again within 60 s. The automation or scene that sent the command still counts as successful: the error comes afterwards and Zigbee2MQTT does not say which command it belongs to.
  • At startup the last known state of every active device is republished to the widgets.
  • Messages that pile up (bursts) are processed in batches: a device's state is written at most once per second within a batch (the last one wins).

docs.title: Replay of recorded sessions
docs.text: tests/fixtures/z2m/session-r3.jsonl is a message session; its expected result session-r3.golden.json is a frozen reference file. The Rust tests (cargo test -p dominet-automation --test replay) replay the same session and require the same result — except for one documented deviation (ADR 0027: metadata written at creation). To add a case: extend the .jsonl file and the expected result in the .golden.json file, checking it by hand.

docs.title: MQTT sources, history and raw archive (lot 4, ADR 0028)
docs.text:
• Sources: administration page /admin/mqtt-sources (administrators). Each active source adds its filter (linky/#, solarmax/+/prod…) and QoS to the subscriptions; adding, editing or deleting one takes effect live, without a restart (a safety reload also happens every 60 s).
  • A message outside the Zigbee2MQTT prefix whose topic matches a source: logged if "Log messages" is set (topic and start of the payload); automatic device if that box is checked and the payload is a JSON object (name = topic without the source prefix, chosen type, state replaced, device reactivated if it was deactivated, broadcast live, recorded in the history); devices whose prefix/name is that topic are marked as seen. The source's handler code is a Rhai script run on every message (see scripts.md); Python code is refused when saving.
  • Tick "Automatic device" when creating the source. A device that publishes a retained message (Linky's report, for instance) only delivers it on subscription: if the box is ticked later, the message has already gone by and the device only appears at the next message or the next resubscription (dominet restart, broker reconnection).
  • History: PostgreSQL (device_state_log, one row per tracked key per second) feeds the charts; daily purge beyond HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS (400 days by default).
  • Raw archive: when REDUCTSTORE_URL is set, every message that writes a history row adds one record to the iot bucket (entry dev_<id>, body = full state, one label per numeric tracked key), FIFO quota IOT_QUOTA_GB (5 GB by default, applied when the bucket is created). It never slows ingestion down: bounded queue, batches of 50 written by a background task; ReductStore unreachable → records are dropped (warning in the log) and writing resumes on its own.
Variable Default Role HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS 400 maximum age of device_state_log rows IOT_QUOTA_GB 5 FIFO quota of the iot bucket (at creation) REDUCTSTORE_IOT_BUCKET iot bucket name (trials on a shared stack)

Tests: cargo test -p dominet-automation --test sources (sources and automatic devices), -p dominet-store --test reduct and -p dominet-server --test mqtt_role (ReductStore and dev broker), E2E mqtt (archive) and mqtt_sources (administration page).

docs.title: Replay of sources
docs.text: tests/fixtures/mqtt/sources-r3.jsonl (+ .golden.json) replays MQTT sources (automatic devices, logging, "seen" marking, reactivation, inactive sources): cargo test -p dominet-automation --test replay_sources. A single, deliberate deviation: the first message of an automatic device does not write its state (ADR 0028). Throughput: cargo test --release -p dominet-server --test throughput -- --nocapture.

docs.title: Notifications: sending channels
docs.text: Since R5 (lot 2, ADR 0038), DomiNet can send e-mails (SMTP) and Free Mobile SMS. The dominet-notify crate knows neither the database nor the UI; dominet_server::notify::Channels assembles it with the configuration.

docs.title: What is configured where
docs.text: What Where Key SMTP server, port, credentials, encryption environment (restart) EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT, EMAIL_HOST_USER, EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD, EMAIL_USE_TLS, EMAIL_USE_SSL, EMAIL_TIMEOUT_SECS Sender setting (immediate) DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL Alert recipient setting EMAIL_RECIPIENT (falls back to the sender) Free Mobile credentials settings (the key is encrypted at rest) SMS_FREE_USER, SMS_FREE_KEY Free Mobile API address environment SMS_FREE_URL (default: the official API)

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• EMAIL_USE_TLS (default): STARTTLS is mandatory, never a plaintext fallback; EMAIL_USE_SSL: TLS from the start (port 465). Both together are rejected. Without encryption, credentials are only allowed towards the loopback (otherwise the configuration is refused at startup).
  • The SMTP password and the Free Mobile key appear neither in Debug, nor in logs, nor in errors (the key travels in the HTTP address: reqwest errors are written without the address, and redirects are refused).
  • A line break in a subject is replaced by a space: no header injection.
  • Free Mobile's HTTP status is checked (400, 402, 403, 500 explained). The message is cut at 160 characters, 5 s timeout.

docs.title: Trying it for real: dominet notify-test
docs.text:
dominet notify-test --email            # to the alert recipient
dominet notify-test --email --to me@example.com
dominet notify-test --sms

This is the only command that really sends (besides alerts, automation notifications and messaging, which also really send as soon as SMTP is configured): it only runs when you ask. Tests, the demo and development talk to fake servers (dominet-notify, testing feature: FakeSmtp, FakeFreeMobile) and never leave the machine.

docs.title: Observability: metrics, alerts, Grafana dashboards
docs.text: DomiNet exposes its metrics to Prometheus, relays its alerts by e-mail and SMS, and ships the platform's Grafana dashboards. End-to-end setup: see deployment (R7 lot 5).

docs.title: Metrics (/metrics)
docs.text: A separate listener (METRICS_ADDR, default 0.0.0.0:9100, off to disable), never published on the host: only Prometheus reaches it, over the Docker network. The public port answers 404 on /metrics. Signals: HTTP requests (method, route, status, latency), WebSocket, MQTT, scheduled tasks (result, duration), recording segments, motions and detections, PostgreSQL pool, firing Prometheus alerts, version. Labels are bounded (normalised route, never the raw URL) and carry no secret. ADR 0051.

docs.title: Alert rules
docs.text: Edited in /admin/prometheus-rules and /admin/grafana-rules, written to provisioning files, services reloaded: see Prometheus and Grafana rules.

docs.title: Platform alerts in the interface
docs.text: The alerts page also shows, read-only, the alerts currently firing in Prometheus and Grafana (read every minute, ADR 0061) and the badge counts them. This is display only: e-mail and SMS delivery is still done by the relay below (Prometheus) and by Grafana's contact point.

docs.title: Prometheus alert relay
docs.text: With PROMETHEUS_URL, the scheduler role reads /api/v1/alerts every minute. A new firing alert sends an e-mail "[DomiNet] Alerte" (alert recipient) and, if critical, a Free Mobile SMS; it then stays quiet for 1 h (PROMETHEUS_ALERT_COOLDOWN). When it disappears, a "RESOLU" e-mail goes out (never an SMS). Each alert has its own identity (a single key for all would silence the second alert), and the "RESOLU" message actually goes out. ADR 0053.

docs.title: Grafana dashboards
docs.text: Seven generic dashboards in deploy/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/: overview (HTTP, tasks, database), automation and devices, surveillance (MediaMTX), camera detail (variable camera_uuid), weather (variable station), device history (variables device_id and key) and energy (see below). The first six are JSON files in the repository; the energy one is hand-written. Per-device dashboards are produced by the application (the device's "Grafana dashboard" option). Data sources postgresql and prometheus, contact point dominet-email (e-mail to EMAIL_RECIPIENT) and notification policy are in deploy/grafana/provisioning/.

docs.title: "DomiNet — Energy" dashboard
docs.text:
One dashboard (energy.json, 30 days by default) that mirrors the energy page: production of the day (qdy key), live power (production pac, Linky PAPP, heat pump power_ab), live net balance (production − Linky − heat pump), a per-day histogram (solar, Linky, heat pump, net balance as a line, read from energy_daily_log) and self-consumption.

  • Self-consumption = share of the solar production used by the house itself: min(production, Linky + heat pump) divided by production, in %. A day with no production has no rate (not 0 %). The "over the period" panel sums the days before dividing (it does not average the rates).
  • Devices are found by their state keys (pac, PAPP, power_ab, qdy), not by name: the ENERGY_*_DEVICE settings need not be copied into Grafana.
  • The "Live power" panel needs pac, PAPP and power_ab to be tracked in their devices' history (Devices page, tracked keys); dominet seed-energy adds them along with the daily-balance counters. Without them that panel stays empty, the rest of the dashboard works.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• cargo test -p dominet-server --test grafana_assets: every SQL query of the dashboards runs on the DomiNet schema, every cited metric exists (DomiNet or MediaMTX 1.21.3), and the self-consumption rate is computed correctly on known days.
  • tools/check-observability.sh: real throwaway Prometheus and Grafana (shifted ports, throwaway database) load rules, dashboards (seven), data sources, contact points and policies without error, run the energy dashboard's queries, and accept the reloads DomiNet asks for.

docs.title: Pitfalls and lessons
docs.text: Every trap met while building the application, by area. Each line says what you see, why it happens, what fixes it and, when there is one, what now guards against it. Read this before rebuilding or porting any part: none of these is obvious in advance and most were found by a test, a build of the image or the real machine, not by reading code.

docs.title: 1. Build and toolchain
docs.text: Symptom Cause Remedy / guard Buttons inert, no message in the browser The server and the WASM are not compiled alike. cargo leptos adds --cfg erase_components and LEPTOS_OUTPUT_NAME; a plain cargo build or cargo test does not, so the server HTML no longer matches the WASM and hydration fails Both settings live in .cargo/config.toml for every build (do not remove them). ui.rs checks the WASM name and the hydration markers; the E2E run on the image is the reference test E2E failures that make no sense Stale WASM or stale image: the interface or the image was not rebuilt Always cargo leptos build --release, then cargo build -p dominet before the E2E; make e2e-image does not rebuild, so run make image-smoke e2e-image make ci is green, the Docker image does not build The Dockerfile copies only crates/ and .sqlx/; an include_str! pointing outside crates/ compiles locally Nothing may be included from outside crates/; run make ci-full before a milestone or when the Dockerfile or a native dependency changes Image cannot link ONNX Runtime The prebuilt C++ library needs g++ at build time, libstdc++6 at run time and glibc 2.38 or newer Rebuild the image as soon as a native dependency is added Server panics at start when REDUCTSTORE_URL is set, only in the image The image has no root certificates; the rustls HTTP client panics when built The image installs ca-certificates; client construction no longer panics Image build fails randomly wasm-bindgen and wasm-opt are downloaded from a CDN The Dockerfile retries four times; otherwise run it again Risk of an unusable binary on the target machine Building with -C target-cpu=native ties the binary to the build machine's CPU (the target is a Skylake without AVX-512) Never publish with target-cpu=native; baseline is x86-64-v2 (ADR 0001) sqlx refuses a query sqlx 0.9 requires AssertSqlSafe for any dynamically built SQL Wrap dynamic SQL deliberately, never concatenate user input Offline compilation fails after adding a query The .sqlx/ metadata is out of date Any new sqlx::query! is followed by make sqlx-prepare; make sqlx-check guards it Clippy flags product names in doc comments clippy::doc_markdown Declare proper nouns in clippy.toml Dependencies drift into advisories A transitive crate gets a RUSTSEC entry (a mail crate did) cargo update -p <crate>; make ci runs cargo deny and cargo audit

docs.title: 2. Web interface (Leptos, server-side rendering)
docs.text:
• Page frozen after a cold start (Leptos 0.8.23): concurrent renders may never finish, in 1 to 5 % of cold starts. The "reactive value disposed" panics in the log are a consequence, not the cause. Guard: web/render_guard.rs abandons and retries a GET that gets no answer in 5 s (3 tries, then 503); reproducer tools/stress-cold-render.sh (ADR 0021).
  • Read a resource under Transition, otherwise server rendering does not wait for it. Render routes with SsrMode::Async.
  • No inline style= or on…= (content security policy). prop:value is not rendered on the server: use value= for the initial state and disabled= instead of prop:disabled.
  • No StoredValue::new_local in a component rendered on the server (a SendWrapper panic on release freezes the page).
  • No resource whose source depends on another resource (loads arrive out of order at hydration and the table is stale).
  • No curly braces in a .ftl file (panic while loading translations).
  • Read form fields through NodeRef and the input value, not signals: browser autofill fills fields without firing input.
  • Several Leptos apps rendered in parallel inside one test process disturb each other: ui.rs runs them one at a time under a lock.
  • Links in the navigation bar must be loaded by the browser, not by the in-app router, when the target is served by the server (/docs/, /grafana/): the router answers "page not found".
  • A required field in a form that is not needed for every case blocks creation (a Grafana widget could not be created because "device / scene / camera" were all required).
  • A tab left open during an update keeps the old front end and can show a badge without its list. /pkg/ is served no-cache with an ETag; a hard reload fixes it.
  • The development WASM is 48 MB (buttons inert for 10 to 30 s); use a release build for demos.

docs.title: 3. Authentication and sessions
docs.text:
• flush() alone does not renew the session identifier: use flush then cycle_id, or the session is fixed.
  • A stolen session could guess the current password without limit: apply the same lockout as the login.
  • Two administrators demoting each other at the same time left no administrator: an advisory lock serialises it (race test).
  • MCP tokens: hashed, scoped, with a mandatory end date, immediate revocation, rate limit; scopes are enforced in a single place.

docs.title: 4. Database and tests
docs.text:
• Creating throw-away databases (#[sqlx::test]) forces a checkpoint; at 20 test threads PoolTimedOut appears about one run in three. The test run is bounded to 8 threads (TEST_THREADS). The same PoolTimedOut appears on every database test when the development database is simply not running.
  • Race conditions found only by deliberate race tests: a default dashboard read before its lock, two concurrent widget insertions blocking on an exclusion constraint (take the row lock first).
  • pg_dump 17 against a PostgreSQL 16 server writes SET transaction_timeout, unknown to the server: drop that line when restoring without the tool.
  • A long task at start-up (resume jobs) must run in the background; waiting for the database before starting the HTTP server made the image smoke test fail when the database is unreachable.
  • A test must not assume an empty broker or an already loaded engine: engines reload their list in the background, so tests repeat the action until the first reaction.

docs.title: 5. MQTT and Zigbee
docs.text: Symptom Cause Remedy A remote-control press is lost Ingestion kept only the last state of a device received within one second; a remote sends action: 1_single then action: "" milliseconds apart Automations also see the grouped states (ADR 0032) Device missing after creating an MQTT source A retained message arrived before "automatic device" was ticked Tick it at creation; a retained device otherwise appears only on re-subscription Throughput test unstable under load Mosquitto drops messages beyond 1 000 queued per client max_queued_messages 100000 in development and production Anonymous access leaks to the secured listener Without per_listener_settings, allow_anonymous true applies everywhere Set per_listener_settings true; one password-protected listener, per-client accounts (ADR 0057) Pairing button does nothing Zigbee2MQTT 2.x rejects {"value": true} ("Invalid payload") Send {"time": 254} A device already paired elsewhere will not pair It remembers its old network Reset it first Renaming a device breaks its commands A device's friendly_name is also its MQTT topic Rename from the administration pages, knowing the topic changes Blind stops mid-movement impossible The relay has no moving key and no STOP state: its state derives from the position and it publishes about one message a second while moving Use the age of the last message (age_secs in scripts). Never write a script from a plugin's name A refusal message stays after the broker returns The notice was cleared only by user action It clears as soon as the device publishes a state Throw-away tests see old Zigbee messages The development broker keeps retained messages Per-test topic prefix and a redirected Z2M_BASE_TOPIC

docs.title: 6. Video and detection
docs.text:
• Software decoding in the container used 85 to 90 % of a core: the container had no /dev/dri, no render group and no driver. Fix: VAAPI (make prod-video), measured at 36 %.
  • The VAAPI fallback was triggered too eagerly by an offline camera. Only the real machine revealed it.
  • ReductStore 1.21 and later refuses an empty RS_API_TOKEN; its image has neither wget nor curl (health check through bash and /dev/tcp).
  • MediaMTX: the configuration schema changes between versions; revalidate on every upgrade. The ICE port (8189, UDP and TCP) is fixed, so only one stack at a time.
  • The password of a camera appears in clear in an ONVIF GetStreamUri answer: mask it everywhere.
  • Only one TCP client at a time on the solar inverter: a diagnostic read fails while the publisher role is running.
  • Test fixtures for ONVIF are rebuilt from captures; confront them with real cameras with the ignored real_onvif test.
  • An endurance script that waits for indexed segments but not archived ones races.

docs.title: 7. Domain logic
docs.text:
• float("1_000") is valid in Python and refused by Rust: the alert rule parser had to accept it (found by comparing with the reference implementation).
  • Times shown in UTC (…Z) in the automation list: the computation is right (solar events are absolute instants, schedules go through TZ, default Europe/Paris, with ambiguous and missing hours handled) but the display should be local.
  • Energy balance: truncation rather than rounding (int(1.005 × 1000)), daylight-saving nights, local-day edges, counter reset, days without data. These are covered by golden fixtures in tests/fixtures/energy.
  • Never copy a coordinate from an example file: weather and solar times were wrong for a whole installation because sample coordinates were kept.

docs.title: 8. Observability (Prometheus, Grafana)
docs.text:
• Grafana needs an SMTP sender address with a dot and a non-empty recipient, otherwise it restarts in a loop. A volume mounted :ro prevents nested mounts.
  • Grafana alert rules with NoData set to "no data" fire forever: "no result" means "all is well" for these rules. Default to OK; fix existing installations by hand.
  • 288 failed e-mails in 12 hours: a stale SMTP password (services not recreated after editing .env) and a recipient written =….
  • Compose interpolates variables of inactive profiles too: prod-guard checks them.
  • Prometheus must load every rule group; a count taken from the rules file is the right check (tools/check-observability.sh).
  • Platform alerts in /alerts read Prometheus GET /api/v1/alerts (state firing) and Grafana's alert manager API with basic authentication; the hub is in-process, so the poller lives in the web role (ADR 0061).
  • The energy dashboard finds devices by state keys (pac, qdy, PAPP, power_ab); those keys must be tracked in the device history, which dominet seed-energy now does.

docs.title: 9. Production and operations
docs.text: Symptom Cause Remedy prod-deploy stops before any build Compose 5.6 delegates to buildx bake, which rejects network: host in build Remove the line Firefox refuses the certificate, Brave accepts it Firefox has its own certificate store Import the CA by hand (or security.enterprise_roots.enabled); libnss3-tools for mkcert -install E-mails sent to =address Double = in .env (NAME==value) prod-guard reports it Changed .env, nothing changes The service was not recreated Recreate the services after any .env change make prod-logs blocks with grep It follows continuously N=100 for the last lines without following Disk full on the production machine A 370 GB target/ and a 73 GB build cache left on it Never build on the production machine Push fails for the 7-minute hook GitHub drops the connection during the hook ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 The pre-push hook fails on MQTT tests It uses the development stack, which was stopped make dev-up first Backup summary showed no PostgreSQL backups It kept the 4 latest lines, all kinds mixed Two per kind Login button inert in one browser Interface did not start in the tab; cause never identified Clear the cache or disable the browser's shields

docs.title: 10. End-to-end tests
docs.text:
• A click before hydration "succeeds" and does nothing: wait for the real-time indicator or repeat the click until the form opens (met four times).
  • The simulated SMTP server is shared by the scripts: filter on your own subject. The E2E server remembers the last device state: give each script its own device number.
  • Two scripts run together can interfere (alerts with platform_alerts: the fake Prometheus is counted in the badge). Run them separately.
  • Two unexplained flaky steps, never reproduced: the memory bar width in system and the publish solarmax diagnostic. Note, do not hide.
  • Run make ci often: a break in the interface tests (truncated translations) was seen only at the end of a lot.

docs.title: 11. MCP and the local assistant
docs.text:
• A script reaches the application through the back door: save_automation and save_mqtt_source accept script code, so a configuration token could write scripts. Rule: any config_upsert whose payload contains a script requires the administration scope.
  • Server functions answered "internal error" or "access denied", fine for a browser, poor for an assistant: tools pass the per-field validation error through unchanged.
  • Audit is written before execution and the call is refused if the audit cannot be written.
  • dry_run on every action, including device commands and scenes.
  • The assistant gets an actor (token scopes or user session), not just an account.
  • The model never executes a change. It proposes an action card; the user confirms with a click; a snapshot is taken first and the change can be rolled back.
  • A small model (Qwen3-8B) sometimes asks permission to continue ("do you want to continue?", "we must first…") instead of calling the tool: a guard re-prompts once. It cannot reliably modify or rename an existing element; do that from the administration pages. The measured 14B model was not better (96 % against 98 %), so a single model was kept.
  • An integer id placed in the data instead of the id parameter must be moved by the tool.
  • Treat everything read through tools as data, never as instructions (injection test with the real model).
  • Evaluation set of 51 requests: 49 pass, none produces a wrong card (the two failures ask nothing and produce no card).

docs.title: 12. Method
docs.text:
• The real machine finds what no development test can see: decoding on the CPU, coordinates, certificates, mail, disk. Plan a rehearsal on real hardware.
  • Count what you ship: put the number in the test (cases compared, scenes, rules) so a silent shrink is visible.
  • A feature that is unreliable with the chosen model should be removed rather than hidden: the assistant's rename feature was dropped.
  • A decision that is not obvious gets an ADR, with the options rejected.

docs.title: Prometheus and Grafana alert rules
docs.text: Two administration pages (administrators only): Prometheus rules (/admin/prometheus-rules) and Grafana rules (/admin/grafana-rules). Rules live in the database; each change rewrites the provisioning file (rules.yml for Prometheus, rules.yaml for Grafana) and asks the service to read it again. These rules watch the platform (application, MQTT, MediaMTX…); rules on device state are elsewhere (/admin/alert-rules, see alerts).

docs.title: Shipped rules
docs.text: dominet seed creates the default rules, written for DomiNet metrics (/metrics, ADR 0051): failing scheduled tasks, application down, 5xx errors, p95 latency, MQTT disconnected, MediaMTX down or without streams; on the Grafana side: heat wave (SQL on device), application and MediaMTX down, 5xx errors. They are created only in an empty table: a deleted rule does not come back.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
