  • Empty value = stored empty, unencrypted (nothing to protect); this allows clearing a secret without the master key.
  • No read-back: the API returns ******** for a set secret; a secret is write-only. Values are never logged (only the setting name is).
  • In-memory cache of decrypted values for internal use (sending SMS, etc.); it disappears with the process.
  • Write refused without a master key (explicit 503) rather than saved in clear. seed checks everything before writing: an error writes nothing.
  • The key is validated at start-up (Config): a key of the wrong length stops the server with a clear message.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Losing the master key makes the secrets unrecoverable (they must be entered again). It must be backed up separately from the database. Changing the key makes existing secrets unreadable; they are flagged (readable = false, 503 on use) and the other settings keep working.
  • No automatic rotation: to change the key, read the secrets with the old one then rewrite them with the new one (a tool to add if the need appears).
  • Encryption protects the database at rest; an attacker who controls the server process (and so the key in memory) is not covered.
  • The same mechanism serves camera passwords.

docs.title: 0012 — Interface: Leptos server functions and a three-crate split
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The front end is server-rendered then hydrated in WASM (ADR 0007). Two decisions are needed: (1) how pages talk to the server and (2) how to organise the crates, knowing that Leptos server functions must exist in the crate compiled for the browser (to provide the client stub) while running server code (state, database, session).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. The browser calls the JSON /api/* API with fetch. One contract for all clients, but server-side rendering still has to fetch its data another way (calling the API from itself, or server functions).
  2. Leptos server functions (#[server]): typed end to end, the same code serves server rendering and the browser, the session and application state are directly available. The JSON API stays for the Android app, scripts and tests.
  3. Split: (a) everything in dominet-server (dependency cycle with the interface), (b) dominet-server as a library, dominet-web for the interface (depends on the server under ssr), dominet for the binary — chosen.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Server functions for the interface, prefix /sf/… (outside /api, so as not to confuse the two contracts). The JSON API /api/* is kept and tested.
  • Three crates: dominet-server (library: config, state, auth, settings, API, CLI), dominet-web (components, pages, server functions, i18n; ssr feature on the server, hydrate on the WASM side) and dominet (thin binary: assembles both). There is thus no circular dependency, and dominet-web can use CurrentUser, AppState, etc.
  • Mounting: dominet-web::ssr::ui_service produces an Axum service (pages, server functions, /pkg files) mounted as the main router's fallback_service. The middlewares (session, origin check, security headers, request id) wrap it like the API; a server function is protected against CSRF like any POST.
  • State in server functions: AppState is provided through the Leptos context; authentication goes through the same extractors as the API (CurrentUser, RequireAdmin) via leptos_axum::extract_with_state.
  • Configuration: LeptosOptions is built by the code (SITE_ROOT, listen address), without LEPTOS_* variables. No hot reload: make front then restart.
  • Build: cargo leptos build from the root ([[workspace.metadata.leptos]]).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A business rule used by both the interface and the API lives in the service layer (already the case: AuthService, SettingsService); JSON routes and server functions are thin wrappers.
  • Server functions are not a public contract: they evolve with the interface. Any third-party client goes through /api.
  • Integration tests of the whole router are in the dominet crate (tests/ui.rs); hydration is checked in a real browser (tests/e2e/).
  • Licences/advisories: BSL-1.0 (xxhash-rust) allowed; the "unmaintained" advisory on paste (a Leptos compile-time macro) is explicitly ignored in deny.toml, to reexamine at every Leptos upgrade.

docs.title: Pitfalls found
docs.text:
• #[server] needs explicit prefix and endpoint for stable URLs; accents in page texts are encoded as UTF-8 in the rendered HTML.
  • The WASM file is loaded before being instantiated: a test that clicks right away loses the first click; wait until a click is taken into account before counting.
  • An integration test rendering Leptos blocked once in the full suite without being reproducible (40 runs afterwards, 60 simultaneous requests on the real server without problem): tests now have a 20 s timeout per request.

docs.title: 0013 — CI on a self-hosted runner
docs.text:
• Status: accepted, then partly replaced by ADR 0015 (CI is no longer automatic: local pre-push gate). The runner design is kept here as history; the public repository has no CI workflow and no runner scripts.
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: CI on GitHub's machines was slow (cold runs of several tens of minutes, caches to restore/export, a Docker image rebuilt without layers) and subject to a minute quota (about 2,000 a month on a private repository, free plan). The developer wanted fast CI without a quota. The same checks already run locally (make ci).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. GitHub machines (status quo) — no maintenance, but slow, capped, and remote caches to manage.
  2. Self-hosted runner on the development machine, without isolation (the machine's Docker, the developer's account) — fast, but a compromised workflow or third-party action would have root-equivalent access (docker group) on the production server.
  3. Self-hosted runner, isolated (dedicated user without sudo, rootless Docker, capped resources) — chosen at the time.
  4. Another dedicated server — better separation from production; still possible later (same install script).
  5. No remote CI, make ci alone — fast and free, but no check on a clean machine and no per-commit trace.

docs.title: Decision (at the time)
docs.text:
• Option 3, this private repository only. The install script set everything up idempotently: a locked gha-runner user outside the sudo/docker groups, rootless Docker for it alone, Rust and tools installed once, runner verified by SHA-256, a user systemd service with automatic restart, weekly Docker cache cleanup.
  • Resource caps on everything the runner launched: CPU weight 20, memory 4 GB "high" and 5 GB maximum.
  • The workflow ran make ci: a single CI definition, identical locally and on the runner; no third-party action (only the official actions/checkout). The test database was a throw-away PostgreSQL container per job.
  • Caches on the runner: a persistent Cargo target, Docker layers of the rootless Docker, pre-installed tools.
  • Guard: pull requests from a fork do not run on this runner. No fallback to GitHub's machines.
  • The emulated arm64 job was removed (slow and greedy); to resume with a native arm64 runner.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• CI became fast (warm caches: a few minutes) and no longer used GitHub minutes.
  • It shared the machine with everything else; the runner was throttled, but a full build remained a load peak.
  • A runner executes repository code: never use it for a public repository or fork PRs, never store secrets on it.
  • Superseded in practice by ADR 0015.

docs.title: 0014 — Generic CRUD component for administration pages
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A generated administration site typically provides about 30 CRUD screens. The first phase replaces four (places, navigation, settings, users) and the following phases add cameras, devices, scenes, etc. Writing each screen by hand would multiply interface code, error cases and translations.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. A generic component driven by a field description (FieldSpec), and concrete server functions per resource — chosen.
  2. Everything generic, server side included (a "save any resource" server function with textual values) — less code, but validation and rights would go through a weakly typed contract, and the target table becomes data sent by the browser.
  3. A hand-written page per resource — simplest to read, longest to maintain.
  4. A derive macro generating page and server functions — elegant, but costly to write and debug for 4 resources.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• crud.rs: CrudTable (filterable table, add/edit form, in-place deletion confirmation, per-field errors). A page supplies the FieldSpecs (name, translation key, type text / text area / checkbox, mandatory, maximum length, table column), the list (Signal<Vec<Row>>) and two Actions (save, delete) that call its server functions. The component knows neither the business type nor the network.
  • Server functions stay concrete and typed per resource. Each starts with require_admin (403 otherwise): page guards only serve display. Expected refusals are values (SaveOutcome::{Saved, Invalid, NotFound}, DeleteOutcome::{Deleted, NotFound, InUse}), not HTTP errors; only failures are errors (logged).
  • Validation is authoritative on the server and reports field by field (FieldProblem { field, kind }) so the interface translates the message under the right field. The domain carries the rule (LocationDraft::problems), validate stays for the API.
  • Labels are keys (tk!("key"), resolved by I18n::tr at display time to follow the language). tk! makes the key findable: tests/i18n.rs checks that it exists in both languages and that no key is orphaned.
  • Displayed content is always escaped by Leptos (test with <script> in a name).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Current field types: text, text area, checkbox, bounded number, drop-down list, password, display-only column and a field that cannot be changed after creation. A Blocked result expresses a business refusal (neither an error nor an invalid field). Settings (fixed keys, typed values, secrets) are not CRUD: a dedicated page on the same typed server functions.
  • A new simple resource = a field description, three server functions, a page of about fifty lines.
  • Resources with relations, secret fields or business rules (last administrator) add field types or result variants; the component evolves with real needs.
  • No duplicated REST API for these screens: the interface goes through server functions (ADR 0012).

docs.title: 0015 — Local gate (pre-push hook) instead of automatic CI
docs.text:
• Status: accepted — replaces the "automatic CI on a runner" part of ADR 0013
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0013 moved CI to a self-hosted runner on the development machine (free, no quota). But the workflow only reruns make ci (plus the interface build and an image test), which the developer already runs before every commit on the same machine, which is also the development and production server. Real cost: 8 to 10 minutes per push, a dedicated system user, rootless Docker, resource ceilings to maintain, and a recent failure (red) impossible to read or reproduce without access to the GitHub API. For a one-developer project, a per-commit trace brings nothing.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. Keep automatic CI (ADR 0013) — conventional, but slow, heavy and redundant here.
  2. Nothing but make ci by hand — simplest, but does not catch a file forgotten in git add (everything compiles in the working tree, nothing is checked on what will really be pushed).
  3. pre-push hook: make ci on a clean copy of the pushed commit — chosen.
  4. GitHub CI triggered on demand only — see Decision.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• .githooks/pre-push (enabled by make hooks, which sets core.hooksPath) extracts each pushed tip commit with git archive (so without untracked files or uncommitted changes), starts a throw-away PostgreSQL (postgres:16-alpine, random port, removed at the end) and runs make ci at low CPU priority (nice). On failure nothing is pushed; the last 60 lines and the log path are shown.
  • A dedicated Cargo target (target/prepush) does not interfere with the build in progress; the first run is longer.
  • make ci-full = make ci + make front + make image-smoke (interface build and Docker image), to run before a milestone and when the Dockerfile or the build chain changes. DOMINET_PREPUSH_CMD='make ci-full' git push applies it to the push.
  • Bypass: git push --no-verify or DOMINET_SKIP_PREPUSH=1. It is a safeguard, not a barrier: a local hook does not protect against a deliberate bypass.
  • The public repository keeps no GitHub workflow; the gate is make ci, run locally and by the hook.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A push takes the time of make ci on a clean copy (a few minutes, less when warm) instead of 8 to 10 remote minutes.
  • Tests run against a throw-away PostgreSQL only: never a real Mosquitto, cameras or Zigbee dongle. They only consume CPU (nice).
  • No CI status on GitHub: the proof that a commit passed the checks is that it could be pushed. If the project gains contributors, going back to automatic CI (ADR 0013, or GitHub-hosted machines) becomes relevant again.

docs.title: 0016 — Nonce-based CSP and the base WebSocket hub
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Hardening the server integration of the interface (static files, content security policy) and laying the base of the real-time channel (/ws/notifications/) that later work (devices, cameras, Android) extends.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
CSP 1. A <meta http-equiv> tag set by leptos_meta (the method documented by Leptos) — ignores frame-ancestors, report-uri and sandbox. 2. A header set by a middleware with its own nonce — impossible: Leptos generates its scripts' nonce during rendering and does not allow imposing one (the field is private). 3. A header set during rendering by the root component, which reads Leptos's nonce (use_nonce) and inserts the header into ResponseOptions — chosen. 4. 'unsafe-inline' — refused: it cancels the point of the CSP.

Real time 1. SSE or long polling — no bidirectional channel, and the Android contract is WebSocket. 2. Axum WebSocket + a tokio::sync::broadcast hub per topic — chosen. 3. An external bus (Redis) — removed from the project.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• CSP: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'. A different nonce on every response. No inline style nor on…= handler: the only style= (the sidebar reopening button) became a class. A test sweeps all pages (same nonce in header and scripts, no forbidden attribute); the end-to-end test checks in Firefox that an injected script without a nonce is blocked and that the WebSocket works despite the policy. The frame-src (Grafana) and media-src/connect-src (camera streams) directives are added with the functions concerned.
  • Static files: /pkg/* with Cache-Control: no-cache (revalidate at every load, 304 answer) — file names do not change between versions, and a stale WASM with a fresh JS would break hydration; hash-based naming (hash-files) would allow a long cache, a possible improvement. Pages and server functions in no-store (private, no history). gzip compression (WASM loses ~70 %). Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin.
  • Hub (hub.rs): topics created on demand, a broadcast of 64 messages, a too-slow subscriber loses messages (logged) without blocking emitters; a topic is removed without subscribers; at most 8 simultaneous connections per account.
  • /ws/notifications/: a session is mandatory (401 otherwise, before opening the WebSocket); the Origin header is checked as for unsafe requests (browsers do not apply the same-origin policy to WebSockets: without it a third-party page could open the connection with the user's cookie); browser messages limited to 1 KiB. Heartbeat (WS_HEARTBEAT_SECS, 25 s by default): a server ping, a pong expected before the next (otherwise close 4408); at every heartbeat the session is revalidated (it exists, the account is active, its password has not changed) otherwise close 4401: logout, deactivation, deletion or reset also cut real time, at most one heartbeat later.
  • WASM client (realtime.rs): open as long as an account is signed in; reconnection with a doubling delay (1 s to 30 s, +25 % random); 4401 stops the attempts; a state indicator in the sidebar; notifications shown as text only.
  • Broadcast: an administrator-only server function (broadcast_notification, Settings page): useful in itself and the only way to check the chain end to end.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Message format (WsServerMsg / WsClientMsg, type tag) in dominet-proto: this is the contract to extend (device_state…). The /ws/devices/, /ws/surveillance/… and /ws/android/… routes are other routes on the same hub; the Android app's token authentication replaces the session for /ws/android/device/{token}/.
  • The hub lives in the memory of a single process (consistent with single-server deployment); spreading over several instances would need an external bus.
  • Per-heartbeat revalidation has a cost (two database reads per connection per heartbeat), acceptable at this scale; a revocation event pushed by the hub could replace it later.
  • A strict policy means no more inline style=/on…= and no third-party resources without changing the CSP.

docs.title: 0017 — Docker image with cargo-leptos and end-to-end tests on the image
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Until this point the image only held the server binary (no WASM/JS/CSS files: pages rendered but did not hydrate). A complete image is now needed. A defect met at the end of the previous work imposes a requirement too: the server (rendered HTML) and the WASM (hydration) must be compiled the same way, otherwise the interface displays but stays inert (disabled buttons, no message); neither clippy nor the Rust tests see it.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. cargo leptos build --release in the image, with cargo-chef to cache dependencies (server and WASM) — chosen.
  2. Build the WASM outside the image (development machine) and copy it — not reproducible, machine dependent.
  3. File-name hashing (hash-files) for a long cache — discarded for now: the fingerprint file must sit next to the binary, which adds one more dependency between development binary, cargo leptos and image (the class of defect just fixed); /pkg/* stays no-cache (revalidation, a few-byte 304).
  4. arm64 — see Decision.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Dockerfile: cargo-leptos 0.3.11 (pinned) and cargo-chef installed in a base layer; two cargo chef cook (server, and WASM with the same target, the same wasm-release profile and the same target/front folder as cargo leptos build --release); cargo leptos build --release produces the binary and target/site; the final image (Debian slim, user 10001) contains /usr/local/bin/dominet and /app/site (SITE_ROOT). .cargo/config.toml is copied from the first stage: it carries the settings common to server and WASM. cargo-leptos downloads wasm-bindgen (version of Cargo.lock) and wasm-opt during the build: network needed. Result: a 1.3 MB WASM (20 MB in development), a 137 MB image.
  • Smoke test (ci/image-smoke.sh): health, /readyz without a database, non-root, clean stop, and /login (200, nonce CSP, expected WASM file, hydration markers), /pkg/* (200, application/wasm, gzip, no-cache, plausible size).
  • End-to-end tests on the image (tools/e2e.sh --image, make e2e-image): a container on the host network, a throw-away database created then dropped, headless Firefox with a temporary profile, the scripts of tests/e2e/. It is the only test that hydrates the page with the production binary and WASM; verified by forcing a failure (exit code 1, "Interactive interface: 0 click") when static files are missing. The same launcher without --image serves the development binary (make e2e).
  • make ci-full = make ci + image-smoke + e2e-image, to run before a milestone and when the Dockerfile or the build chain changes (DOMINET_PREPUSH_CMD='make ci-full' git push applies it to a push). make ci stays the ordinary gate (ADR 0015).
  • arm64 not built. The development machine has no emulation (exec format error) and configuring binfmt/QEMU needs root; it is a non-blocking point until a Raspberry Pi 5 is targeted. To resume with a native arm64 machine: the Dockerfile has no architecture dependency, only the downloaded wasm-bindgen/wasm-opt versions must exist for aarch64.
  • No HEALTHCHECK in the image (the slim image has no curl): the /healthz probe is declared in the production docker-compose.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A change to the Dockerfile, .cargo/config.toml, Cargo.toml (profiles, Leptos metadata) or tool versions is validated with make ci-full.
  • A long cold first build (cargo-leptos, server and WASM dependencies); afterwards only project code is rebuilt: a one-line change rebuilds the image in about 2 min 30 (measured).
  • Tools downloaded during the build (wasm-bindgen, wasm-opt) are a network dependency of the build; an internal base image or a cache of these binaries could replace them.

docs.title: 0018 — Dashboard schema: overlap exclusion and references without foreign keys
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: dashboard and widget are introduced. Two difficulties: (1) two widgets of the same dashboard must never overlap, even when two moves arrive at the same time; (2) a widget designates a device, a scene or a camera, tables that do not exist yet.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Overlap. (a) Check in Rust before writing — not atomic: two simultaneous requests both pass. (b) An application lock alone — correct but does not prevent other code (CLI, migration, hand-written SQL) from breaking the invariant. (c) A PostgreSQL exclusion constraint (EXCLUDE USING gist, btree_gist extension) — the invariant lives in the database — chosen.

References. (a) Create minimal device/scene/camera tables now — encroaches on later work and freezes a schema not yet known. (b) Columns without a foreign key (device_id, scene_id integers, camera_uuid UUID), the key being added by the migration that creates the target table — chosen. (c) Store references in the config JSON — loses integrity and queries.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• A 12-column grid; grid_col, grid_row, width, height (col/row are tricky words in SQL), all bounded by CHECKs (grid_col + width <= 12). A widget's rectangle is a box(point(col, row), point(col + width - 1, row + height - 1)) in cell coordinates, bounds included: contiguous widgets pass, an overlap is refused (widget_no_overlap, SQLSTATE 23P01, reported by the repository as RepoError::Conflict). Tested on the database (constraints) and on the repositories (races).
  • Widget writes serialised per dashboard: the repository takes a row lock on the dashboard before inserting, modifying or moving. Without it, two simultaneous insertions on the same cells block each other in the constraint check (deadlock detected, documented PostgreSQL behaviour) instead of being cleanly refused; a race test (6 concurrent insertions, 10 rounds) brought it to light.
  • Default dashboard: a partial unique index (WHERE is_default) = at most one per owner. The repository takes a lock on the owner's row, rereads the state after the lock (a read before it gave a stale value: the race revealed it), and moves the status from one dashboard to another in the same transaction. An account's first dashboard is its default; the status is not removed directly, it passes to another dashboard.
  • Cascade deletion: user → dashboards → widgets.
  • presentation (text, '' = automatic), config (a JSON object of at most 4 KB) and content (HTML of the text widget, at most 20,000 characters) are bounded in the database and validated by the domain (WidgetDraft::problems, per field): consistency of type / presentation / references, Grafana configuration (panel_url http(s), or dashboard_uid + panel_id, or key with a device).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The production database must be able to run CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist (a "trusted" extension since PostgreSQL 13, included in the postgres:16 image).
  • Later migrations add the foreign keys widget.device_id, widget.scene_id, widget.camera_uuid (ON DELETE SET NULL) and handle possible orphan references.
  • A widget whose target disappeared keeps a reference to nothing while the key does not exist: the interface shows "source unavailable".
  • HTML content is not sanitised by the repository: sanitising (ammonia) is done at save time, on the server.

docs.title: 0019 — Multiplexed WebSocket protocol: typed topics, last state kept
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A base WebSocket hub exists (ADR 0016): one connection per tab, a single topic (notifications), messages broadcast to all. Device state must now flow through it (then system statistics, cameras…): the dashboard follows dozens of devices, each interesting only the tabs that display it. A tab that subscribes must also receive the current state at once, without waiting for the device's next message (which may never come for a quiet sensor).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Connections. (a) One WebSocket connection per topic — multiplies connections (limit of 8 per account) and heartbeats. (b) One multiplexed connection, the client subscribing and unsubscribing by message — chosen.

Topics. (a) Free strings — a typo becomes a phantom topic. (b) A Topic type in dominet-proto (Notifications, System, Device(i64), Camera(Uuid)), with a strict canonical text form (device:7, never device:07 nor device:+7) — chosen: server and browser share the same type, an invalid topic is refused at parsing.

Initial state. (a) The client queries a REST API on subscription — two paths to keep consistent, and a race window between the answer and the first message. (b) The hub keeps the last message of each topic ("retained", as in MQTT) and sends it after Subscribed — chosen.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Client → server messages: subscribe {topic}, unsubscribe {topic}. Server → client: subscribed {topic}, refused {topic, reason} with reason ∈ invalid (unreadable topic), forbidden (insufficient right), limit (128 subscriptions per connection), then the topic's messages (device_state, notification, …), in a flat {"type": …} format.
  • Authorisation per topic (authorize in web/ws.rs): any signed-in account reads notifications, system and device:*; camera:* is decided with the camera table. The notifications subscription is automatic and cannot be removed.
  • Last state: Hub::publish_retained records the message before broadcasting it, so a subscriber arriving during the publication receives the snapshot or the message, never neither. Memory is bounded by the number of devices; bursts are grouped per device by the ingestion.
  • Server side, each connection keeps its subscriptions in a table; each is a task relaying the topic's channel to the connection's mailbox and aborted on close (test: subscriptions are released). Subscribing twice has no effect (idempotent); an unknown or malformed client message is ignored, capped at 1 KiB.
  • Browser side, components subscribe through Realtime::subscribe(&Topic) / unsubscribe, which reference-counts: two widgets on the same device produce one subscription, removed when the last disappears. An effect (layout.rs) sends the difference between wanted and sent state (subscription_diff). On every (re)connection, on receiving hello, the client forgets what it believed subscribed and sends everything again: reconnection after a server restart is therefore transparent (end-to-end test).
  • Simulation tool (Settings → Device state simulator, administrators): a server function inject_device_state that publishes a state under device:<id> (a JSON object of at most 4 KB). It serves as the first real consumer of the protocol before MQTT and as a test bench for widgets.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The dashboard only has to subscribe to the devices it displays; the ingestion publishes with publish_retained without touching the protocol.
  • One more topic = one Topic variant (+ its Display/FromStr, its canonical-form tests) and a rule in authorize.
  • Camera stream access remains to be decided; the right to read devices for all accounts is a decision to revisit if per-device rights appear.
  • The last state stays in memory: a server restart empties it until the next message (the ingestion reloads it from the database).
  • WsServerMsg is no longer Eq (it carries a serde_json::Value); PartialEq is enough for the tests.

docs.title: 0020 — System statistics: sysinfo, published as the last state of the system topic
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-01

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference implementation measured CPU, memory and disk every 5 s (a background thread) and every tab polled /api/system-stats/ every 5 s. The sidebar gauges are kept, a temperature is added, and a WebSocket hub with last state kept is now available (ADR 0019).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Source of measurements. (a) Read /proc and /sys by hand — little code but fragile (formats, containers, other platforms); (b) procfs / sysinfo; (c) sysinfo (MIT, no unsafe on our side, a unified CPU / memory / disks / sensors API) — chosen.

Broadcast. (a) Tabs poll the API in a loop — N authenticated requests (session read in the database) every 5 s per tab; (b) the collector publishes on the system topic (last state kept) and tabs subscribe — one computation, one publication, a new tab served at the first beat — chosen. The REST API remains (clients without WebSocket, scripts) and rereads the same last state: no second cache, no on-demand measurement, so no extra load from an indiscreet client.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• dominet-server::system_stats: Sampler (sysinfo instruments kept from one reading to the next, essential for CPU load which is a difference), reading off the reactor (spawn_blocking), first measurement after MINIMUM_CPU_UPDATE_INTERVAL, then every SYSTEM_STATS_SECS seconds (default 5, 1 to 3600).
  • Conversion into SystemStatsDto by pure functions (build, pick_temperature), tested without a machine: GiB and percentages to one decimal, percentages bounded to 0–100 and never NaN, used memory = total − available, disk = / only.
  • Format: the keys cpu{percent,count}, memory{percent,used_gb,total_gb,available_gb}, disk{percent,used_gb,total_gb,free_gb}, updated_at (Unix seconds) plus temperature. disk and temperature are null when the machine does not expose them: a missing value rather than a wrong one. With no measurement at all (start-up, collector stopped), the API answers 503, not zeros.
  • Temperature: the CPU sensor first (coretemp, package, cpu, tctl, k10temp, soc), otherwise the hottest; values outside 0 < t ≤ 150 ignored.
  • GET /api/system-stats/ requires a signed-in account (401 otherwise), all roles.
  • Browser: a SystemGauges component subscribed to the system topic; bars are divs whose width is set through the CSSOM (style:width), the only way compatible with the CSP without unsafe-inline; "…" values while no measurement is received or if the connection is cut (no stale figure).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• In Docker, /proc describes the host (CPU, memory) but the disk is the container's and the temperature needs /sys/class/thermal mounted; otherwise null.
  • An always-active system topic costs one message per interval even without a subscriber (negligible: a few hundred bytes).
  • sysinfo adds transitive dependencies: cargo deny and cargo audit check them.

docs.title: 0021 — Page render guard: abort and retry a frozen render
docs.text:
• Status: accepted (workaround, to remove when Leptos fixes the defect)
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The realtime end-to-end test failed about 1 time in 10 on the Docker image (a page that never finishes: goto or fetch without an answer, 30 s script timeout). The investigation, summarised:

  • The server is not broken: during the freeze, /healthz, / and /admin/settings answer in 0.0 s to another client with the same cookie. Only one request is lost.
  • Reproduced without a browser (tools/stress-cold-render.sh): after a cold restart, 3 concurrent requests on the same page freeze 1 request in 1 to 5 % of cases (/admin/settings as well as /); 0 out of 100 with one request at a time, 0 out of 150 on an endpoint that only queries the database (/api/auth/me, eight concurrent requests), 0 out of 100 once the same page has already been rendered once. Production image, debug binary and optimised binary: same behaviour as soon as renders overlap when cold.
  • All server threads sleep during the freeze (0 processor ticks in one second): it is neither a loop nor a held lock, it is a wait that is never woken up in the Suspense/Transition rendering of Leptos 0.8.23 (the last stable version; 0.9 only exists as a candidate).
  • Independent of the statistics collector: active or nearly idle (1 s or 3,600 s) gives the same rate (2/40 against 1/40), and the pitfall "several Leptos apps rendered in parallel disturb each other" was already known (the ui.rs test serialises them).
  • The panics in the log ("reactive value that has already been disposed", in tr! of the language selector) are a consequence: when the client disconnects, the request is dropped, its reactive context is released and an orphan task of the frozen render wakes up. They also appear when a client cuts off during a healthy render.
  • Hypotheses tried and discarded: a new_blocking resource in the layout (replaced by new: freeze unchanged), on_cleanup of the real-time subscriptions (the faulty read is leptos-fluent's, not ours), sorting by Firefox headers (Accept-Language…), build mode.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: (a) Wait for a Leptos fix — leaves 1 to 5 % of frozen pages in cold concurrent-render situations. (b) Move to the 0.9 candidate — an uncontrolled API change in the middle of a phase. (c) Rewrite the pages to avoid Transition/resources — enormous, and the exact cause is not isolated. (d) Guard: bound the render of a GET and retry it — a GET changes nothing, a new render almost always succeeds — chosen.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
web/render_guard.rs wraps the interface service (pages and static files): for a body-less GET/HEAD, the response must arrive within 5 s (a normal render takes a few tens of milliseconds); otherwise the render is abandoned and the request, copied identically (method, address, headers, extensions: session, peer address), is retried, at most 3 times; after that the answer is a 503 with Retry-After: 1. POSTs (server functions), requests with a body and WebSockets are never timed out or retried. Every abandonment is logged (WARN … page render without answer: abandoned and retried).

Checked by tools/stress-cold-render.sh: 300 cold starts on the image with the guard, 0 anomalies, 1 render retried and successful (without the guard: 1 to 5 frozen requests per 100 starts).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A frozen render costs 5 s instead of an indefinite hang; a genuinely slow render (> 5 s, saturated database) is retried needlessly, up to 3 times (read-only, bounded).
  • The log contains panics from orphan tasks after a retried render (noise, no effect on other requests: confirmed by the load test).
  • To remove when Leptos fixes the defect: delete render_guard, rebuild the image and require 0 anomalies and 0 retried renders from tools/stress-cold-render.sh over several hundred starts before concluding.
  • The defect has probably been present from the start; the end-to-end tests escaped it because pages were rendered one at a time.

docs.title: 0022 — Dashboard read view: class-based placement, sanitised HTML, restricted Grafana iframes
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The read-only dashboard replaces the provisional home page (editing comes afterwards). Three security and robustness constraints drive the design: the CSP forbids the style attribute (placing each widget by style="grid-column: …" is not possible), the text widget's content is HTML typed by an administrator, and Grafana is displayed in an iframe that the CSP blocks by default.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Placement by classes: a widget carries vc-c-N (column N from 1 to 12), vc-r-N (row 1 to 100), vc-w-N and vc-h-N (width and height, 1 to 12). These classes set CSS variables (--c, --r, --w, --h, plus --w8 and --w4, the width reduced to 8 then 4 columns) and a single .vc-widget rule derives grid-column / grid-row from them. On medium (≤ 1200 px) and narrow (≤ 768 px, ≤ 480 px) screens widgets are placed one after another (auto / span …) instead of keeping their original column, which would fall outside the reduced grid. The domain's maximum row goes from 999 to 99 (the CSS covers 100 rows of 120 px, 12,000 px: plenty); the SQL constraint stays at 999 (the domain is stricter, which needs no migration).
  • text widget HTML sanitised at display time (dominet_server::html::sanitize_widget_html, the ammonia crate): formatting, lists, tables, links and images; no script, iframe, form, style or event handler; http, https, mailto, tel links only, with rel="noopener noreferrer"; id and class attributes removed. The server returns already-safe HTML (content_html): the browser has no security decision to make. The same sanitising serves at save time: the database is not a trusted source (hand-written SQL, import). The "plain text of the configuration" fallback becomes an escaped text with line breaks.
  • Grafana iframes limited to one origin: the address is computed on the server (widget_view::grafana_src: panel_url, device + key, dashboard_uid + panel_id) and is only loaded if its origin is the one of the GRAFANA_PUBLIC_URL setting; otherwise the widget shows "address refused". The CSP gains frame-src <origin> (read from the settings cache, SettingsService::cached_string, loaded at start-up so the header does not have to query the database). uid and key are filtered (alphanumeric characters, -, _): they cannot inject parameters. The iframe carries sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin".
  • Visibility: an account only sees its own dashboards. ?d=<id> of another account, absurd or non-existent falls back to the default dashboard, revealing nothing (tested). Administration of all dashboards comes with editing.
  • Devices: a device widget renders from the hub's last retained state (server rendering), then follows device:<id> live (reference-counted subscription, ADR 0019). The automatic presentation is deduced from the state's keys (widget_view::resolve_presentation: light, blind, climate, fan, lock, weather, switch, binary sensor, sensor, generic); units come from a table of Zigbee2MQTT keys.
  • Dependencies: dominet-domain becomes usable in WASM (uuid without the v4 feature, never used); ammonia on the server side.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A row beyond 99 is refused by the domain; a widget wider than the screen is placed in sequence rather than at its original column.
  • The CSP now contains frame-src on every page (the login included): a minimal surface (one origin, configurable), but not zero; it disappears if the setting is empty or invalid.
  • A Grafana widget whose address changes origin afterwards (setting modified) shows "address refused" instead of loading an iframe the browser blocks.
  • The dashboard selector is a native <details>: no script, keyboard accessible.

docs.title: 0023 — Dashboard editing: administrators only, pointer drag, conditional-field form
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Dashboards become editable: move a widget, create and correct dashboards and widgets. The plan said "owner or administrator" for moving, whereas the earlier decision and the reference implementation reserve layout to administrators.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Editing reserved to administrators (moving, creating, modifying and deleting dashboards and widgets), checked by each server function (403 otherwise, tested for all eight). An ordinary account sees and opens its dashboards but does not modify them; an administrator fills those of all accounts from the administration. Deliberate gap with the plan ("owner or administrator"): letting any owner edit their dashboard would require a second set of rights (fields, widget types, Grafana) that the reference never had.
  • Moving through pointer events (drag.rs) with pointer capture: the same code for mouse, finger and stylus (HTML5 drag and drop does not work with a finger). The widget follows the pointer through a transform set by the CSSOM (allowed by the CSP, unlike the style attribute), a dotted frame shows the target cell, and on release the move_widget server function decides: outside the grid or overlapping → refusal, the widget returns to its place and a message explains why. The server has the last word (the database exclusion constraint, ADR 0018). Active only with the full 12-column grid (≥ 1201 px): below that, widgets are placed in sequence and their on-screen position is no longer the grid's. No keyboard moving; the administration form (column, row) replaces it.
  • Administration: /admin/dashboards (dashboards of all accounts; the owner designated by user name, immutable afterwards) and /admin/widgets?d=<id> (a dashboard's widgets). The generic CRUD component (ADR 0014) gains field_visible: a field is only displayed if a page function judges it useful given the current values (device for device and grafana, scene, camera, content for text, JSON configuration for grafana and camera). Visibility goes through a Memo per field: typing in one field does not recreate the others.
  • Validation: input travels as text (WidgetInput) and the server converts it, field by field (parse_widget), before the domain rules. An overlap is reported on the col field (ProblemKind::Overlap). A text widget's HTML is sanitised at save time (ADR 0022), in addition to display time.

docs.title: Pitfalls met (not to repeat)
docs.text:
• Leptos local storage in a server-rendered component: a StoredValue::new_local (hence SendWrapper) created during rendering is released by another thread → panic and a frozen page. The drag handler (drag::Handle) is ordinary on the server and local only in the browser.
  • A resource whose source depends on another resource (list of widgets depending on the selected dashboard, itself coming from the dashboard list): at hydration, loads chain out of order and the table stayed stale after a save (100 % failure of end-to-end attempts at 1 in 12 depending on the variant). A single server call (widgets_page) now returns the selected dashboard and its widgets.
  • Braces in a Fluent file ({"panel_url": …}): they are expressions; the parse error makes translation loading panic at the first render.
  • In end-to-end tests, wait for hydration to finish (the "Real time: connected" indicator) before the first click: before it, a button is present and enabled but has no effect.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• An ordinary account cannot populate its own dashboard: an administrator must do it (or a per-account editing right may be added later).
  • A dashboard cannot change owner (delete and recreate).
  • camera and scene widgets save with their reference (UUID, number) from the start.

docs.title: 0024 — Browser end-to-end tests: stay on Marionette/Firefox
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Playwright had been planned for the end-to-end tests. Since the first phase they run with Firefox driven by Marionette (a home-made, dependency-free client, tests/e2e/marionette.py), plugged into a throw-away database, the local binary and the Docker image (tools/e2e.sh). Node, needed by Playwright, is absent from the host (the production machine).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: (a) Stay on Marionette — 11 scripts, 286 checks, nothing to install, already in make ci-full; the WebDriver pointer actions (WebDriver:PerformActions) suffice to test pointer drag and drop. (b) Install Node and Playwright — automatic waits and traces, but a second ecosystem on the production machine and a rewrite of the existing scripts.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Option (a), until proven otherwise: reassess if Marionette cannot test live video.

Rules learned, to apply in every new script: - Wait for hydration to finish (the "Real time: connected" indicator) before the first click: a button present and enabled before hydration has no effect. - Use a device number specific to the script: the end-to-end server is shared and remembers each device's last state. - Prepare data the interface cannot create through E2E_DB_SHELL (SQL on the throw-away database); prefer the interface when it can do it. - A failure must be explainable: tools/e2e.sh shows the beginning of the server's panic or the end of its log, KEEP_SERVER_LOG keeps the log, DOMINET_BIN/DOMINET_SITE try another build profile.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No Node on the host; end-to-end tests stay runnable on the production machine.
  • No automatic waits: every wait is written (wait_for); an unstable test is a defect of the test or of the product, to elucidate (two Leptos rendering defects were found this way).

docs.title: 0025 — Device schema: replaced state, per-second history, images in the database
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Devices (Zigbee2MQTT, generic MQTT sources), their history, images, MQTT sources and weather stations are introduced. The acceptance criterion is a replay: the same MQTT messages must give the same Devices, states and history rows as the reference implementation. The schema and domain rules therefore take over its semantics, quirks included, while taking advantage of PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Tables: device_group, device_label, device, device_image, device_state_log, mqtt_source, weather_station. BIGINT identity primary keys; friendly_name unique and case-sensitive.
  • State replaced, not merged: device.state (a JSON object) is replaced at every message, last_seen = now(), available = true; availability (…/availability) does not touch last_seen. The MQTT listener's operations are repository methods (apply_state, set_available, upsert_discovered, upsert_auto, touch_by_topic): one SQL statement each, hence idempotent (the QoS 1 duplicates of ADR 0005 have no effect but last_seen).
  • Key lists as TEXT[] (tracked_keys, hidden_keys) rather than JSON: the type guarantees the shape (a list of texts); exposes and state stay JSONB.
  • History: device_state_log(device_id, key, ts, value_num, value_str) per second, UNIQUE(device_id, key, ts), batch writes (UNNEST) with replacement of an existing row of the same instant. An index (device_id, key, ts DESC) for charts and (ts) for purging (configurable retention).
  • Discovery (bridge/devices): creation with the zigbee2mqtt prefix, the hidden key update and a type deduced from exposes; an existing device keeps its type, tracked keys, icon and state (only the discovered metadata is refreshed). Quirk of the reference kept: only composite elements of exposes are flattened to deduce the type, so a Zigbee2MQTT light, switch or cover (which carry features but are not composite) stay generic. The replay against the reference checks this equivalence; fixing the deduction is an improvement to decide separately. Units, on the other hand, flatten all features.
  • auto_device sources: the device is created or updated and reactivated (active = true), without its type changing.
  • Images: a device_image table (reduced JPEG, 5 MiB at most, types checked) served by an ETag route: no volume to back up separately. image_url (an external URL) remains possible.
  • Names and topics: a device name is used to build topics; the domain refuses control characters, MQTT wildcards (+, #), leading or trailing / and // (is_valid_friendly_name). A discovery with an invalid name is ignored rather than failing. A subscription filter (mqtt_source.topic_pattern) must be a valid MQTT filter (+ on a whole level, # last level).
  • Foreign key widget.device_id (announced by ADR 0018): ON DELETE SET NULL; orphan references are set to NULL before adding the constraint. A reference to a non-existent device is refused when saving the widget.
  • handler_code of sources: kept as is (≤ 20,000 characters) and displayed, executed by Rhai; code in another language is not portable.
  • Labels: KNOWN_LABELS (25 keys) is in the domain; dominet seed-labels [--dry-run] creates the missing labels of keys present on devices, never overwriting.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• 21 tables; the end-to-end scripts that used fictitious device numbers now create their devices.
  • The replay against the reference result settles any semantic gap; the type deduction of light/switch/cover is the first quirk to watch.
  • No production data migration here.

docs.title: 0026 — Supervised MQTT client: immediate or refused publications, re-subscribe on every connection
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The application listens to Zigbee2MQTT and MQTT sources, and publishes device commands, weather readings and SolarMax values. The client spike (ADR 0005) validated rumqttc. What remains is the client's long-term behaviour: what to do with a command when the broker is unreachable, how to resume after a drop, how to change subscriptions live, how to stop cleanly.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• dominet-mqtt crate, with no dependency on the server: settings (MqttSettings, password masked in Debug), client (start), payload decoding, topic matching. The server adapts its configuration (mqtt::settings). rumqttc without default features: clear TCP (a local-network broker, anonymous or with a password); TLS will be added when a remote broker needs it.
  • One task supervises the connection: poll() in a loop, recovery after an error with a growing delay (250 ms to 5 s), re-subscription of the whole wanted set on every ConnAck (nothing is assumed about the broker session, ADR 0005), state exposed through a watch channel (Connecting, Connected, Disconnected). Persistent session (clean_session = false) and a stable client identifier.
  • A publication fails at once if the link is down (PublishError::NotConnected) instead of being queued. A light or blind command executed ten minutes after the click is worse than a displayed error. A message accepted by the API is delivered at least once (QoS 1, resent after reconnection); what the broker had accepted without forwarding survives its stop only if it persists its data.
  • Wanted subscriptions: a filter → QoS set replaced as a block (set_subscriptions); the task applies the difference at once if the link is up (diff_subscriptions, pure and tested), otherwise at the next connection. A QoS change re-subscribes. MQTT sources modified in the interface thus apply without a restart.
  • Received messages decoded: UTF-8 (otherwise Latin-1), JSON if possible, otherwise text. An input queue of 8,192 messages: when full, reading from the network waits (the broker slows down, nothing is lost).
  • Stop: shutdown() (a level, not an event: a pause in progress does not absorb it), clean disconnection, end of the task. If nobody consumes the messages or holds the handle any more, the task stops.
  • Roles: dominet serve starts web and, if MQTT_HOST is set, mqtt; --only mqtt runs the client alone (the process then waits for the stop signal). Default identifier dominet (MQTT_CLIENT_ID).
  • Tests: unit (matching, decoding, subscription difference, publication topics, masked password); integration on the development Mosquitto (round trip, retained messages, live subscriptions, stop) and on a throw-away Mosquitto (a named, persistent container removed at the end) for drops: the shared broker is never stopped.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• During an outage, commands are refused and the publishers' readings are lost for the current cycle; they resume at the next cycle. Device states come back from the broker (Zigbee2MQTT retained messages) at reconnection.
  • Drop tests need Docker (already required by the development stack) and the eclipse-mosquitto:2.0 image.
  • QoS 1 messages may arrive twice: ingestion is idempotent (ADR 0025).

docs.title: 0027 — Zigbee2MQTT ingestion: same result as the reference implementation, checked on recorded sessions
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The acceptance criterion is a replay: the same MQTT messages must produce the same devices, states and history rows as the reference implementation. Reading its code to reproduce it is not enough (a quirk of the flattening of exposes had already been found). The reference implementation had to be executed on the same messages and compared.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Frozen reference result: the reference message handler was run once on a message file, on a throw-away PostgreSQL, with a virtual clock (the time comes from the file) so that the per-second history is reproducible. The result (devices and history, as JSON) is versioned next to the message file (session-r3.golden.json): the Rust tests need neither Docker nor the reference. The scripts that produced it are not kept; the file is.
  • Replay session (tests/fixtures/z2m/session-r3.jsonl, 64 lines): 11 devices of varied shapes (sensor, light, blind, sockets, contact, presence, unsupported device, a name containing a / or spaces), coordinator, re-discovery with changed metadata, added device, states repeated within the same second or not, booleans, texts, nested objects, null, accented characters, availabilities in all their forms, unknown device, device deactivated then reactivated, noise to ignore (/set, /get, bridge/*, non-JSON or non-object payloads).
  • dominet-automation::ingest module, generic over the storage ports and over a Sink (broadcast; later automations and alerts): it knows neither PostgreSQL nor the hub, so it can be replayed on a file. Routing (route) follows the order of the reference: bridge/devices, bridge/info (object), …/availability before the exclusion of bridge/… topics, then …/set/…/get, then the state.
  • One ingestion task, in batches: messages are taken in batches of 256; a device state is ignored if the next message about the same device is also a state received within the same second (bridge/devices breaks any grouping). The final result is identical (replaced state, per-second history where the last wins; checked by the "one-second batches" replay), the intermediate broadcast is lost. Outside bursts each batch holds one message: no grouping. Measured: 4,000 messages (50 devices × 80) in 1.7 s, 832 broadcasts. Consequence for automations: under a burst, a "device state" trigger only sees the last state of each device per second (see ADR 0032).
  • Server sink (HubSink): every change is published on device:<id> with last state retained (ADR 0019); at start-up, the known database state of every active device is republished, so widgets show it even after a restart. permit_join is remembered in AppState.
  • Zigbee2MQTT prefix = the Z2M_BASE_TOPIC setting: changing it in the interface changes the subscription (<prefix>/#, QoS 1) and the routing live, without a restart. upsert_discovered receives this prefix.

docs.title: Deviations from the reference
docs.text:
1. Metadata at creation (fixed): the reference puts ieee, vendor, model_id, description and exposes in defaults, but an upsert whose defaults only apply at creation: a discovered device stays without metadata until the next bridge/devices republication. Here they are written immediately. The replay test does not hide the gap: it requires the device to carry exactly the metadata of the last discovery in the file.
  2. Invalid names ignored: a discovery whose name contains an MQTT wildcard or a control character is ignored (the reference would accept it); texts longer than their column are truncated (the reference would fail with a database error).
  3. Quirk kept: only composite elements are flattened to deduce the type (ADR 0025) — the reference result confirms it (a classic Zigbee2MQTT lamp stays generic).
  4. Messages outside the Zigbee2MQTT prefix are handled by the generic sources (ADR 0028).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Every extension of the replay (auto_device sources) uses the same mechanism: a message file, a reference result, a comparison.
  • The Rust tests compare with the versioned file and need nothing else.

docs.title: 0028 — MQTT sources, history and the raw ReductStore archive
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Zigbee2MQTT ingestion listens to zigbee2mqtt/#. The reference implementation also listens to every active MqttSource (Linky, SolarMax, weather…), can create a device at every message (auto_device), records tracked keys in history (PostgreSQL) and — decision of ADR 0002 — raw IoT must also go to ReductStore. This work adds these three things and the administration page for sources.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Dynamic sources. Ingestion keeps the list of active sources (Ingestor::set_sources); a message outside the Zigbee2MQTT prefix is matched against each source's filter (topic_matches, MQTT 3.1.1). Modifying a source in the administration notifies the listener (AppState.sources_changed, an in-process Notify) which rereads the sources, updates the routing and the subscriptions (difference only: set_subscriptions). A safety reload every 60 s covers the case where administration and listener run in two processes (--only web, --only mqtt). A filter declared twice (or equal to <prefix>/#) is subscribed once, at the highest QoS.
  • Behaviour taken from the reference: for each matching source — a log entry if log_messages (topic and beginning of the payload, 512 characters), an automatic device if auto_device and the payload is a JSON object; then, if at least one source matched, active devices whose base_topic/name or base_topic equals the topic are marked seen. The automatic device takes the topic without the source's prefix as its name (otherwise the whole topic), replaces its state, is reactivated if it was disabled, is broadcast in real time and recorded in history like a Zigbee2MQTT device.
  • handler_code is kept, editable and displayed in the administration; it is run by the Rhai host (ADR 0006).
  • Raw ReductStore archive (iot), optional (REDUCTSTORE_URL). One record per message that writes at least one history row: body = the full JSON state, one label per numeric tracked key (booleans are 0/1), entry dev_<id>, timestamp in µs. The bucket name is iot (configurable: REDUCTSTORE_IOT_BUCKET, for tests), FIFO quota IOT_QUOTA_GB (default 5) applied at bucket creation. Writing goes through a bounded queue (10,000) and a task writing in batches of 50 (HTTP header limit found by the spike): ingestion never waits for ReductStore. Server unreachable: the bucket is recreated on the next attempt, records that do not go through are dropped and counted (a warning at the first outage, a message at recovery). Two messages of the same device in the same microsecond get shifted timestamps (ReductStore refuses duplicates).
  • PostgreSQL stays the source of charts. device_state_log is purged once a day beyond HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS (default 400; ADR 0002 proposed 30 days provisionally). Environment variables rather than application settings: like REDUCTSTORE_URL, they describe the deployment, not the house's behaviour.
  • /admin/mqtt-sources page (administrators): the generic CRUD component (ADR 0014), typed list/save/delete server functions, field-by-field validation by the domain (MqttSource::problems: a valid MQTT filter, QoS 0 to 2, lengths), prefix stripped of its trailing /.

docs.title: Deviations from the reference
docs.text:
1. State at creation of the automatic device: the reference writes state, available and last_seen in defaults, with an upsert whose defaults only apply at creation: a source's first message leaves no state in the database (it is only broadcast). Here the state is written at once (same defect as the one fixed in ADR 0027).
  2. Invalid names ignored: a topic that would make an invalid device name (more than 128 characters, wildcard, control character) is ignored instead of causing a database error.
  3. No "retry once" on database connection loss: the connection pool reconnects, a lost message is resent by the broker's QoS 1 as long as the session persists.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• During a ReductStore outage, PostgreSQL history continues; only the raw archive has a gap (counted in the log, in a metric later).
  • Changing IOT_QUOTA_GB does not act on an existing bucket (set it in ReductStore or delete the bucket): a documented limit.
  • The weather and SolarMax publishers publish on the broker: their topics are declared like any source (meteo/#, solarmax/#); nothing special on the ingestion side.
  • ReductStore's HTTP client (rustls) cannot be built without root certificates, and reduct-rs panicked then: the Docker image installs ca-certificates, and the server uses try_build — on failure it starts without an archive (warning) instead of stopping. Discovered by the end-to-end test on the image (make ci-full), not by host tests.

docs.title: 0029 — Device commands, pages and images
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Devices have been brought from MQTT into the database and live. This work makes them usable: command them, see them (list, detail, widgets), administer them, give them an image, generate their Grafana dashboard. The reference implementation publishes any JSON (device_command), puts everything in a generated administration site and stores an uploaded image as is.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Commands (dominet_server::control). Any signed-in account may command (the family turns on a light); opening pairing (permit_join), uploading an image, generating a Grafana dashboard and configuring devices are reserved to administrators. A command is a non-empty JSON object, 1 KB at most, 3 levels at most (dominet_domain::command) — the interface only sends flat objects, Zigbee2MQTT accepts a few nested objects (color), nothing else makes sense. It is published at QoS 1, not retained, on <prefix>/<name>/set, for an active device only. With no link to the broker (no mqtt role, broker down) it is refused at once (Unavailable), never queued: a command replayed later would be a surprise. The effect shows when the device republishes its state; the interface anticipates nothing.
  • Device widgets (device_widget). The type, labels (name, unit) and hidden keys come from the device table (DeviceMetaDto, carrying only the labels of keys present in the state). Automatic presentation follows the type when it is precise, otherwise the state (ADR 0025: a Zigbee2MQTT lamp stays generic, so the state decides). Commands are {"state":"ON"}, brightness, color_temp, position, OPEN/STOP/CLOSE, LOCK/UNLOCK, the occupied_heating_setpoint set point in steps of 0.5, fan_mode. Buttons are enabled if the server has an MQTT client and the device is available; otherwise disabled with the tooltip "source unavailable".
  • Pages. /automation/ (list) and /automation/devices/<id> — both spellings of the address are served. Filters (group, place, type) through a GET form: no state in the browser, the address is shareable. Cards reuse the widget body (same code, same commands, same real time). The detail shows identity, topics, the last 24 hours of tracked keys (SVG curves computed in the browser, no library) and, for an administrator, the tools: image, Grafana dashboard, pairing (on the list).
  • Administration: /admin/devices, /admin/device-groups, /admin/device-labels with the generic CRUD (ADR 0014). A new field type Choice: a drop-down whose choices come from the database, supplied by a context (Choices) — Select types stay static and translated. A dashboard widget chooses its device from a list instead of a number.
  • Images: PostgreSQL (device_image), served by /media/devices/<id> with ETag (private, no-cache: revalidated, 304 without body). Upload by multipart form to /api/devices/<id>/image (administrators, redirect to the page): 5 MB and 8,000 pixels per side at most, format recognised by content (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF), then decoded, reduced to at most 400 × 300 and re-encoded as JPEG (transparency composited on white). What is stored is therefore always a sane, small image, whatever file was sent. The image crate without default features (jpeg, png, webp, gif).
  • Grafana dashboard (dominet_domain::grafana, dominet_server::grafana): one panel per tracked key, written as a file in GRAFANA_DASHBOARDS_DIR (never through the API: a dashboard loaded from a file becomes "provisioned" and the API refuses to modify it). Atomic write (temporary file then rename), incremented version, old file deleted if the device is renamed, sanitised file name. Without a configured folder, the page says so.
  • Simulator: only acts on an existing device, with its real name; it broadcasts without writing anything to the database.

docs.title: Deviations from the reference
docs.text:
1. A validated command (object, size, depth) instead of publishing anything.
  2. An image re-encoded and reduced instead of kept as is; formats refused by content and not by the Content-Type header sent by the browser.
  3. Pairing is reserved to administrators (the reference: any signed-in account).
  4. No editing page of a generated site: editing is in the /admin/… pages.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A browser without WebAssembly cannot command (buttons are interface actions) but sees all pages; image upload and filtering work without JavaScript.
  • A device's detail only shows numeric keys; text history (e.g. action) stays in the database and in Grafana.
  • There is no optimistic state (the interface does not show the command before the device's echo): the price is a slight delay, the gain is that a displayed state is always a real state.

docs.title: 0030 — Weather and SolarMax publishers, supervised inside the server
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference implementation ran two separate processes (a weather publisher and a SolarMax publisher) that read an external source and publish on MQTT; the MQTT-source pipeline turns them into devices. The SolarMax was contacted at a hard-coded address, the production inverter's. Project rule: no contact with the inverter without explicit agreement.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Server tasks: a publishers role (active by default when MQTT_HOST is set) starts supervised tasks (supervise: a panic restarts the task with a 1 to 60 s pause). It publishes through the mqtt role's client if it runs, otherwise through its own (identifier …-publishers, no subscription). --only publishers allows a separate process. The loops live in dominet-integrations and only know the Publisher trait: they are tested without a broker.
  • Weather: the task always runs but only queries the API for enabled stations (no station, no request). A cycle goes through the enabled stations; a failing station does not stop the others. The pause is the shortest refresh_minutes of the enabled stations (30 s without a station: a database reread, no API request, to see quickly a station created by dominet seed-weather in another process) and the task is woken when a station is created or modified in the administration (AppState.stations_changed). The API address is OPEN_METEO_URL (default: the public API): tests and CI talk to a simulated API.
  • SolarMax: the protocol is ported to Rust (solarmax::protocol, pure) and checked against frozen vectors from the reference. Byte-identical requests, same scaling, same rounding (half-even: round(115.25, 1) is 115.2). The asynchronous TCP client is time-bounded, drops the connection at the slightest error and resumes at the next cycle. An inverter alarm (SAL ≠ 0) is an error: nothing is published. The publication topic is a setting (SOLARMAX_TOPIC).
  • No default inverter address. Without SOLARMAX_HOST there is no SolarMax publisher and dominet publish solarmax refuses to run. Tests use a simulated inverter (a TCP server on 127.0.0.1).
  • Diagnostic: dominet publish weather|solarmax [--print-only] runs one cycle, prints the result and publishes (unless --print-only).
  • Administration: /admin/weather-stations (generic CRUD, decimal comma accepted, all form problems reported together). dominet seed-weather [--lat --lon …] creates the "Weather" source (meteo/#, automatic devices), the meteo_locale device and the station.
  • dominet dump-context: a YAML snapshot of active devices (type, state schema deduced from current values, numeric keys, command topic, place) and reference schemas. The YAML is written by an emitter of a few dozen lines (no maintained YAML library needed): strings always quoted, reserved keys quoted.
  • serde_json switches to preserve_order: the key order of a state is the database's.

docs.title: Deviations from the reference
docs.text:
1. No fake initial state for the weather device: it waits for the first real reading.
  2. The weather device's manufacturer and model are not filled in: a hand-created device does not carry these discovery fields.
  3. The weather topic is meteo/<suffix>.
  4. A publication no longer creates an MQTT connection per message (the reference connected, published and disconnected at every cycle): the server's client stays connected.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A broker outage interrupts publications (refused at once, logged); they resume at the next cycle without intervention.
  • A second --only publishers process and another mqtt role must not run at the same time with the same client identifier (the -publishers suffix avoids it).
  • Real contact with the inverter and with the Open-Meteo API remains reserved to explicit demonstration with agreement.

docs.title: 0031 — Scene, automation, alert and energy schema
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Scenes, automations, alert rules and the energy balance follow the reference implementation. Reading its code showed that device_state was never evaluated there and that mqtt_publish published nothing: we implement the data's intent, not all of the mechanics. This work lays down the schema, the domain and the repositories; later work plugs the engine into them.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• JSON shape of the reference in the database, strong types in memory. automation.trigger_type + trigger_config, condition, action_type + action_config keep the reference's shape (real scenarios load as they are, without conversion). The domain reads them into enums (Trigger, Condition, Action) that validate field by field; a database row that can no longer be read back is flagged as corrupt data rather than silently ignored. Plugins are read as script (Rhai, code in the script column).
  • Scenes. scene + scene_action (device, JSON command, position). The name is unique (the script API activates a scene by name; the reference imposed nothing and crashed on a duplicate). Commands follow the same rules as widget commands (non-empty JSON object, 1 KB, 3 levels), at most 100 per scene. Creating and replacing actions is one transaction: never a half-written scene. widget.scene_id becomes a foreign key (ON DELETE SET NULL, orphan references set to NULL before the constraint).
  • Execution log automation_run (one row per firing: instant, cause, status ok|error|skipped|limited, duration, message bounded to 1,000 characters), deleted with the automation, purged by age. The reference only had last_triggered and trigger_count (kept).
  • Scheduler. schedule_job gains automation_id (unique, deleted with the automation) and accepts the nine solar events (the original constraint only admitted two).
  • Alerts. alert_rule (device, key, operator, numeric or text threshold, severity, cooldown in minutes, three channels) and alert (status firing|resolved|acknowledged, triggering value, dates, acknowledgement by an account). AlertRuleDraft::evaluate is the reference's computation: value and threshold read as numbers (numeric text and booleans included, float(True) = 1.0), fallback to case- and space-insensitive text equality for eq / neq only, contains on the text form of the value (True, None). An alert whose rule is deleted stays (without a rule); those of a deleted device go with it. latest_firing only looks at current alerts: this is the reference's quirk (an acknowledged alert leaves the cooldown computation), reproduced on purpose.
  • Energy. energy_daily_log (one local day per row, four integers in Wh). recent(n) returns the last n days from oldest to newest: the reference wrongly returned the first n (the page froze after thirty days).
  • Cron. CronSpec::parse takes the syntax of a classic crontab (lists, ranges, steps, a reversed range that wraps around the field, named weekdays, Sunday = 0); the next-run computation is described in ADR 0033.
  • Real scenarios. A conversion of a real installation's context into tests/fixtures/automation/prod-context.json; dominet_domain::scenarios reads it (feature scenarios, never in the binary). No import: these are test data sets.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Administration forms validate through the same problems() as the database: a single source of rules.
  • The execution log grows with activity: purge tied to the history retention.

docs.title: 0032 — Automation engine (mqtt_message and device_state triggers)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Reading the reference implementation showed that device_state was never evaluated there, that mqtt_message was only evaluated for Zigbee2MQTT states and that mqtt_publish published nothing (no client). We implement the documented intent, keeping identical what works in the reference (topic wildcards, payload filter, condition). The engine must keep up with the ingestion rate (2,000 messages/s) without slowing it down.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• One engine, one queue. The ingestion (Sink) announces two things: every useful message (message) and every device state (device_state). An EngineHandle discards at the source whatever no automation waits for (a read of an in-memory copy of the active automations, with no database access) and queues the rest in a bounded queue (1,024). A single Engine::run consumes the queue, event by event, in order: never two automations at once, never a race on counters. Queue full: the event is dropped and counted (never a wait on the ingestion side).
  • Which messages trigger mqtt_message. Device states and availabilities and all messages outside the Zigbee2MQTT prefix (among them those of a topic with no MQTT source: the client subscribes by itself to the topic of every active mqtt_message automation, QoS 1). Not bridge/… messages nor …/set / …/get commands: an automation that commands a device would see its own command go by.
  • Meaning of device_state. Fires for every state message of the device whose state[key] equals value, by the text form of scalars (28 = "28") or numerically (28.0 = 28); never non-scalar values. Remote-control keys are events (action: 1_single): a repeated "ON" state fires again at every message.
  • Bursts: grouped states stay visible. The ingestion (ADR 0027) only keeps the last state of a device received within the same second. A remote control sends {"action":"1_single"} then {"action":""} a few milliseconds apart: the first would be lost. The Sink therefore also receives state_skipped for every grouped state (not stored, not broadcast, but seen by automations, in its place in the order). Found by an intermittent test of a remote-control scenario.
  • Equalities of the reference. 1 == 1.0, True == 1, recursive equality of lists and objects; a key absent from the payload counts as None for the filter (a null filter lets it through); topic matching where # accepts the end of any level. Checked against the reference implementation on 396 cases (frozen in tests/fixtures/automation/matching.json).
  • Anti-loop guard. At most 30 firings per automation per minute (sliding window); the following ones are ignored and the overflow is logged once a minute (limited).
  • Effects through a port. Executor (publish, activate a scene, notify): the server implements it with the mqtt role's client (QoS 1 publication, not retained), scenes::activate_by_id and the notifications real-time topic. Tests simulate it. A scene activated with a failure, an unknown scene and a refused publication are failures (error) in the log.
  • Log and counters. Every firing that passed the filter and the condition writes an automation_run row (cause, status, duration, detail) and increments trigger_count / last_triggered — failures and no-effect actions included. A false filter or condition writes nothing (the log would drown). Purge after 30 days, once a day.
  • Hot reload. Any change (administration) wakes the mqtt role's loop (automations_changed), which reloads the engine and recomputes subscriptions; a safety reread every 60 s.
  • Scripts and scheduling. script actions go through the Rhai host (ADR 0034); schedule and solar triggers go through the scheduler (ADR 0033).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The engine never waits for the ingestion and vice versa; its only constraint is the bounded queue (never reached in practice: an automation takes a few milliseconds).
  • Deviations from the reference are all deliberate and tested.

docs.title: 0033 — Scheduler (cron, sun) and solar computation
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference implementation relied on an external scheduler: a CrontabSchedule (zone Europe/Paris) or a SolarSchedule per schedule / solar automation, and ephem for the sun. We want to do without it, with a computation checked against the reference.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• A scheduler role, in the default serve process (with web), the single instance of an installation. It reads the schedule_job table; the next run is persisted (next_run_at) for the administration but recomputed at start-up and on every definition change. It sleeps until the next run, at most 30 s, and wakes up when the administration edits an automation (schedule_changed).
  • No catch-up. A run discovered more than 60 s after its time (server stopped, slow database) is not replayed: the job notes "missed (N s late, no catch-up)" and moves on.
  • Synchronisation with automations. Every active automation with a schedule or solar trigger has an automation-<id> job (task run_automation) that follows its definition; disabled, deleted or turned into mqtt_message, its job disappears.
