An unchanged definition keeps its next run. The system job compute_daily_energy (5 0 * * *, zone TZ) is created if missing and never overwritten afterwards (it can be edited).
  • Cron. Classic five-field syntax (ADR 0031), wall-clock time of the job's zone (TZ, Europe/Paris by default). The day of month and the day of week must both match (not Vixie cron). Daylight-saving changes as in the reference: a non-existent hour (spring jump, 02:30) is read with the offset from before the jump (so 03:30 summer time), a repeated hour (autumn fall-back) is taken at its first occurrence and its second occurrence fires nothing. Each behaviour is covered by the frozen reference values.
  • Sun without a dependency. dominet_domain::solar: Meeus series for the sun's position, equation of time, hour angle. Same conventions as the reference: sunrise and sunset at the upper limb at −34′ (centre ≈ −0.83°), dawns and dusks at the centre at −6°, −12°, −18°, solar noon = meridian transit. Midnight sun or polar night: no event within the next three days, so no event; the job retries 6 h later.
  • Interval. Supported by the table and the computation (after + n × unit); no automation produces one today.
  • Execution. The scheduler fires the automation through the same engine as messages (Engine::fire: guard, log, counters), so scene, publication and notification behave identically. An --only scheduler process opens its own MQTT client (no listening) if a broker is configured.

docs.title: Verification against the reference
docs.text:
• 119 sequences of six cron runs (17 expressions × 7 starting points: daylight-saving nights, year end, 29 February): identical to the second.
  • 1,036 solar events (9 events × 5 places × 12 months × 2 starting hours, including Reykjavik and Sydney): maximum gap 13 s (tolerance 90 s). Cases where the reference itself fails (midnight sun) are set aside. Expected values are frozen in tests/fixtures/automation/schedule.json.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No external scheduler and no Redis: one process, one table.
  • Solar accuracy depends on series good to about 0.01°: plenty for blinds, to revisit only beyond the polar circles.
  • chrono-tz (embedded IANA database) enters the server binary, never the WASM (the domain does not depend on it).

docs.title: 0034 — Rhai scripts: implementation (automations and source handler code)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-02

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0006 chose sandboxed Rhai (spike go). This work integrates it into the automation engine (ADR 0032) and opens it to the handler_code of MQTT sources, with an editor and a dry run.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Host in dominet-automation::script, as in ADR 0006: engine rebuilt at every execution, new_raw + the standard package, 200,000 operations, 250 ms, depth 24 / 48, strings 16 KB, arrays 2,000, maps 500, no eval or import, execution in spawn_blocking. Deviations from ADR 0006: limits are constants (Limits::default(), passed as a parameter) and not AppSetting settings — nothing justifies them in administration yet; no AST cache (compilation in the order of ten microseconds, negligible against the database).
  • All or nothing. Effects (publish, scene, log_value) are collected then applied in order only if the script ends without error: a script that publishes then crashes does not leave a half-applied state (the reference applied as it went). An effect refused at application (broker down, unknown scene) does not stop the following ones and makes the execution fail in the log.
  • Missing key = (). ADR 0006 made access to a non-existent key fail; with payload.moving == "UP" on a state that has no moving (a common case: Zigbee2MQTT states are partial), it was an error at every press. Access returns (); a typo becomes silent, print helps find it.
  • The Executor port grows: publish takes a text, and scene_by_name, log_value and devices (a snapshot of active devices, read only when an action is a script) are added. Scripts therefore go through the same engine, the same guard and the same log as other actions.
  • Trigger context: the event carries the topic (the device's for a state), the message and the device concerned; a schedule or solar trigger gives an empty context.
  • Source handler code. Ingestion announces (Sink::source_handler) the messages of active sources that have code; the engine runs them in the same queue. No automation so no automation_run row: the result goes to the server log. A 10 s mute for a source whose code fails: a chatty source with faulty (or hostile) code does not monopolise the engine (at worst 250 ms every 10 s). Correct code is not limited in count (a source like Linky sends a message per second).
  • Code in another language refused with a clear message. At save time, script::check recognises Python-style code (def, import, from … import, class, elif, context., logger., trailing colon) before trying to compile, then returns the Rhai parser's error (line, column). The field shows Invalid script: … (ProblemKind::Syntax).
  • Editor: a fixed-font code area (FieldKind::Code of the generic CRUD) and a dry run (scripts/dry-run, administrators): same host, real device states, effects described and not applied. CodeMirror remains possible later without changing the API.
  • Shipped shutter scripts. Two example scripts (crates/dominet-domain/data/volet-sb-est-*.rhai) stop a moving shutter on a press, otherwise open (left button) or close (right button); they depend on a specific relay's behaviour (position-derived state, about one message per second while moving) and are examples to adapt.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The time limit only acts between two Rhai operations: any future host function must be non-blocking and bounded (today all are in-memory additions).
  • A slow script (250 ms) delays the following events of the single queue; the bounded queue drops and counts what overflows.
  • The hostile scripts of ADR 0006 are all replayed in unit tests, in dry run and in end-to-end tests (the server answers during and after).

docs.title: 0035 — Alerts: evaluation, lifecycle, send port
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-03

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference implementation evaluates alert rules after every device state, creates an alert with a minimum delay between two (cooldown), resolves current alerts when the condition ceases, and lets the user acknowledge them (an alerts page, a sidebar badge). The requirement is to reproduce its rules quirks included, to verify them by running the reference implementation, to broadcast the alert to the interface and to provide a send port.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Evaluation. After every recorded state message (Zigbee2MQTT and automatic devices; Sink::device_state, not the grouped states), dominet_automation::alerts::AlertEngine reads state[key] for each enabled rule of the device: key missing or null → nothing (neither firing nor resolving); condition true → an alert is created unless a current alert of the rule for this device is younger than cooldown_minutes; condition false → the rule's current alerts are resolved. Same structure as the automation engine: a handle that discards at the source what no rule watches, a bounded queue, a loop.
  • Quirks of the reference reproduced on purpose, all verified: an acknowledged alert no longer counts in the cooldown (the next hot state creates one at once); an alert that stays true is recreated at every cooldown expiry; cooldown = 0 creates an alert at every true state; the true / false / true toggle does not hold the resolved alert's cooldown; a non-numeric value with a numeric operator = false (eq / neq fall back to case- and space-insensitive text equality); contains searches the text form of the value (True, None).
  • Gap found by the reference run. float("1_000") is 1000 in the reference (underscores between two digits); f64::from_str refuses it. Fixed in float_from_text (2,030 identical combinations since).
  • Verification against the reference implementation: the rule evaluation run on 2,030 combinations; the alert cycle replayed with a controlled clock over 8 scenarios (cooldown, acknowledgement, missing value, text, fast toggle…), the state of alerts compared after every step with the Rust engine's on a throw-away database. The expected values are frozen in tests/fixtures/automation/alerts.json.
  • Efficiency. Enabled rules are in memory per device (reloaded at every modification and every 60 s); the database is only read to decide a firing (last current alert); a resolution only writes if the (rule, device) pair may have a current alert (an in-memory set filled at start-up from the database).
  • Notifier port (fired(&AlertNotice), changed()). UiNotifier publishes on notifications the short text ([DomiNet] rule — device: value) with a level according to severity (info, warning, error) and logs the rule's three channels. AlertNotice also carries the long text (e-mail). notified stays false until a real channel (e-mail, SMS, Android push) has sent it.
  • Current alert count. A new real-time topic alerts (WsServerMsg::AlertCount, last state kept, any signed-in account): the sidebar badge and the /alerts page update live, without polling. The count is published at start-up, at every firing / resolution and every acknowledgement.
  • Pages. /alerts (any signed-in account: filters current / resolved / acknowledged / all, 200 alerts, acknowledge one alert, acknowledge all); /admin/alert-rules (administrators, generic CRUD: numeric threshold with a decimal comma accepted, three channels, delay 0 to 1,440 min). The "Alerts" link of the sidebar is fixed (like the reference's badge) and not a menu entry in the database: existing installations are not modified. Deleting a rule leaves its alerts (without a rule).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• States grouped by ingestion are not evaluated: under a burst, an isolated threshold crossing in the same second as a following state of the same device may be missed (the reference evaluated every state). Weather / energy values arrive much more slowly.
  • E-mail, SMS and Android channels plug in behind Notifier without touching evaluation.

docs.title: 0036 — Daily energy balance
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-03

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference implementation aggregates every night (00:05) the counter history into a per-day balance (EnergyDailyLog): Linky peak and off-peak, solar production, heat pump. A page shows the last 30 balances (a Chart.js chart loaded from a CDN), the live state, and a JSON API. The requirement: the same computation, verified against the reference, a chart without a JavaScript library, and the means to put devices in a state to produce the history.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Same computation as compute_daily_energy, run by the reference implementation as the oracle:
  • the day is the local day (from local midnight to the next local midnight: 23 h on the day of the spring change, 25 h on the day of the autumn change) — adding one day to a zoned datetime is a wall-clock addition;
  • cumulative counters (HCHP, HCHC, energy_a, energy_b): maximum − minimum of the day, truncated towards zero, never negative; text values are ignored;
  • production = maximum of qdy (kWh, reset every day) × 1000, truncated (int(1.005 * 1000) is 1004 in the reference: same float, same result);
  • a missing device counts zero (warning). 13 days (including daylight-saving nights, the last and first second of a local day, a value reset to zero, a day without data) are identical. Expected values are frozen in tests/fixtures/energy/.
  • Devices: ENERGY_LINKY_DEVICE, ENERGY_SOLAR_DEVICE, ENERGY_PAC_DEVICE (defaults consommation, prod, PAC-CE), read from the configuration. The computation lives in dominet_automation::energy, generic over the repositories.
  • Who runs it: the system job compute_daily_energy of the scheduler (00:05 local, ADR 0033), which computes yesterday (local day) or args.date; dominet aggregate-energy [--days N | --date YYYY-MM-DD] to catch up. Recomputing replaces.
  • dominet seed-energy adds (without removing anything) to the three devices' tracked keys those the computation needs, and the live powers shown by the Grafana energy dashboard: without history of these keys the balance stays at zero and nothing says so. A missing device is reported, not created.
  • Deliberate deviation: the last N days. The reference returned the first 30 recorded balances: the page froze after thirty days. EnergyRepo::recent(n) returns the last n, oldest to newest.
  • API GET /api/energy/?days=N (signed-in account; 30 by default, 365 at most, unreadable = 30) as {"data": [...]} with computed linky_total_wh and net_wh.
  • Page /automation/energy: four live cards (solar production pac and qdy of the day, Linky consumption PAPP and PTEC, heat pump power_ab, net balance = production − consumption − heat pump with "surplus" / "deficit") fed by the device:<id> topics; 7 / 14 / 30 / 90 day ranges; a table, most recent first. Today's production is shown in kWh.
  • Server-computed SVG chart (dominet_domain::energy::chart_svg, tested): solar / Linky / heat pump bars and a net-balance curve, "round" ticks (1, 2, 5 × 10ⁿ), a negative axis when a day is in deficit, tooltips (<title>). No script, no style attribute (CSP): inserted through inner_html of a text fully produced by the server from numbers and dates.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Without key tracking (seed-energy) or history, the page says so and offers the two commands.
  • The current day's balance only exists after 00:05: the page shows "today" only live.
  • Any day can be recomputed with aggregate-energy.

docs.title: 0037 — Android relay and messaging: data model
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-06

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The Android relay (a phone sends received SMS and call events, receives SMS to send) and internal messaging (one message, several recipients, e-mail and/or SMS) are needed. The tables message, message_recipient, android_device, sms_message, call_log exist from the first phase. The Kotlin application must not change.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Clear-text token: a database leak gives access to all devices.
  • Token fingerprint: only the SHA-256 fingerprint is stored; the clear value is shown at creation or regeneration only.
  • SMS acknowledgements: reuse sms_message.id (browser SMS) and message_recipient.id (messaging) as the protocol's message_id — ambiguous, two identifier spaces.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• android_device.token (UUID) is replaced by token_hash (hexadecimal SHA-256, 64 characters, unique). The token is produced by gen_random_uuid() in SQL, the fingerprint too: the clear value only travels in the creation / regeneration answer. A malformed token in the address (canonical_token) is treated as unknown.
  • sms_outbox queue: an SMS requested from a device has its own identifier, which becomes the message_id of send_sms and comes back in sms_sent_ack. The origin is exactly one of: a browser SMS (sms_message_id) or a messaging recipient (message_recipient_id) (constraint sms_outbox_one_origin). An acknowledgement only changes the pending rows of the device that sends it: another device, an unknown identifier or a second acknowledgement have no effect. pending rows older than the delay (60 s) become failed (expire).
  • Call log (plan_call, pure): ringing / outgoing create; missed / ended close the open call of the same number, or create an already finished entry; answered and unknown states do nothing. Deliberate deviation from the reference: the most recent open call is closed (the reference took the oldest).
  • Messaging: states pending / sent / failed / na per channel and recipient (initial_statuses: pending only if the channel is requested and the contact detail exists); the message becomes sent when no send is pending any more (finish_if_complete, atomic).
  • Protocol in dominet_domain::android (pure, tested against frames taken from the Kotlin code, tests/fixtures/android/frames.json): parse_device_frame applies the reference's defaults; unreadable JSON is ignored.
  • Ports: AndroidDeviceRepo, SmsRepo, CallRepo, SmsOutboxRepo, MessageRepo; adapters PgAndroidDevices, PgSms, PgCalls, PgSmsOutbox, PgMessages.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The migration is one-way: the clear token exists nowhere any more; losing it means regenerating it (and reconfiguring the phone).
  • Importing devices from another system must compute the fingerprint from the existing token (encode(sha256(convert_to(token::text,'UTF8')),'hex')).
  • Later work adds the WebSocket endpoint, asynchronous messaging and the real channels (SMTP, Free Mobile) on these ports.

docs.title: 0038 — Delivery channels: e-mail (SMTP) and Free Mobile SMS
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-06

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference sent e-mails through a framework mail module (Gmail SMTP) and alert SMS through an HTTP GET on the Free Mobile API, without checking the return code. Both channels are taken over for alerts, messaging and the notification automation action, without ever sending for real during development.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• E-mail: lettre (asynchronous SMTP, rustls); or a sendmail command; or an HTTP call to a third-party service. lettre takes over the usual variables and adds no service.
  • Tests: a third-party simulation crate, or small home-made fake servers on loopback. A home-made fake server records exactly what is received and also serves the demonstration.
  • What is set where: everything in the environment, or everything in settings. The SMTP server (host, password) is an installation matter; the sender, the recipient and the Free Mobile credentials already exist as settings modifiable without a restart.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• dominet-notify crate (no database or interface): SmtpSender (lettre, plain UTF-8 text, one connection per message, configurable timeout) and FreeMobile (reqwest, GET ?user&pass&msg, 160 characters, 5 s). The server adaptations live in dominet_server::notify::Channels.
  • Environment: EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT, EMAIL_HOST_USER, EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD, EMAIL_USE_TLS (default true), EMAIL_USE_SSL, EMAIL_TIMEOUT_SECS (10), SMS_FREE_URL. Settings (already in the registry): DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL, EMAIL_RECIPIENT (the sender by default), SMS_FREE_USER, SMS_FREE_KEY (encrypted secret).
  • Encryption without fallback: STARTTLS is mandatory (a connection that does not obtain it fails, nothing is sent in clear); direct TLS with EMAIL_USE_SSL; TLS and SSL together are a configuration error. Credentials without TLS are only accepted towards loopback: the configuration is refused at start-up otherwise.
  • No secret in output: Debug masks the password and the key; HTTP errors are written without the address (without_url, since the key is in the address); redirects are refused so the key does not follow.
  • Deliberate deviations from the reference: Free Mobile's HTTP code is checked (400, 402, 403, 500 explained); a line break in a subject becomes a space.
  • Fake servers (dominet_notify::testing, feature testing): FakeSmtp (EHLO, AUTH PLAIN / LOGIN, MAIL / RCPT / DATA, configurable refusals, no STARTTLS) and FakeFreeMobile (configurable HTTP code). No test, nor the demonstration, contacts a real SMTP server or Free Mobile.
  • dominet notify-test --email [--to] --sms: a real send of a test message, the only real path, run by the user.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• STARTTLS / TLS encryption is not exercised by the tests (the fake server is in clear): it is by notify-test on the user's side; the tests only check that it is required.
  • A change of EMAIL_* needs a restart; a settings change is picked up at the next send (no cache).
  • Later work (alerts, messaging, the notification action) calls Channels; the Notifier port keeps its interface.

docs.title: 0039 — Android relay, server side: endpoint, presence, orders and events
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-07

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The Kotlin application (unchanged) opens /ws/android/device/<token>/, sends sms_received, call_event, sms_sent_ack, understands auth_ok, send_sms, pong and ignores the rest. The schema and protocol are laid down (ADR 0037); the endpoint, the "online" presence, order sending, and a way to notify browsers are needed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Exact endpoint: /ws/android/device/{token}/, with no cookie or Origin (the application sends none). Malformed or unknown token: the WebSocket opens then closes with code 4001 (the reference refused before accepting; for the application, which reconnects after 5 s in both cases, it is identical). A malformed token does not touch the database. The token is never logged: the path is masked (/ws/android/device/***/) in access logs and CSRF refusals (web::loggable_path).
  • One connection per device: a new one replaces the old one (closed with 4009). "Offline" is only set when the current connection closes: a phone that reconnects before the old line is detected dead does not flicker offline.
  • Heartbeat: a control frame every 30 s; 90 s without any frame received (OkHttp answers every ping by itself): close 4408. At start-up of the web role every device goes back offline (the reference left devices "online" after a hard stop).
  • Frames received: read by dominet_domain::android; unreadable JSON, non-object or unknown type ignored; a frame over 64 KiB: connection cut; empty number: ignored; number, contact and body trimmed to the database bounds (30 / 100 / 5,000 characters) rather than refused. A JSON ping receives pong.
  • Orders (AndroidRelay): send_sms puts a row in sms_outbox then pushes send_sms {to, body, message_id} where message_id is that row's identifier; device offline: refusal without recording anything; a row sent into the void: marked failed at once. push_alert sends alert_notification to all connected devices (the current application ignores it). An acknowledgement only counts for the pending row of its device.
  • Acknowledgement delay: a task sweeps every 10 s the rows without acknowledgement for 60 s and fails them ("no acknowledgement from the device"); a late acknowledgement has no effect. For a messaging recipient, the acknowledgement (or failure) updates its SMS status then the message state.
  • Browsers: topic android:<id> of the existing WebSocket (WsServerMsg::Android { device_id, event }, events device_status, sms_received, call_event, sms_sent_ack in the reference's message format). Presence is retained by the hub (a subscriber receives it at once). Subscription reserved to the owner or an administrator; an unknown device and another's device get the same refusal. No /ws/android/browser/<id>/ (no external client).
  • Call in progress: for answered or an unknown state nothing is written but browsers see the open call (like the reference); the empty call the reference broadcast when no call exists is not rebroadcast.

docs.title: Verification against the reference
docs.text: The reference consumer was run once on 21 sessions of the application; tests/fixtures/android/oracle.json keeps the frames returned, the state of SMS and calls, and the events broadcast; crates/dominet/tests/android_oracle.rs replays them against the Rust server and requires the same results. Known gaps, outside these sessions: the most recent open call closed, an empty number ignored, the reference consumer crashes on JSON that is not an object ([1], 42) whereas Rust ignores it, acknowledgements matched through the queue (the reference broadcast any message_id, even unknown; its identifiers collided), dates without a zone not handled (the application always sends an offset).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The Android pages and messaging only have to call AndroidRelay::send_sms, read the android:<id> topic and the database.
  • One device per connection; if a second phone used the same token they would disconnect each other in a loop (every device has its own token).
  • The 60 s delay and the heartbeat are constants (overridable in tests through AndroidRelay::new(Timing)).

docs.title: 0040 — Android pages: rights, token shown once, live update
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-07

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The relay (ADR 0039) receives SMS and calls; the pages that show them (/android/…), device registration and SMS sending from the browser are needed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Four pages: dashboard /android, devices /android/devices, SMS /android/sms?device=N, call log /android/calls?device=N. Operations (add, delete, new token, send) are server functions, not confirmation pages: deletion asks for confirmation in place.
  • Rights: any signed-in account adds its devices and sees its own; an administrator sees all devices (repositories take Option<UserId>, None = all). A device that is not the account's is "not found" (the same answer as an unknown identifier), for pages, sending, deletion and new token.
  • Token shown once: only creation and regeneration return it (NewAndroidDeviceDto, whose Debug masks the token); no list, no reload page contains it. A banner shows it with the address to enter and a "hide" button.
  • Live: pages follow the android:<id> topics of their devices; each event increments a counter (Realtime::android) that restarts the page's read. A simple choice: reread instead of merging events (100 rows at most, light queries), so the screen always equals the database.
  • Sending: the device must be connected (otherwise refusal, nothing recorded); the outgoing SMS is recorded, put in the queue (sms_outbox) then handed to the device; other tabs receive SmsQueued. The page shows each outgoing SMS's state (pending, sent, failed with its reason) read from the queue; without acknowledgement after 60 s: failed.
  • Read at display: opening the SMS page marks the device's received SMS as read. No purge, 100 rows per page.
  • Validation: field by field (device name and number; recipient, message).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• tests/ui.rs: rights per account, validation, token returned once (and absent from lists), read marking, deletion, regeneration.
  • android_ws.rs: an SMS written in the browser reaches the application and its state follows the acknowledgement (sent, failed with reason).
  • End-to-end tests/e2e/android.py with a simulated phone (tools/sim_android.py: a standard-library WebSocket client, same JSON frames as the Kotlin application, answering control frames like OkHttp): add from the interface, presence, SMS and calls live, sending with acknowledgement and failure, refusal when offline, new token (the old one is cut with 4001), deletion.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The address to enter in the application is ws://host/ws/android/device/<token>/; wss:// comes with TLS.
  • A page rereads at every event: if volume became large, events would be merged in the browser.

docs.title: 0041 — Messaging: asynchronous sending, live statuses, rights
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-07

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Internal messaging (one message, several accounts, e-mail and/or SMS) exists in the reference with synchronous sending: the request waits for each e-mail, and an SMS stays "pending" without a maximum delay. The channels (ADR 0038), the Android relay (ADR 0039) and the data model (ADR 0037) exist.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Synchronous, like the reference: simple, but the page blocks while the SMTP answers (up to 10 s per recipient) and nothing is visible before the end.
  • Asynchronous with a database queue and a worker: robust to restarts, but heavy for a few messages a month.
  • Asynchronous in a background task (chosen): the message and its recipients are saved in one transaction, then a tokio task does the sends.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Sending (dominet_server::messaging::send): creates the message (sending) and one recipient per account with initial_statuses (pending only if the channel is requested and the account has the address / mobile, otherwise na — a deliberate deviation from the reference, which marked "failed: no address"), then hands back control. The detail page opens at once.
  • Background task: one send at a time for the whole server (global lock); for each recipient, the e-mail goes through Channels::send_email (subject = the message's subject, plain text), then the SMS is handed to the most recently seen online Android device, of any owner (like the reference). Without a device: sms: no Android device connected; device dropped meanwhile: sms: device unreachable. An e-mail failure is written email: <reason>.
  • SMS: stays pending until the application's acknowledgement, or up to 60 s (ADR 0039, expire_stale). Settlement goes through android::settled, which updates the recipient and closes the message.
  • End: the message becomes sent (with sent_at) as soon as nothing is pending (finish_if_complete, atomic). sent means "processed", not "all succeeded": the table says what failed.
  • Audience: all (active accounts), staff (active administrators), plus chosen accounts; cumulative without duplicates (resolve_audience). An inactive account chosen explicitly is served (like the reference) but the form only offers active ones.
  • Live: topic message:<id> of the WebSocket (WsServerMsg::MessageProgress { message_id, complete }), published at every processed recipient and every acknowledgement. Allowed to the sender, recipients and administrators; an unknown message and another's message get the same refusal. The browser rereads the page at each event (like the Android pages, ADR 0040). Events are not kept by the hub: the page rereads anyway on opening.
  • Rights: compose and list sent messages = administrators; inbox = any account; detail = sender, recipient or administrator — the sender and administrators see the full table, a recipient only their own state. Unknown or foreign message: "not found".
  • Resume at start-up: a message left sending after a hard stop has its pending sends declared failed ("interrupted by a server restart") then is closed (recover_interrupted), so nothing stays "in progress" indefinitely. It is not known whether the interrupted send went out: failure is the prudent answer, the sender may resend.
  • Pages: /messaging (sent), /messaging/inbox, /messaging/compose, /messaging/<id>; the last 100 messages per list.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• crates/dominet/tests/messaging.rs (6 tests, a fake SMTP and a phone that talks like the application): e-mails received with sender, subject and text; SMS handed over with the right number; statuses before and after the acknowledgement; an SMTP that refuses and no phone; an SMS without acknowledgement failed after 60 s; events up to complete; subscription rights (sender, recipient, administrator, foreign, unknown); resume after restart.
  • Unit: audience composition.
  • End-to-end tests/e2e/messaging.py (31 checks): form refused empty, send, live status tracking with a hand-made acknowledgement, simulated SMTP (tools/sim-smtp.py), the recipient's inbox without the others' table, reserved pages, failure without a phone with its reason.
  • No real send: tests never reach a real SMTP host or Free Mobile.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A server that stops during a send may have sent an e-mail that the database declares failed; resending is safe for the server, but the recipient could receive it twice.
  • Sending is globally serialised: enough for a few recipients, to revisit (bounded queue, limited concurrency) if volumes changed.
  • No drafts or attachments (the schema's draft state stays unused).

docs.title: 0042 — Alerts and automation notifications on real channels
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-07

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The Notifier port (ADR 0035) was laid down: a fired alert produces a banner, its three channels (e-mail, SMS, Android) are recorded but not served, notified stays false. The channels (ADR 0038) and the Android relay (ADR 0039) are now delivered.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Alerts: AlertNotifier (dominet_server::alerts) replaces UiNotifier. On fired: the banner goes at once, then a background task serves the rule's channels — e-mail to the alert recipient (EMAIL_RECIPIENT, the sender by default) with the subject [DomiNet Alert <severity>] <rule> and the long text; Free Mobile SMS with the short text (160 characters); an alert_notification push to all online Android devices. Alert evaluation never waits for a send.
  • Isolation: each channel is tried even if another fails; an unconfigured channel (no SMTP, no Free Mobile credentials) is skipped with an information message, a real failure is logged (never the secret). notified becomes true after the attempt, failures or not; failures are not retried (the rule's repeat delay takes care of it).
  • Android push kept although the current application ignores it ("Message ignored"): it is compatible with a future version, and the rules interface says so (a note under the checkbox).
  • Free Mobile HTTP code checked (the reference ignored it): a refusal is a logged failure.
  • Automation notification: the notification action keeps the banner and also sends an e-mail to the alert recipient (subject [DomiNet] Notification) and, if the automation ticks "SMS", a Free Mobile SMS (Channels::notify). A channel that fails does not prevent the other.
  • No real send: tests and the demonstration use the fake SMTP, the fake Free Mobile and a simulated phone.

docs.title: Before a first real use
docs.text: Automations that have a notification action (and alerts whose e-mail / SMS boxes are ticked) will really send messages as soon as the server is connected to a real SMTP and real credentials: check with dominet notify-test, run by yourself.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• crates/dominet/tests/alert_channels.rs (5 tests): the real alert engine fires, the e-mail (sender, recipient, subject, text), the SMS (credentials, short text) and the push received by a connected phone are exactly the expected ones; only the rule's channels serve; e-mail refused: the SMS goes and notified becomes true; an unconfigured channel skipped; automation notification (SMS only if requested, failure reported).
  • End-to-end: the alert e-mail received by the simulated SMTP and the alert marked notified, on the Docker image.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• An alert whose send fails is not replayed: only the next firing (after the rule's delay) retries.
  • Channels is in AppState: any future notification (Prometheus alerts) uses it as is.

docs.title: 0043 — Surveillance schema: cameras, recordings, events
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-07

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Surveillance covers cameras, PTZ presets, recordings, snapshots, motion events, detection events and the detector configuration.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Seven tables, with CHECK constraints that repeat the domain's rules (ports, fps, priority, enumerations, confidence in [0, 1]): the database refuses what the domain refuses. Deleting a camera: everything that belongs to it goes in cascade; deleting a place: the camera is detached (SET NULL).
  • Public identifier: camera.uuid, a UUID drawn by the database (gen_random_uuid()), displayed as 32 hexadecimal characters (CameraUuid). It is the MediaMTX path name and the widget key (camera_uuid, without a foreign key). The numeric key stays the internal foreign key.
  • Secrets: RTSP password, ONVIF password, web password and web API key are stored encrypted (*_enc, the v1: format of ADR 0011). The domain only sees a Sealed (already encrypted text, masked Debug): encryption and decryption are done by the server (SecretBox, associated data specific to the camera and the field), never by the repository. URLs that contain a password only exist in memory (source_url); masked_source_url is the only one that is displayed or logged.
  • Repositories: one port per aggregate (CameraRepo, PtzPresetRepo, RecordingRepo, SnapshotRepo, EventRepo for motions and detections, DetectorConfigRepo). Recording follows pending → uploading → done | error; list_unarchived returns what remains to push (resume after a stop). detector_config is a singleton (id = 1) created by the migration.
  • Free fields: the stream path refuses spaces and @, the host only allows letters, digits, ., -, : — they enter a URL passed to MediaMTX and ffmpeg.
  • Choices: segment duration in milliseconds (duration_ms); YOLO classes as TEXT[]; detection labels as JSONB validated as an array; preset positions position.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A camera imported from another system will have secrets to encrypt and a new identifier.
  • Changing DOMINET_MASTER_KEY makes camera secrets unreadable, like those of settings (ADR 0011): the camera stays, the passwords must be entered again.

docs.title: 0044 — MediaMTX client and camera administration
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-07

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference created a MediaMTX path per active camera through the REST API and rewrote mediamtx.yml so the configuration survived a restart. Decisions needed: secrets, identifier, synchronisation, rights.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• dominet-surveillance::mediamtx client (reqwest, 5 s timeout): paginated list, read, add, replace, remove, and sync (create or replace each wanted path, delete the paths of our cameras that are no longer wanted). Only the names of 32 hexadecimal characters are ours: the ~.* of the configuration and any other path are never touched.
  • replace rather than patch: it replaces the whole configuration, so an option removed from a camera (forced TCP, recording) disappears from the path. Checked on MediaMTX 1.21.3: replace creates the path if missing, delete of an absent path answers 404 (treated as a success).
  • No rewriting of mediamtx.yml: the API alone. A restarted MediaMTX loses the paths added live; the database is authoritative and the web server reruns a full synchronisation at start-up (and the administration button on demand). In production, the YAML is generated from the database by the deployment. Known limit: if MediaMTX restarts alone, its cameras are missing until the next synchronisation.
  • Source = secret: the source URL contains the camera's password. PathConf does not show its source in Debug, MediaMTX errors are cleaned of it, and nothing is logged.
  • CameraService (server): encrypts secrets with the associated data camera:<uuid>:<field> (the public identifier is drawn before insertion, since it binds the encryption), keeps a secret left empty on modification, reuses the RTSP credentials for ONVIF if missing, keeps what ONVIF synchronisation learned (manufacturer, model, profile, PTZ). A camera whose secret is unreadable (master key changed) is not removed from MediaMTX by mistake.
  • A MediaMTX failure does not undo the save: the database is authoritative, the failure is logged and sync_all catches up.
  • Configuration: MEDIAMTX_API_URL, optional; without it nothing is synchronised and the administration says so.
  • Rights: /surveillance (viewing) for any signed-in account; /admin/cameras (CRUD, synchronisation) and the matching server functions for administrators. The viewing page exposes neither IP address, path nor credentials.
  • Fake MediaMTX (dominet_surveillance::testing, feature testing): the configuration API in memory, with simulated failure, modelled on the verified behaviour of the real one. A test ignored by default (real_mediamtx) replays the client against the development stack's MediaMTX.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Live view, snapshots, ONVIF and PTZ are added on these same cameras.
  • A camera password can only be entered with a configured master key.

docs.title: 0045 — ONVIF, discovery and adding cameras
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-07

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference speaks ONVIF with a Python library, discovers cameras through a small separate HTTP server in host network (port 8765) and creates a record for every device found, before the user has chosen. ADR 0008: a hand-written SOAP client. Decisions: discovery, no contact with a production installation.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Client (dominet_surveillance::onvif): GetSystemDateAndTime, GetDeviceInformation, GetCapabilities, GetProfiles, GetStreamUri. Answers read without regard to name prefixes (the four camera families use different ones). WS-Security PasswordDigest with correction of the camera's clock (read without authentication first); no connection reused (Thingino closes it).
  • Service addresses keep the registered camera's host: only the port and path announced by GetCapabilities are taken. A camera behind address translation sometimes announces its own; above all, an answer must not be able to send us to another host.
  • Secrets: Credentials and StreamUri show nothing in Debug. The NVT camera's stream URL contains the password in clear: mask_secrets hides it by pattern (user:***@, password=***) and by known value (a password containing _ would otherwise be cut too early); only the masked form leaves the module.
  • Synchronisation (onvif_sync): the first profile is the main profile and PTZ = presence of the PTZ service; ONVIF credentials, otherwise the stream's. Results are saved without touching entered settings.
  • Adding by address (add_by_ip): the ONVIF port is searched among 80, 8080, 8899, 2020, 8000, but an open port is not enough: it must answer GetSystemDateAndTime. An already known address returns the existing record. With credentials, the camera is synchronised at once (a failure does not cancel the addition).
  • Discovery (deviation from the reference): results are listed with an "Add" button, instead of creating a record per device. A device already registered at this address is flagged.
  • WS-Discovery: 3 probes one second apart, 6 s of listening, outgoing interface by the default route, one announcement per address. The discovery role (host network) and the web role do not call each other: they go through PostgreSQL (LISTEN/NOTIFY, channels onvif_discovery_request / onvif_discovery_result), which replaces the reference's HTTP server without a new port. The web role relays results to the discovery WebSocket topic (administrators only), after marking addresses already registered. Without a discovery role: the interface says so after five seconds.
  • No discovery by default: dominet serve does not start the discovery role (it needs host network); dominet serve --only discovery.
  • Verification: a fake ONVIF server checks the digest and the clock like a camera (4 families of answers); a fake WS-Discovery responder answers unicast on loopback (CI never does multicast). The answers of fixtures/onvif/ are reconstructed from the spike (no secret, no real address). Two tests ignored by default confront them with real cameras (real_onvif, read-only) when an access file is present.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A camera that multicast does not see (one model) is added by its address.
  • PTZ, imaging and the onvif night mode reuse this client.
  • The discovery role needs database access: it uses it as a message channel.

docs.title: 0046 — Camera live view: Rust/WASM WHEP player
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-08

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0010: the browser negotiates a WebRTC session with MediaMTX through WHEP; this work makes it an application feature: live page, dashboard widget, reconnection, camera:<uuid> WebSocket topic. Decisions: browsers without H.264, rights.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Player (dominet_web::live::WhepPlayer, client in whep.rs, web-sys): recvonly offer, ICE gathering (2 s at most), POST application/sdp, track attached to the <video>; on close, DELETE of the session resource (Location header), so MediaMTX releases the connection at once. The decision part is pure and tested on the machine (StallDetector, failure_for_status).
  • Reconnection through getStats: a read every 2 s; no new decoded frame for 8 s (15 s for the first, the time of a key frame) → session closed and restarted, with the WebSocket's growing delay (1 s doubling up to 30 s, plus 25 % random). The player says what it does: "connecting", "stream lost: reconnecting", "no stream".
  • Browser without H.264: RTCRtpReceiver.getCapabilities is queried before any attempt; without H.264, an explicit message (and the names of suitable browsers) replaces the silent failure. If MediaMTX answers 400 to a browser without H.264, the same message. Fallback through refreshed snapshots: deferred (it needs snapshots).
  • WHEP address: <MEDIAMTX_WEBRTC_SCHEME>://<MEDIAMTX_WEBRTC_DOMAIN>/<uuid>/whep: if the configured domain is a host of the instance itself (ALLOWED_HOSTS without localhost, 127.0.0.1, wildcards), it is replaced by the host through which the browser arrived, scheme, port and path kept (dominet_domain::public_url, tested). A scheme other than http / https is refused.
  • CSP: connect-src adds MediaMTX's origin when it differs from the page's; in production, behind nginx /webrtc/ (same origin), nothing to add. The page opens no other origin.
  • Rights: any signed-in account watches an active camera (camera_live, page /surveillance/live/<uuid>, camera widget). An inactive or unknown camera gets the same answer. The browser never receives the source stream's address or a credential: only MediaMTX's WHEP address.
  • camera:<uuid> WebSocket topic: accepted for any signed-in account if the camera exists and is active (same refusal for an unknown and an inactive camera); events (motion, detection) arrive later. The topic stays written with the dashed UUID, the contract's canonical form, while the camera's public identifier is written as 32 hexadecimal characters.
  • Widget: WidgetDto.camera; one <video> per display (instance tells two widgets of the same camera apart); an unknown or inactive camera shows "camera not found or inactive".

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• End-to-end test with a real H.264 stream (tests/e2e/live.py, in make e2e): ffmpeg publishes an H.264 test pattern into the development MediaMTX, the camera pulls it, and headless Chromium (DevTools protocol, websockets) opens the page: "live" state, 640×360 resolution, playing time that advances, statistics displayed; the stream is cut (the player reports it) then restored (it reconnects by itself); leaving the page closes the session at MediaMTX. Debian's Firefox ESR (no H.264) shows the explicit message. Without Chromium, ffmpeg or websockets, the script says so and only checks the Firefox part.
  • Rust tests: WHEP address (own hosts), CSP, page and server function (rights, inactive camera, no secret), WebSocket topic, widget.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Headless Chromium validates the network path and decoding; the look and smoothness are judged in your browser.
  • End-to-end latency with a real camera is not measured here (the test pattern is encoded locally); it depends on the camera's GOP (ADR 0010).
  • The development WASM (48 MB) delays hydration: the player starts when the page is hydrated (RELEASE=1 make dev-run).

docs.title: 0047 — PTZ control and day / night switching
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-08

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference drives PTZ through a WebSocket (ONVIF ContinuousMove / Stop, presets in the database) and controls day / night, IR-cut and light through four methods (OpenIPC, Thingino, ONVIF, Goform). ADR 0008: the ONVIF client. Decisions: rights, methods tested against fake servers.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• ONVIF PTZ (dominet_surveillance::onvif::ptz): PtzControl reads once the PTZ service address and the token of the first profile that carries a PTZ configuration (the one the spike validated on the cameras), then ContinuousMove (only the axes in motion are sent; all zero = a Stop), Stop, GetStatus (position, coordinate space, MoveStatus), presets (GetPresets, SetPreset, RemovePreset, GotoPreset at half speed) and AbsoluteMove in the space announced by the camera (Thingino: degrees; the default would be [-1, 1]), waiting for the end of the movement (8 s at most). Speeds are brought into 0.05..1 (an unreadable value never produces a movement).
  • WebSocket /ws/surveillance/ptz/<uuid>/: the reference's protocol, unchanged (move, zoom, stop, get_presets, set_preset, remove_preset, goto_preset; answers presets and error, plus a ready the reference did not have). Deliberate deviations:
  • administrators only — the reference let any signed-in account in; refusal before opening (session, role, origin, unknown / inactive / PTZ-less camera);
  • automatic stop of a movement not refreshed (PTZ_DEAD_MAN_SECS, 8 s) in addition to the stop on close: a frozen tab does not leave a camera turning to the end stop (some have no software stop, see ADR 0008);
  • a preset of the same name replaces the old one and removes the camera's old token (the reference left it orphan); the database stays the source of truth; a preset without a token is reached by AbsoluteMove to its saved position.
  • Interface (/surveillance/live/<uuid>, administrators): a direction cross (a held direction resends its order every 250 ms, stop on release, when leaving the button and if the pointer is interrupted), zoom, two speeds, presets; link resumed every 1.5 s if it drops. Buttons only appear if the camera has PTZ and a day / night method.
  • Day / night (dominet_surveillance::night, NightControl trait, four methods):
  • openipc: GET /night/<toggle|light> (daynight and ircut go to toggle, which activates the right engine pin);
  • thingino: POST /x/json-imp.cgi, X-API-Key, toggle remembered per camera and per action (24 h: the camera does not reread its state);
  • onvif: GetImagingSettings → a single field changed → SetImagingSettings of the complete object (a partial object resets the other settings); AUTO and DAY go to NIGHT, NIGHT to DAY; the light toggles brightness between 0 and 80;
  • goform: JSON {Type: 1, Data}, X-Digest authentication (a challenge without body, then an MD5 answer with qop=auth); only DayNightMode (or Control for the light) changes, ModeSupportList is not sent back. Web credentials, otherwise the stream's.
  • Command through the camera_night server function: administrators, active camera only. No error contains a secret.
  • Verification: a stateful fake ONVIF (position, speed, presets, image settings, MOVING delay), fake OpenIPC, fake Thingino (API key), fake Goform (the Digest challenge); the Digest computation is compared with a value computed separately; a real WebSocket end to end (rights, origin, speeds, automatic stop, presets, AbsoluteMove in the camera's space); a Firefox end-to-end test against a simulated ONVIF camera that logs every order (tests/e2e/ptz.py).

docs.title: Consequences / limits
docs.text:
• goform has no test camera: its conformity rests on the reference read, on the verified Digest computation and on a fake server; to confirm on matching hardware.
  • One camera model never gives its position (GetStatus returns 0, 0): a preset saved on it has position 0, 0 and a camera token (it works by token, not by position).
  • Trials on real cameras (PTZ, IR-cut) are done with an access file kept outside the repository; no order was sent to a real camera.

docs.title: 0048 — Decoded frames (FrameSource) and snapshots
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-08

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Snapshots, motion detection and YOLO need decoded images; ADR 0003 chose a long-lived ffmpeg per camera. The reference started a cold ffmpeg per camera and per round (60 s) for the latest image, and another for each capture (2 to 4 s of waiting). Decisions: browsers without H.264, a single FrameSource at 2 frames/s.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• FrameSource (dominet_surveillance::frames): a trait (latest, subscribe) and one implementation, a supervised ffmpeg per camera reading MediaMTX's re-stream (<MEDIAMTX_RTSP_URL>/<uuid>) and writing JPEGs to its output (fps=2, width 1280 at most and never enlarged, -q:v 5). A JPEG carries its dimensions (ADR 0003: ONVIF sometimes gets the resolution wrong) and serves as a snapshot as is; motion detection and YOLO decode it. Splitting the JPEG stream is tested byte by byte (packets of 1 byte up to the whole stream, a stream cut in the middle of an image).
  • Supervision: restart with a doubling delay from 1 to 30 s (reset to 1 s after 10 s of running), restart of a stream that gives no image for 20 s, a single decoding thread (the bottleneck is the processor). Opportunistic hardware decoding: VAAPI (hwdownload then software scale, ADR 0003) if /dev/dri/renderD128 exists; if ffmpeg stops without having produced anything and its error output blames the hardware (VAAPI, /dev/dri, hwdownload, unimplemented function…), immediate fallback to software, for good. Later fix: the first version switched as soon as ffmpeg stopped without an image, so also when the camera was offline, its stream not yet published or joined mid-GOP (the hardware decoder then lacks its reference frames); now only a device error condemns VAAPI at once, and a hardware decoding error only after three failures in a row; measurement on the target machine revealed it (VAAPI works there and divides the decoding cost by three, see Measurements). FFMPEG_HWACCEL=off turns it off. VAAPI decoding is not exercised by the tests (CI has no GPU): its command chain is checked, its operation remains to be measured on real hardware.
  • video role: follows the list of active cameras (reread at every signalled change and every 30 s), one ffmpeg per camera; dominet serve starts it when MEDIAMTX_RTSP_URL is set (otherwise --only video).
  • Latest image on disk: the video role writes <SNAPSHOTS_DIR>/latest/<uuid>.jpg at most once a second, atomically (temporary file then rename; a reader never sees a truncated image). It is the interface with the web role, which may be another process (separate containers, shared volume): no image transfer through the database or the network. An image older than a minute is not served (the camera sends nothing any more); neither is a file that is not a complete JPEG.
  • On-demand snapshot: no cold ffmpeg. ?force=1 and the capture wait for an image newer than the request (4 s at most, one per second in practice); failing that, the latest still-recent image. Route kept: GET /surveillance/camera/<uuid>/snapshot/ (any signed-in account; 204 if there is no recent image; no-store); ?save=1 and the "Take a picture" button of the live page: administrators.
  • Gallery (/surveillance/snapshots, any signed-in account; deletion: administrators): database rows (snapshot) and files <uuid>/<timestamp>.jpg; filter by camera and by day (read in the TZ zone, a 23-hour day at the clock change); 200 at most. Additions: a cap SNAPSHOTS_MAX_PER_CAMERA (500) — beyond it the oldest are deleted with their file —; the files of a deleted camera go with it.
  • Fallback without H.264: a browser that does not decode H.264 in WebRTC shows, instead of the video, the camera image refreshed every second and a banner explaining why. The file read is the video role's image: without it, the image stays empty and the banner says so.
  • Security: the path of a file read comes from the database; it is refused if it contains anything but simple components (.., root). File names are produced by the application (public identifier and timestamp).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Real ffmpeg on lavfi sources: cadence (5 frames/s requested → 5 frames/s measured), width reduced then never enlarged, complete JPEGs, restart of a source that stops (numbering continues), cause of a failure and missing binary, process stopped on destruction. video role: an active camera has its source and latest image, an inactive one not, a disabled camera loses both; writing at most once a second, never a truncated file read.
  • Snapshots: cap and file deletion, filter by day, deleted camera, rights, ?force=1, ?save=1.
  • End-to-end (tests/e2e/live.py, real H.264 stream through ffmpeg → MediaMTX → video role): latest image at 640×360, fresh image, capture, file, gallery, deletion, and the fallback in Firefox (no H.264) with an image that renews itself.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Tests without ffmpeg (another machine) skip the check with a message; the Docker image embeds it and make ci-full exercises it.
  • One ffmpeg per active camera runs permanently (≈ 3 % of a core per 720p stream in software at 2 frames/s, measurements of ADR 0003).

docs.title: 0049 — Camera recording, ReductStore archive and replay
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-08

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference had MediaMTX record (record: true on the path of cameras in continuous or motion mode, or after a manual start), scanned /recordings every 60 s, created a Recording per segment, pushed the whole file to the ReductStore bucket surveillance (entry cam_<uuid>, labels event_type, ASCII camera_name, camera_uuid, a 50 GB FIFO quota) and served the local file, failing that ReductStore. The local file was never deleted (the volume grew without limit) and the last file of each camera was always ignored. Criterion: "1 hour of continuous recording without losing a segment".

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• MediaMTX records, DomiNet writes no video. PathConf already carries record (continuous and motion: true); the format (fmp4), the path (/recordings/%path/%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S-%f), the segment duration and the part (1s) are MediaMTX's global configuration (development: 10 s; production: 60 s).
  • Scan (dominet_surveillance::recording): a segment is finished when its file has not been modified for RECORDINGS_GRACE_SECS (15 s). Deliberate deviation: the reference always ignored the last file, so the last segment of a camera whose recording stops was never taken; here the modification date is enough, all segments are. Start date read from the name (MediaMTX's %f = microseconds; read by hand), failing that the modification date.
  • video role (dominet_server::recordings): every RECORDINGS_SCAN_SECS — indexes the finished segments of active cameras that record (mode ≠ none), then archives. Segment type: manual in manual mode, motion if a motion falls in its window (RECORDINGS_SEGMENT_DURATION), otherwise continuous. A segment already indexed (unique path in the database) is never indexed twice.
  • Archive (dominet_store::video::ReductVideo): bucket surveillance (REDUCTSTORE_VIDEO_BUCKET), entry cam_<uuid>, timestamp in microseconds, labels as above (NFKD then ASCII for camera_name), FIFO quota VIDEO_QUOTA_GB at bucket creation. Deliberate deviation: the local file is deleted after a successful push, the volume no longer grows. A failing push (ReductStore down) notes the error on the segment (status = error), keeps the file and retries at every pass; without REDUCTSTORE_URL segments stay on disk (pending) and are served from it.
  • Replay: GET /surveillance/recordings/<uuid>/<id>/stream/ (any signed-in account). Local file if it still exists (tower_http::ServeFile: Range, native seek), otherwise the segment is read from ReductStore and served with the same Range support (206, Content-Range, 416). A path in the database outside RECORDINGS_DIR is never served. Page /surveillance/recordings/<uuid>: one day at a time (server zone, local hours), a native <video> player, previous / next; deletion: administrators (file, ReductStore entry, row).
  • Manual recording: PATCH /v3/config/paths/patch/<uuid> {"record": bool} (MediaMtx::set_record), a Start / Stop button on the recordings page (administrators, camera in manual mode only). A full MediaMTX resynchronisation (start-up, "Synchronise" button) puts the path back to its base state — so it stops a manual recording in progress.
  • Deleted camera: its segment folder is deleted with it, after its path is stopped.
  • Security: paths served or deleted must be under RECORDINGS_DIR without ..; folder identifiers are known camera UUIDs.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Unit: segment name reading (with / without fraction, microseconds), cooled segments only, last segment of a stopped camera taken, unreadable name, Range ranges (start, end, suffix, out of bounds), previous / next days (leap years).
  • Integration (real ReductStore of the development stack, throw-away bucket, real database): indexing by mode, type motion / continuous / manual, push, local file deleted, reread from ReductStore with the exact labels, no duplicate at the next pass, deletion; ReductStore down then back (file kept, error noted, resumed); without archive; path outside the folder refused; manual recording (fake MediaMTX, refusal outside manual mode).
  • End-to-end (tests/e2e/recordings.py, real H.264 stream → development MediaMTX → ReductStore): the path records, segments archived, 200 / 206 / 404, MP4 signature, size matching the index, page, player, manual mode (start and stop, manual segment), deletion.
  • Endurance (tests/e2e/recordings_soak.py, SOAK_SECONDS=3600 tools/e2e.sh recordings_soak): one hour of continuous stream, no gap between consecutive segments, none in error, cumulated duration ≥ 97 % of the published duration, all reread from ReductStore. Result: 3,600 s of continuous stream, the 7 checks pass.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• No 24-hour timeline: list + player. Postponable.
  • motion mode records continuously (only the type distinguishes segments with motion); a motion-triggered recording would be a change of behaviour, to decide.
  • The /recordings volume must be shared by MediaMTX and the video role, and writable by the latter (deletion). In development, MediaMTX runs under the user's identifier (DEV_UID) so files belong to them.

docs.title: 0050 — Motion and object detection
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-08

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The reference (detect_motion_camera, run_yolo_detection, OnnxBackend): for each camera in motion mode, every 30 s, it reopens the stream, reads ~20 frames, compares the first and the last (gray, 21 × 21 blur, absdiff, threshold 25, 5 × 5 opening, pixel ratio > MOTION_THRESHOLD 0.01), creates a MotionEvent, publishes on MQTT, notifies (per-camera delay 600 s) then runs YOLOv8n if the camera enables it (one frame, the camera's classes and confidence, annotated image, DetectionEvent, MQTT, 300 s notification). Decisions: a single FrameSource with a sliding window, the model, measurements.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Motion in pure Rust (dominet_surveillance::motion, no dependency on OpenCV): the same algorithm, with OpenCV's details reproduced (14-bit integer gray, separable blur with reflect-101 borders, σ derived from the kernel size, opening with neutral borders). Parity measured against OpenCV 5 on 8 synthetic image pairs (tests/motion_parity.rs): maximum gap 0.0002 of the ratio (test tolerance 0.0005); same decisions at the 0.01 threshold for every case. OpenCV's 8-bit blur is fixed-point, not reproduced bit for bit.
  • Sliding window: the FrameHub keeps the last 20 images of each camera; every MOTION_INTERVAL_SECS (30), the first and the last are compared — only two images are decoded and blurred. No stream is reopened (the reference: 2 to 4 s of set-up each round). At 2 frames/s the window covers ~10 s (the reference: ~2 s at 10 frames/s), so a slow motion is easier to see; a deliberate deviation, adjustable by the threshold. At least 5 images and a last image younger than 15 s, otherwise no verdict.
  • Consequences of a motion: MotionEvent, MQTT dominet/surveillance/<uuid>/motion (camera_uuid, camera_name, confidence to 4 decimals, timestamp), e-mail + SMS Motion detected — <name> (<place>): x.x% with a per-camera delay MOTION_ALERT_COOLDOWN, then YOLO. The video role publishes through the mqtt role's client if it runs in the process, otherwise through its own (<client_id>-video).
  • YOLO (dominet_surveillance::yolo, ort pinned =2.0.0-rc.15, ADR 0009): same input / output / thresholds as the reference detector (640 × 640, score ≥ 0.10 then NMS 0.45 class-agnostic, the camera's threshold and classes applied afterwards). A session pool with one compute thread (YOLO_WORKERS, default 1), loaded at the first detection (the model does not occupy memory if turned off). Input: the latest FrameSource image (JPEG at most 1280 wide), not a raw stream image like the reference: compression and reduction add a slight gap, negligible for class, box and score (see parity). Parity measured on 4 images (Ultralytics' public bus.jpg sample and three variants: resized, cropped, without object): 17/17 detections of the reference found again (same class, IoU > 0.9, score gap < 0.02), none in excess.
  • Global setting: DetectorConfig (one row; enabled, save_frames, model_path), modified in the interface (/surveillance/events, administrators). Off by default. save_frames: annotated image <uuid>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.jpg in DETECTIONS_DIR, served by GET /surveillance/detections/<id>/frame/ (any signed-in account). Deviation: boxes are drawn, not the text (no embedded font).
  • Events page /surveillance/events (any signed-in account): recent motions and detections (server time), the annotated image when it exists.
  • Model: yolov8n.onnx is not committed; make fetch-model exports it from the official Ultralytics weights in a throw-away container (same version and options as the reference file: ultralytics 8.4.82, opset 12, simplify; licence AGPL-3.0). make image fetches it if absent and the Dockerfile embeds it (/models). Without a model the parity tests say so and verify nothing; detection logs "model unavailable".

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Unit: integer gray, normalised kernel and σ of OpenCV, reflect-101, blur of a flat image and of a point, ratio (squares, specks and thin lines erased by the opening, strict threshold), NMS and box scaling, IoU, pre-processing, annotation, class and confidence filter, per-camera delay.
  • Parity: motion_parity.rs (OpenCV) and yolo_parity.rs (the reference detector).
  • Integration (real ffmpeg, real model, development Mosquitto, fake SMTP): a fixed source (no motion) and an oscillating source (motion, event, MQTT, a single e-mail despite two motions), no window; detector off / YOLO off / unwanted class (nothing), wanted class (event, readable annotated image, MQTT, e-mail), without save_frames (no file).
  • End-to-end events (a real H.264 stream of the bus image, oscillating brightness): quantified motion, "bus" detection with an annotated image served as JPEG, page, detector turned off from the interface.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Load measurements (CPU / RAM, cameras held) are in Measurements: on the target machine, 12 1080p/15 cameras in full mode (recording, archive, motion, YOLO) = 45 % of the machine with VAAPI, 8 cameras = 60 % in software.
  • motion mode still does not trigger recording (see ADR 0049); YOLO only triggers on motion (no periodic sampling, although DetectionTrigger::Periodic exists in the schema).
  • VAAPI decoding and the GPU are not used for YOLO (ADR 0009).

docs.title: Addendum: Docker image
docs.text: The precompiled ONNX Runtime library used by ort is C++: building needs g++, running libstdc++6, and the whole needs glibc ≥ 2.38. The image therefore moves from Debian 12 to Debian 13, identical to the target. Discovered by make ci-full, which had not been rerun after the Dockerfile change.

docs.title: ADR 0051 — Prometheus metrics (/metrics)
docs.text: Status: accepted.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Prometheus must scrape the application (15 s) with rules on up, 5xx errors, p95 latency and task failures, without exposing data to visitors: /metrics is therefore not served on the public port.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. A /metrics route on the public port, protected by a token: one more secret, and one more page behind nginx.
  2. A separate listener (METRICS_ADDR), reached by Prometheus on the Docker network, never published on the host nor proxied.
  3. Library: metrics + metrics-exporter-prometheus (without its built-in listener) or prometheus-client.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Option 2: METRICS_ADDR, default 0.0.0.0:9100, off to disable; a port already taken is reported and does not stop the server (several processes on a development machine). The public router does not know /metrics (404, tested).
  • metrics + metrics-exporter-prometheus without listener: a global recorder installed once (metrics::handle()), the listener is ours.
  • dominet_* names (Prometheus convention): dominet_http_requests_total{method,route,status}, dominet_http_request_duration_seconds (histogram 5 ms to 30 s), dominet_http_requests_in_flight, dominet_ws_connections, dominet_mqtt_messages_received_total, dominet_mqtt_disconnections_total, dominet_mqtt_connected, dominet_scheduler_tasks_total{task,result}, dominet_recordings_total{outcome}, dominet_motion_events_total{camera}, dominet_detection_events_total{camera}, dominet_db_pool_connections{state}, dominet_build_info{version}, dominet_process_start_time_seconds.
  • Bounded labels, nothing sensitive: the route is the route template (MatchedPath) or a fixed family (/sf/*, /pkg/*, /api/*, ui), never the raw URL (identifiers, Android token); no account identifier; the camera is identified by its public UUID. Tested.
  • Pool and MQTT gauges are refreshed every 15 s and just before each read.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Prometheus rules are written on these names (5xx rate → dominet_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}, p95 latency → histogram_quantile on dominet_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket, failed tasks → dominet_scheduler_tasks_total{result="error"}).
  • Each role's process has its own metrics (the dominet-discovery service, in host network, must use METRICS_ADDR=off to expose nothing on the LAN).
  • The metrics library is a simple facade (dominet-mqtt uses it too); without an installed recorder, calls cost almost nothing.

docs.title: ADR 0052 — Prometheus and Grafana alert rules
docs.text: Status: accepted.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Prometheus alert rules (AlertRule) and Grafana rules (GrafanaAlertRule) are database rows edited in the administration; the provisioning files (rules.yml, rules.yaml) are derived from them, then the services are asked to reread them. An alert_rule table already exists in Rust: those are rules on device state, unrelated.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. Rules in the database, editable, files regenerated and services reloaded.
  2. Static versioned files: simpler, but no more online editing.
  3. A single model for both services: the fields differ (raw SQL, no-data / error states, folder).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Option 1, two tables (prometheus_rule, grafana_alert_rule): constraints are repeated as CHECKs (severity, states, uid in [a-z0-9_-]), and also validated by the domain field by field.
  • Documents: prometheus_rules_document / grafana_rules_document (domain, pure functions) build exactly the documents: grouping by group (Prometheus) or (folder, group, interval) (Grafana), group interval = that of the first rule, a source other than prometheus read as raw SQL with a window of at least 60 s. A home-made YAML rendering (blocks, quoted strings): the file reads back like the document.
  • Writing and reloading (RulesService): temporary file then rename (never a half-written file); POST {PROMETHEUS_URL}/-/reload; POST {GRAFANA_URL}/api/admin/provisioning/alerting/reload with the GRAFANA_USER / GRAFANA_PASSWORD account. A refused or unreachable reload is reported, not fatal: the file stays written. Paths and addresses are optional (PROMETHEUS_RULES_PATH, PROMETHEUS_URL, GRAFANA_ALERTING_PATH, GRAFANA_URL); absent, the service is "not configured".
  • When: after every save or deletion in the administration, at start-up of the web role, on demand (page button, dominet sync-rules).
  • Shipped rules: dominet seed creates the default rules (DomiNet's metric names, ADR 0051), only in an empty table: a rule the administrator deleted does not come back. Addition: DominetMqttDown (MQTT client disconnected for 5 min). SchedulerTaskFailureRate covers failed scheduled tasks.
  • dump-context lists the active Grafana rules (sorted by source then uid).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Documents built from varied inputs are frozen in tests/fixtures/observability/; Rust tests replay the same inputs and the YAML files read back identically.
  • MediaMTXNoStreams: an earlier expression (mediamtx_paths == 0) cited a metric that does not exist (observed on MediaMTX 1.21.3, ADR 0053) and so never fired; it becomes (sum(paths{job="mediamtx",state="ready"}) or vector(0)) == 0.
  • Grafana rules on PostgreSQL read device.state: their execution against the schema is checked by the observability test.

docs.title: ADR 0053 — Prometheus alert relay and Grafana dashboards
docs.text: Status: accepted.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Alerts raised by Prometheus must reach the owner by e-mail (and by SMS for critical ones), and Grafana needs dashboards written for the metrics of this application. The relay itself had two defects, and some dashboards cited metrics that do not exist.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Relay (prometheus_alerts, scheduler role, active only if PROMETHEUS_URL is set): every PROMETHEUS_ALERTS_POLL_SECS (60 s), GET /api/v1/alerts. A new firing alert → e-mail "[DomiNet] Alert" + a Free Mobile SMS if critical (the channels of ADR 0038: never a real send outside an explicit request); silence of PROMETHEUS_ALERT_COOLDOWN (3,600 s). The core is a state machine without input-output (clock supplied), hence testable.
  • Two deliberate deviations from the previous behaviour, which were defects:
  • the cache was indexed by fingerprint, a field that Prometheus's alerts API does not provide (it is Alertmanager's): all alerts shared the same key and the second stayed silent for an hour after the first. Rust draws the alert's identity from all its labels.
  • a "RESOLVED" message was planned for the resolved state, which Prometheus never returns (it removes the alert from the list). Rust sends "RESOLVED" (e-mail, never SMS) when a notified alert disappears, or turns resolved. It is one more e-mail per ending alert.
  • Messages keep the format ([DomiNet — FIRING] name (SEVERITY), summary, description), checked pass by pass (pending alert ignored, silence, resolution, missing severity, silence expiry).
  • Grafana dashboards: the six generic dashboards are ported (SQL table and variable names, PromQL expression by expression). Device dashboards (device_<name>) stay produced by the application (ADR 0029). Old MediaMTX names (paths_bytes_received…) become paths_inbound_bytes… (MediaMTX 1.21.3 declares the former obsolete). The weather station is recognised by the state key weather_code. Server function routes (/sf/<point>) become an exact route label when the server knows them (status ≠ 404), which makes the "commands" and "scene activations" panels possible (completes ADR 0051). dominet_scheduler_task_duration_seconds is added for the task duration panel.
  • Provisioning files in deploy/: grafana/provisioning/{datasources,dashboards,alerting} (PostgreSQL and Prometheus sources, e-mail contact point, policy) and prometheus/prometheus.yml (jobs dominet:9100 and mediamtx:9998). Compose mounts them.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Integration test grafana_assets: every SQL query of the dashboards (macros and variables replaced) passes EXPLAIN on DomiNet's schema; every metric cited by a dashboard or shipped rule exists, in metrics::names() or in the real MediaMTX 1.21.3 listing (tests/fixtures/observability/mediamtx-1.21.3.names). This test found mediamtx_paths, a non-existent metric in the MediaMTXNoStreams rule (ADR 0052 corrected).
  • tools/check-observability.sh: real throw-away Prometheus 2.52 and Grafana 11.0 on shifted ports, throw-away database: promtool check rules, rule loading, reload requested by DomiNet accepted by both services, Grafana loads dashboards, sources (real PostgreSQL connection), contact points, policies and alert rules without error, and runs a dashboard SQL query.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: • Rule files must be on a volume shared between dominet (write) and Prometheus / Grafana (read).

docs.title: ADR 0054 — Backups and restore
docs.text: Status: accepted.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A nightly backup (3 am) of the database and of the ReductStore volume, kept 7 days, is worth only what a restore can recover: what matters is being able to restore, not only to back up.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Database: pg_dump (SQL, --clean --if-exists --no-owner --no-privileges), gzipped, written under a temporary name then renamed (never a half-written file). Standard format: restorable by hand (gunzip -c f.sql.gz | psql). The client is in the image (postgresql-client).
  • ReductStore volume: a tar.gz archive of the data folder mounted read-only (REDUCTSTORE_BACKUP_SRC). Accepted limit: consistency is "best effort" while ReductStore writes (it writes immutable blocks then an index); the restore was verified with real records read back by a second ReductStore.
  • Integrity check: each file has its SHA-256 sum beside it (*.sha256, readable by sha256sum -c); a restore verifies it before touching anything.
  • Database password: passed to the PostgreSQL clients through the child process environment (PGPASSWORD), never on the command line (visible in ps).
  • Restore: dominet restore <file>|--latest postgres --yes replays the SQL in a single transaction (ON_ERROR_STOP): a failure does not leave a half-restored database; --yes is mandatory (it replaces the data). restore --latest reductstore --to <folder> extracts the archive (ReductStore stopped; a non-empty folder is refused without --force; paths that escape the target folder are ignored).
  • Line dropped at restore: pg_dump 17 (Debian 13's, in the image) writes SET transaction_timeout = 0;, a parameter unknown to PostgreSQL 16 (the stack's server): the restore would fail. Observed on the real binary; the single SET transaction_timeout… line is removed from the stream (tested).
  • Retention: BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS (7), applied after each backup; the most recent of each kind is never deleted (a long stop of the job must not leave nothing).
  • Scheduling: in the scheduler (scheduler role), every day at BACKUP_HOUR (3, local time, daylight-saving handled), active only if BACKUP_DIR is set. dominet backup triggers it by hand, dominet backups lists, dominet restore restores.
  • Monitoring: metrics dominet_backup_runs_total{result}, …_last_success_timestamp_seconds (files re-read at start-up), …_last_duration_seconds, …_last_size_bytes{kind}; shipped rules BackupTooOld (over 36 h) and BackupFailing. Without BACKUP_DIR the metric does not exist and nothing alerts.

docs.title: Not backed up — good to know
docs.text:
• Encrypted secrets (camera passwords, SMS keys) are only readable with the original DOMINET_MASTER_KEY: keep it apart (a database backup without it loses those secrets).
  • Video segments still on disk (before archiving), snapshots, annotated images, generated Grafana dashboards and the Prometheus / Grafana volumes are not backed up: they are recomputable or short-lived data; the Compose files say which ones are volumes.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
